### `shopping_inventory`

Represents the authoritative, real-time inventory state for each SKU.
This is the sole source of current stock count and status per SKU.
Adjustments are never made directly; all changes are append-only logged
and then reflected here. Soft delete used for SKU discontinuation/audit
retention. Foreign key to the SKU entity, all other SKU/product
information is referenced, never stored/duplicated.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_sku_id`
  > SKU entity this inventory record tracks. [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus).
  > One-to-one with inventory record.
- `quantity`
  > Current available units. Must be >= 0. Stock-outs (0) and re-stocks
  > update this value atomically.
- `created_at`: When inventory record was created. Used for auditing.
- `updated_at`: When inventory last changed. Updated only via atomic adjustment flow.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft deletion/audit retention: populated if SKU is removed/discontinued,
  > not physically deleted for compliance.

### `shopping_inventory_adjustments`

Ledger-style append-only log for every adjustment event that alters
inventory. Immutably captures before/after, delta, reason, actor context.
Snapshots exact stock transitions for compliance, rollback, and detailed
reporting. Does not soft-delete/never updated. Actor polymorphic fields
store actor_id (uuid) and actor_type (string) for disambiguation between
customers, sellers, admins. All IDs are simple UUIDs, never relations, to
prevent coupling between audit and account systems.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_inventory_id`
  > Reference to the inventory instance being changed. {@link
  > shopping_inventory.id}.
- `shopping_sku_id`: SKU which was adjusted. [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus).
- `actor_type`
  > Which actor class performed this adjustment (customer, seller, admin, or
  > system). Polymorphic: not a relation.
- `actor_id`
  > UUID of the involved actor (user/admin/seller/system). No foreign key:
  > denormalized for immutable audit history.
- `reason_code`
  > Reason code for adjustment (order, refund, manual, etc). Used for
  > filtering and analytics.
- `quantity_before`: Quantity before adjustment applied.
- `quantity_after`: Quantity after adjustment.
- `adjustment_amount`
  > Delta applied by adjustment: quantity_after = quantity_before +
  > adjustment_amount.
- `context_note`
  > Optional context/note (order/payment reference, administrator comment,
  > batch ID, etc).
- `created_at`
  > When the adjustment event was logged. Creation timestamp only, never
  > updated.

### `shopping_inventory_alerts`

Inventory operational alerts: low-stock, stockout, anomaly triggers. Each
alert is unique per SKU/condition. Alerts track if they are open (active)
or resolved along with context of resolution. Actor info on resolution is
polymorphic: actor_type string and actor_id UUID (no foreign keys, as
alerts may be resolved by admins, sellers, or system events).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_sku_id`: The SKU for which the alert was generated. [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus).
- `alert_type`
  > Type of alert: low_stock, out_of_stock, anomaly, manual. Used for logic
  > and filtering.
- `resolved`: True if alert has been addressed and is no longer active, else false.
- `triggered_at`: When alert was created (triggered).
- `resolved_at`: Timestamp alert was resolved/closed, if applicable.
- `resolved_actor_type`
  > Actor class that resolved the alert. Optional: 'admin', 'seller',
  > 'system'.
- `resolved_actor_id`: UUID of resolving actor (admin/seller/system). Optional. No FK.
- `context_note`
  > Explanation or context on why alert was opened or resolved. Useful for
  > operators.

### `shopping_carts`

Shopping cart owned by a logged-in customer for storing items prior to
order. Each customer has at most one active cart. Associates directly
with the corresponding [shopping_customers](#shopping_customers) and is cleared upon
successful order or account deletion. Supports persistence, merging guest
carts (by session) at login. Main entry point for cart-related API
operations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_customer_id`
  > Belonged customer's [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers). References owner of
  > the cart.
- `created_at`: Cart creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Cart last updated timestamp (e.g., addition/removal of item).

### `shopping_cart_items`

Items contained in a customer's cart. Strict junction between
shopping_carts and shopping_skus, with unique constraint per sku. Stores
the quantity, variant/sku context, and add/update timestamps for each
item-in-cart. Enforces no duplicate SKUs per cart.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_cart_id`: Parent cart's [shopping_carts.id](#shopping_carts).
- `shopping_sku_id`: Contained sku's [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus).
- `quantity`
  > Item quantity for this SKU within the cart. Enforced maximum at
  > application level (e.g., 10).
- `added_at`: When this item was added to cart.
- `updated_at`: Latest update (quantity change) for the cart item.

### `shopping_guest_carts`

Shopping cart for a guest (unauthenticated, session-based) user. Each
guest cart is identified by a unique session key and optionally has an
expiration. No customer or account FK present. Serves as the basis for
merging into account cart upon login/registration. Deleted or expired per
business policy.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `session_key`: Opaque unique session key for guest cart (e.g., UUID, random secret).
- `created_at`: Cart creation time.
- `updated_at`: Cart last update time for activity tracking.
- `expires_at`
  > When this guest cart will expire and be deleted. Enforced by scheduled
  > cleanup jobs.

### `shopping_guest_cart_items`

Items in a guest cart. Junction table mapping a guest cart
(session-based) to specific SKU selections and quantities. Unique per
(cart, SKU). Deleted upon guest cart merge/expiration.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_guest_cart_id`: Parent guest cart's [shopping_guest_carts.id](#shopping_guest_carts).
- `shopping_sku_id`: Contained sku's [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus).
- `quantity`: Quantity for this SKU in guest cart.
- `added_at`: Timestamp item added.
- `updated_at`: Latest update timestamp.

### `shopping_wishlists`

Wishlist owned by a logged-in customer. Each customer has at most one
wishlist. Contains SKUs/products the customer is interested in; supports
independent management apart from the cart. Main entry point for wishlist
API operations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_customer_id`: Belonged customer's [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers). Owner of the wishlist.
- `created_at`: Wishlist creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Wishlist last update timestamp.

### `shopping_wishlist_items`

SKUs contained in a customer's wishlist. Junction between wishlist and
SKU, unique per (wishlist, SKU). Allows future addition of metadata
(e.g., added date) and supports efficient lookup for customer
recommendations.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_wishlist_id`: Parent wishlist's [shopping_wishlists.id](#shopping_wishlists).
- `shopping_sku_id`: Contained sku's [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus).
- `added_at`: Timestamp SKU was added to the wishlist.

### `shopping_orders`

Core order entity representing a customer purchase transaction.
References one customer and includes summary pricing and relationship to
lines, splits, addresses, and payment attempts. Audit timestamps support
full lifecycle traceability. Central to all business fulfillment and
payment processes.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_customer_id`: Purchasing customer's [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers).
- `order_code`
  > Globally unique, human-readable order reference code (e.g.,
  > ORD-20240001). Used in customer and business workflows.
- `total_price`: Total price for the entire order (aggregated from lines).
- `status`
  > Current order status (see status history for changes). E.g. 'pending',
  > 'paid', 'processing', 'fulfilled', etc.
- `created_at`: Order creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Order last updated timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Order soft delete timestamp; null if active.

### `shopping_order_lines`

Individual order line item, representing a single SKU and its
quantity/fulfillment. Linked to both shopping_orders and shopping_skus.
Basis for refunds, fulfillment, status, and review eligibility.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_order_id`: Parent order's [shopping_orders.id](#shopping_orders).
- `shopping_sku_id`: Purchased SKU's [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus).
- `shopping_seller_id`: Owning seller's [shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers).
- `quantity`: Ordered quantity of the SKU.
- `unit_price`: Final per-unit price for this SKU in the order (post-discount/tax).
- `status`
  > Current fulfillment status of this item (e.g., pending, shipped,
  > delivered).
- `created_at`: Order line creation time.
- `updated_at`: Order line update time.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete for this line; null if active.

### `shopping_order_splits`

Represents split of an order, per seller, when a customer order contains
items from multiple sellers. Each split is processed, fulfilled, and
tracked independently.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_order_id`: Parent order's [shopping_orders.id](#shopping_orders).
- `shopping_seller_id`: Seller for this split's [shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers).
- `split_code`: Unique code for this split (order + seller). Used for tracking/reporting.
- `subtotal_price`: Subtotal price for this seller in this order, sum of related order lines.
- `status`: Current status for the seller's portion (e.g., 'pending', 'fulfilled').
- `created_at`: Split creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Split last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete for this split; null if active.

### `shopping_order_status_histories`

Audit log of order and split status changes over time. Captures
transition events, who/what triggered them, previous/new status,
timestamp, and optional notes. Used for business auditing and
troubleshooting.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_order_id`: Order's [shopping_orders.id](#shopping_orders).
- `shopping_order_split_id`
  > Order split's [shopping_order_splits.id](#shopping_order_splits), if status applies to a
  > split. Nullable.
- `from_status`: Previous status value.
- `to_status`: New status value for the transition.
- `triggered_by`: Actor/role/automated source that initiated the transition.
- `event_note`: Optional freeform note about the event/context.
- `occurred_at`: Timestamp of status transition.

### `shopping_payment_attempts`

Tracks all attempts to pay for an order (including failures, retries, or
alternate payment methods). Links to core order; each record includes
results and unique payment gateway identifiers as appropriate.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_order_id`: Order this payment attempt is for: [shopping_orders.id](#shopping_orders).
- `payment_reference`
  > External provider or gateway reference for this payment attempt. May be
  > empty until submitted to processor.
- `attempt_status`: Status for this attempt (e.g., pending, completed, failed, cancelled).
- `amount`: Total amount attempted to charge.
- `attempted_at`: Timestamp of payment attempt creation.
- `completed_at`: When payment attempt finished (succeed/failed); null if still pending.

### `shopping_order_fulfillments`

Actual fulfillment action for a given order line. Links to an order line
with details such as fulfillment/shipping date, label, fulfillment
address, and status. Multiple fulfillment records possible per line to
support split-shipments or partial fill scenarios.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_order_line_id`: Order line being fulfilled: [shopping_order_lines.id](#shopping_order_lines).
- `shopping_seller_id`: Seller fulfilling this order line: [shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers).
- `shopping_seller_address_id`
  > Fulfillment source address: [shopping_seller_addresses.id](#shopping_seller_addresses)
  > (warehouse, etc.).
- `fulfillment_code`
  > Tracking code/label for fulfillment event. Human-readable, unique for
  > this record.
- `quantity_fulfilled`: Quantity filled in this fulfillment event.
- `fulfilled_at`: When fulfillment (handoff to carrier) completed.
- `status`: Current status (e.g. 'pending', 'shipped', 'delivered', 'cancelled').
- `note`: Optional note for fulfillment details (instructions, etc).
- `created_at`: Fulfillment record creation time.
- `updated_at`: Record update time.

### `shopping_order_addresses`

Stores delivery/billing address records associated to orders. Subsidiary
record — not independently managed, but supports audit and business
reporting in event of address changes. Kept for audit trail after order
is completed.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_order_id`: Order associated with this address: [shopping_orders.id](#shopping_orders).
- `type`: Address type, e.g. 'shipping', 'billing' (noted for each record).
- `recipient_name`: Name of the delivery/billing recipient.
- `recipient_phone`: Contact phone for recipient (formatted as per local standards).
- `zip_code`: Postal or ZIP code, as required by destination.
- `base_address`: Main street address (no apartment/extra details).
- `detail_address`: Apartment, suite, or additional info (optional).
- `city`: City name/district for route assignments.
- `state_province`: State, province, or region.
- `country`: Country code (ISO 3166-1 or platform standard).
- `created_at`: Address record creation time.
- `updated_at`: Address record last update time.

### `shopping_refund_requests`

Central entity for refund, return, or cancellation requests. Represents a
standalone business process initiated by a customer or escalated by a
seller/admin. Contains references to the original order and actor,
request type, reason, context, and status. Attachments and request items
are linked via subsidiary tables. Approval and override processes
reference this model.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_order_id`: Referenced order. [shopping_orders.id](#shopping_orders).
- `shopping_actor_id`
  > ID of the actor initiating the request (customer/seller/admin). {@link
  > shopping_customers.id}/[shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers)/{@link
  > shopping_admins.id} depending on actor_type.
- `actor_type`
  > Type of actor initiating the request. Must be 'customer', 'seller', or
  > 'admin'.
- `request_type`: Business type of request: 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'.
- `business_reason`
  > Short non-nullable business provided reason for the request. E.g. 'item
  > defective', 'ordered by mistake', etc.
- `request_context`
  > Optional additional structured context or metadata associated with the
  > request (may contain JSON as string).
- `status`
  > Current business status of the request (e.g., 'pending',
  > 'awaiting_approval', 'approved', 'declined', 'completed', 'escalated',
  > etc).
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the refund request was created.
- `updated_at`
  > Timestamp when the request was last modified (status changed, reason
  > updated, etc).
- `deleted_at`: Optional soft deletion of refund request for business/audit reasons.

### `shopping_refund_request_items`

Links individual order line items to a refund request. Used to itemize
which order lines/SKUs are subject to refund, return, or cancellation
claims. Contains FK refs to parent request, order, and order line item,
and tracks quantity and item-specific reason if set. Always a child of a
refund request.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_refund_request_id`: Parent refund request. [shopping_refund_requests.id](#shopping_refund_requests).
- `shopping_order_id`: Target order. [shopping_orders.id](#shopping_orders).
- `shopping_order_line_id`: Specific order line (SKU) being refunded. [shopping_order_lines.id](#shopping_order_lines).
- `quantity`
  > Number of units in the order line requested for
  > refund/return/cancellation (must be ≥1, ≤ order line quantity).
- `item_business_reason`
  > Optional item-specific business reason for requesting refund. Overrides
  > parent reason if set.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the refund item was created.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp of last modification to this item record.

### `shopping_refund_attachments`

Stores any evidence, photos, documents, or files attached to a refund
request or refund item. Each attachment always references a parent
request and optionally a specific request item. Links to generic
attachment files handled in global file storage. Always subsidiary to a
refund request.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_refund_request_id`: Parent refund request. [shopping_refund_requests.id](#shopping_refund_requests).
- `shopping_refund_request_item_id`
  > Optional: refund request item this attachment is associated with. {@link
  > shopping_refund_request_items.id}.
- `attachment_file_id`
  > FK to attachment file entity (managed in the file storage subsystem).
  > [shopping_product_images.id](#shopping_product_images) or generic attachment.
- `attachment_type`: Type of attachment (e.g., 'evidence', 'photo', 'invoice', etc).
- `description`: Human-readable description of attachment purpose or content.
- `uploaded_at`: Time attachment was uploaded.

### `shopping_refund_status_histories`

Append-only snapshot/audit log of all status transitions, actor actions,
and context for a refund request. Every change to a refund's status,
escalation, approval, or override creates a new record. Supports full
audit trails. Provides a read-only chronological timeline.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_refund_request_id`: Parent refund request. [shopping_refund_requests.id](#shopping_refund_requests).
- `shopping_actor_id`
  > ID of the actor making this status change. {@link
  > shopping_customers.id}/[shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers)/{@link
  > shopping_admins.id}.
- `actor_type`: Type of actor making the status change: customer, seller, admin.
- `previous_status`: Request status before this transition.
- `new_status`: Request status after the transition.
- `timestamp`: When this status change occurred.
- `change_context`: Optional additional context or comments for audit/reference.

### `shopping_refund_approvals`

Record of approval or rejection actions for a given refund request.
Includes compliance and workflow details; each approval is tied to the
request and status history, and records actor and audit fields. Approval
actions are explicitly recorded regardless of acceptance or rejection for
traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_refund_request_id`
  > Refund request being approved/rejected. {@link
  > shopping_refund_requests.id}.
- `shopping_refund_status_history_id`
  > Specific status change being approved/rejected. {@link
  > shopping_refund_status_histories.id}.
- `shopping_actor_id`
  > Actor performing the approval/rejection action. {@link
  > shopping_admins.id}/[shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers).
- `actor_type`: Type of actor approving/rejecting (admin, seller).
- `action`: Approval action taken: 'approved', 'rejected', or relevant state.
- `note`: Optional note or rationale for approval/rejection.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the approval/rejection is recorded.

### `shopping_refund_admin_overrides`

Captures administrative override/escalation/forced-resolution actions by
platform admin for refund cases. Used for compliance, legal, or
regulatory interventions. References parent refund request, admin actor,
context, and timestamps. Always subsidiary to a refund instance.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_refund_request_id`: Parent refund request. [shopping_refund_requests.id](#shopping_refund_requests).
- `shopping_admin_id`: Admin actor performing the override. [shopping_admins.id](#shopping_admins).
- `override_type`: Type of override (e.g., 'force_accept', 'force_reject', 'reassign', etc).
- `reason`: Business or legal reason for performing the override.
- `detailed_context`: Optional detailed business/technical context or metadata for trace.
- `created_at`: Timestamp when the override was initiated.

### `shopping_shipments`

Represents a single logical shipment process which may fulfill part or
all of a customer order. Contains courier allocation, main status, and
summary delivery data. Each shipment aggregates multiple packages and
references the originating order, allowing support for split shipments
and multi-carrier fulfillment. Business context: managed by admin or
warehouse ops; users/sellers view but do not edit. Relates to {@link
shopping_shipment_packages}.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_order_id`: Originating order. [shopping_orders.id](#shopping_orders).
- `shopping_seller_id`: Owning seller/business for this shipment. [shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers).
- `code`: Unique shipment code for business/ops tracing (e.g. SHPT-2025-0001).
- `status`
  > Shipment lifecycle status (e.g. pending, packed, in_transit, delivered,
  > canceled, returned).
- `carrier_company`: Allocated shipping/courier company (display name, e.g. FedEx, CJ대한통운).
- `carrier_service_type`
  > Specific courier service used (e.g. overnight/express/standard, if
  > multi-option).
- `scheduled_dispatch_at`
  > Planned dispatch/shipping datetime for warehouse logistics (nullable for
  > ad-hoc).
- `dispatched_at`: Actual shipment dispatch timestamp (for logistics/audit trail).
- `delivered_at`: Final shipment delivered/courier scan timestamp (null until completed).
- `canceled_at`: If canceled, timestamp of shipment cancellation.
- `created_at`: Entity creation timestamp (UTC).
- `updated_at`: Entity last updated timestamp (UTC).
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp; null unless deleted.

### `shopping_shipment_packages`

Physical package unit within a shipment. Each shipment may contain 1..n
packages, supporting split or consolidated packaging. Tracks package
dimensions, weight, carrier label, and fulfillment details. Used for
traceability, lost/damaged shipment handling, and external tracking
number assignment. Relates to [shopping_shipments](#shopping_shipments) via shipment_id
and to [shopping_shipment_trackings](#shopping_shipment_trackings).

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_shipment_id`: Parent shipment this package belongs to. [shopping_shipments.id](#shopping_shipments).
- `sequence`: Sequence/order of the package within the parent shipment.
- `package_label`: Carrier/warehouse-assigned package ID or label for internal ops.
- `tracking_number`: Courier-generated unique tracking number (external use).
- `package_weight_grams`: Weight in grams for carrier, shipping cost, and customs.
- `length_cm`: Length (cm) of package for shipper/courier specs.
- `width_cm`: Width (cm) for fulfillment and shipper/courier specs.
- `height_cm`: Height (cm) of package.
- `status`
  > Package status (e.g. pending, ready, shipped, in_transit, delivered,
  > lost, damaged).
- `delivered_at`: If final, recorded delivery timestamp (external scan).
- `lost_at`: If lost/undeliverable, recorded timestamp.
- `damaged_at`: If carrier or warehouse logs as damaged during process, timestamp noted.
- `created_at`: Entity creation timestamp (UTC).
- `updated_at`: Last update UTC timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft-delete timestamp, null unless deleted.

### `shopping_shipment_trackings`

Tracking instance for each package/courier. May exist for each
shipment_package if more than one carrier or external tracking source is
involved (e.g. handoff between domestic/international carriers). Used for
reconciliation of multiple tracking sources and complete audit trace.
Each is linked to a single package and may log API/scan info, last known
status, and expected/estimated delivery. Not managed directly by
end-users.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_shipment_package_id`
  > Parent package this tracking instance is associated with. {@link
  > shopping_shipment_packages.id}.
- `tracking_source`
  > Source of tracking data (e.g. courier_api, warehouse_scan,
  > customer_report, manual); for logging provenance.
- `external_tracking_id`
  > Unique tracking reference provided by external carrier/courier API (if
  > available).
- `status`
  > Most recently reported status from this tracking instance (e.g.
  > in_transit, delivered, delayed, exception, lost).
- `status_detail`
  > Full text from latest tracking event/status message (raw message or
  > system mapped).
- `last_update_at`: Timestamp of last update from carrier/API/scan or manual update.
- `estimated_delivery_at`: Estimated delivery time, if provided by courier or computed by system.
- `created_at`: Row created UTC timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last modification UTC timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp.

### `shopping_shipment_tracking_events`

Immutable, append-only log of all significant tracking events for a
shipment package. Each event corresponds to a single timestamped scan,
status update, or tracker API callback—may include carrier codes,
location, raw event text, and associated URLs or external references.
Enables full audit trail and external integration troubleshooting.
Managed as an event log, not for direct CRUD except system ingestion.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_shipment_tracking_id`
  > Linked tracking instance (which is, in turn, linked to a package). {@link
  > shopping_shipment_trackings.id}.
- `event_time`
  > Datetime of this tracking event (scan/callback/receipt/etc; not
  > necessarily same as system ingested time).
- `event_code`
  > Courier or platform event code (‘DELIVERED’, ‘IN_TRANSIT’,
  > ‘OUT_FOR_DELIVERY’, etc), or custom code for system events.
- `location`
  > Event location (city, warehouse, or geo string); null if not supplied by
  > source.
- `raw_status`
  > Raw status/description from external tracking event or API; full,
  > unmapped text.
- `external_ref`
  > URL or reference provided by external tracker system (tracking link, scan
  > ID, etc).
- `ingested_at`
  > UTC time when this event was ingested by the system (differs from
  > event_time when delayed).
- `created_at`: Row creation time (UTC).
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft-delete flag/timestamp; event log is never hard-deleted, but
  > deletions are tracked for audit.

### `shopping_reviews`

Main business entity representing a customer review for a specific SKU in
an order. Each review is uniquely associated with a customer, a SKU, and
an order line, ensuring eligibility rules are enforced. Review records
contain rating, text, and status/state fields. Key relationships: links
to customer, SKU, order line. Independent entity for full CRUD,
moderation, and audit tracking.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_customer_id`: Reviewer customer. [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers)
- `shopping_sku_id`: Reviewed SKU. [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus)
- `shopping_order_line_id`
  > Order line this review corresponds to (enforces eligibility). {@link
  > shopping_order_lines.id}
- `rating`: Star rating value (1–5, required for aggregation)
- `comment`: User review comment (10–2000 characters, required).
- `state`
  > Current review state (visible, pending_moderation, removed, under_review,
  > etc.). Business workflow uses values such as: 'visible', 'pending',
  > 'removed', 'under_review'.
- `created_at`: Review creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp for most recent review modification.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete marker for removed reviews (nullable).

### `shopping_review_attachments`

Supporting entity for storing file, image, or video attachments belonging
to a single review. Attachment records reference reviews and store
metadata about the uploaded content. Managed only within the review API
context.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_review_id`: Parent review. [shopping_reviews.id](#shopping_reviews)
- `file_uri`: Storage URI or URL for the attachment file.
- `file_type`: Mime/media type of the attachment (e.g., image/png, video/mp4).
- `file_size`: Attachment file size in bytes.
- `created_at`: Attachment creation timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete marker for the attachment (nullable).

### `shopping_review_moderations`

Snapshot/audit trail entity recording all moderation or state transitions
for reviews. Each record logs an action (e.g., approved, removed,
restored), actor (admin), timestamp, and any rationale or comments.
Enables full moderation traceability.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_review_id`: Target review. [shopping_reviews.id](#shopping_reviews)
- `moderator_admin_id`: Admin moderator who performed the action. [shopping_admins.id](#shopping_admins)
- `action`
  > Type of moderation action (approved, removed, restored, flagged, edited,
  > etc.).
- `reason`: Moderator-provided reason or notes about the action taken.
- `created_at`: Timestamp this moderation action was performed.

### `shopping_review_abuse_reports`

Main entity for customer- or seller-initiated abuse reports against a
review. Independently created entity that logs the actor, review, type of
abuse, report comments, and audit timestamps. Enables report CRUD and
workflow review by admins.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_review_id`: Reported review. [shopping_reviews.id](#shopping_reviews)
- `reporter_customer_id`: Customer reporting the review. [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers)
- `report_type`
  > Type/category of abuse reported (e.g., spam, hate_speech, off_topic,
  > etc.).
- `comment`: Optional textual explanation or evidence for the report.
- `state`: Abuse report state (open, processed, dismissed, etc.).
- `created_at`: Report creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Most recent report modification timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete, null if active.

### `shopping_audit_logs`

Contains immutable records of all critical business and
security-sensitive operations performed on the platform. Each record
represents an atomic, auditable event, such as admin/seller/customer
actions, privilege escalations, or system overrides. Designed for
compliance and traceability across the system. Linked to the actor
performing the action when available. Used for regulatory reporting,
security investigations, and dispute handling.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`: Admin actor performing the logged operation. [shopping_admins.id](#shopping_admins).
- `seller_id`
  > Seller actor affected by this action if relevant. {@link
  > shopping_sellers.id}.
- `customer_id`
  > Customer actor affected by this action if relevant. {@link
  > shopping_customers.id}.
- `category`
  > Structured log category or domain (e.g., 'security', 'order', 'refund',
  > 'inventory').
- `event_type`
  > Machine-readable code for the specific action (e.g.,
  > 'ADMIN_SUSPEND_SELLER', 'ORDER_MANUAL_REFUND', 'PRIV_ESCALATION').
- `ip`: IP address from which the operation originated, for traceability.
- `description`: Human-readable summary of the event, for audit reports or investigation.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp (immutable atomic event recording).
- `updated_at`
  > Record update timestamp (immutable, but may indicate additional
  > annotation).
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete marker if the log was removed from default query views.

### `shopping_admin_action_logs`

Contains records of major administrative operations—such as admin
grants/revocations, privileged data edits, forced password resets,
dispute decisions, and system policy changes. Linked to both the action
author (admin) and, optionally, the affected actor. Used for internal
auditing, role reviews, and compliance checks. Each log entry is
immutable and fully auditable.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`: Admin actor who performed the action. [shopping_admins.id](#shopping_admins).
- `affected_admin_id`
  > Admin account affected by this action, if relevant. {@link
  > shopping_admins.id}.
- `affected_seller_id`: Seller account affected. [shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers).
- `affected_customer_id`: Customer account affected. [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers).
- `action_type`
  > Constant representing the action kind (e.g., 'GRANT_ROLE', 'FORCE_RESET',
  > 'SUSPEND_SELLER').
- `entity_type`: Type of entity affected (e.g., 'product', 'order', 'user', 'setting').
- `entity_id`
  > ID of the affected entity (could be product, order, etc.), for linkable
  > action context.
- `reason`: Optional business context or rationale for the admin's action.
- `created_at`: Action record creation time.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete marker; set if the log should be hidden from normal reports.

### `shopping_admin_suspensions`

Records all suspensions imposed by platform admins upon other admins,
sellers, or customers. Includes both temporary and permanent suspensions.
Used for audit trails, business rule enforcement, and compliance
reporting. References the admin who enacted the suspension, the affected
entity, suspension reason, dates, type, and decision status.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `admin_id`: Admin who imposed the suspension. [shopping_admins.id](#shopping_admins).
- `suspended_admin_id`: Suspended admin, if applicable. [shopping_admins.id](#shopping_admins).
- `suspended_seller_id`: Suspended seller, if applicable. [shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers).
- `suspended_customer_id`: Suspended customer, if applicable. [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers).
- `suspension_type`
  > Type of suspension imposed (e.g., 'temporary', 'permanent',

- `reason`: Detailed business reason for suspension (policy violation, fraud, etc.).
- `start_at`: Suspension effective start time.
- `end_at`: End time for temporary suspensions; null if permanent.
- `status`: Current status (e.g., 'active', 'expired', 'revoked', 'pending_appeal').
- `created_at`: Suspension creation record timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Record update timestamp, for audit/log purposes.

### `shopping_platform_announcements`

Stores all platform-wide announcements initiated by admins. Each record
captures title, content, target audience, visibility windows, publication
status, and author (admin reference). Used to push maintenance, update,
and official notices to all or filtered user segments. Status and
schedule fields control announcement display periods.

- `target_audience`

- `publish_start_at`: Optional scheduled start datetime for announcement display.
- `publish_end_at`: Optional end datetime for announcement visibility.
- `created_at`: Record creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Timestamp when record last updated (may be for content changes).
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp for hiding from listings/reporting.

### `shopping_policy_violations`

actor or entity (customer/seller/admin/product/order/etc). Each record
references the violated policy, the reporting actor, affected entity,

Used for compliance, after-action reviews, automation triggers, and
escalation to appeals. Supports complex violation lifecycle.

- `reported_by_customer_id`

- `affected_seller_id`: Seller account affected by violation. [shopping_sellers.id](#shopping_sellers).
- `affected_customer_id`: Customer account affected by violation. [shopping_customers.id](#shopping_customers).

- `violation_code`: Machine-readable code for violation (from business policy reference).

- `status`

- `updated_at`: Last update timestamp (typically investigation note/decision).
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete for audit/cleanup, not for physical erasure.

### `shopping_appeals`

Tracks formal appeals filed against suspensions, account actions,

- `decision_at`: Datetime of appeal decision.
- `created_at`: Appeal filing timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Last updated timestamp (investigation, notes, status changes).

### `shopping_business_policies`

Defines named business policies for platform-wide application or specific
domains. Used to codify and audit enforceable business rules such as
return windows, commission rates, and user eligibility thresholds.
Referenced by other domains for outward enforcement; never contains
operational data itself.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `policy_name`
  > Unique name for the business policy (e.g., 'order_return_window',
  > 'seller_onboarding_requirement'). Used for outward reference and
  > enforcement in other domains.
- `scope`
  > Scope or domain where this policy applies (e.g., 'global', 'orders',
  > 'sellers').
- `value`
  > Value or threshold for the policy (e.g., '30', 'approved'). Can be
  > interpreted as string, integer, or enum as required by consuming domain.
- `description`
  > Detailed description of the business purpose and operational impact of
  > this policy.
- `active`: Whether this policy is currently active and enforced platform-wide.
- `created_at`: Policy creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Policy update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`
  > Soft delete timestamp, if the policy is archived or replaced. Null if
  > active.

### `shopping_business_constraints`

Defines system-wide or domain-specific constraints (e.g., rate limits,
maximum SKU count, min/max purchase values). Used for enforcing
quantitative limits or operational boundaries across the platform.
Referenced by other domains by outward FK, never inward.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `constraint_name`
  > Unique name of the constraint (e.g., 'max_orders_per_user_day',
  > 'sku_max_per_product'). Used for lookups and enforcement.
- `scope`
  > Scope or domain for the constraint (e.g., 'global', 'carts', 'checkout',
  > 'products').
- `limit_value`
  > Constraint value, typically an integer or decimal encoded as string
  > (actual enforcement handled in consuming domain).
- `unit`: Unit for the constraint's value (e.g., 'count', 'seconds', 'amount').
- `description`
  > Full business explanation of what limit this constraint applies and its
  > operational significance.
- `active`: Whether the constraint is currently in force.
- `created_at`: Constraint creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Constraint last update timestamp.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp; null if constraint is active.

### `shopping_feature_flags`

Manages feature toggles and rollout switches for platform capabilities
(e.g., beta features, A/B experiments, domain-scoped rollouts). Admins
can independently enable/disable features or set percentage rollout.
Outward referenced for controlled enablement, not bound to specific
session or user here.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `flag_name`
  > Unique name of the feature flag (e.g., 'new_checkout_flow',
  > 'wishlist_enabled'). Used for outward reference and API enablement.
- `scope`
  > Domain or context where this feature applies (e.g., 'global', 'orders',
  > 'checkout', 'frontend').
- `enabled`
  > Indicates whether the feature is enabled system-wide for the associated
  > scope.
- `rollout`
  > (Optional) Percentage 0-100 for gradual rollout/experimentation. 100 =
  > fully enabled, 0 = off (used for A/B testing).
- `description`
  > Explanation of feature flag purpose and behavior under enabled/disabled
  > conditions.
- `created_at`: Feature flag creation timestamp.
- `updated_at`: Update timestamp for the feature flag.
- `deleted_at`: Soft delete timestamp; null if flag is active.

### `shopping_review_rating_aggregates`

Materialized view table that stores denormalized pre-aggregated rating
and review statistics for each SKU and its parent product. Optimizes
product and SKU listing queries for average rating and review count. Not
directly modifiable by users.

Properties as follows:

- `id`: Primary Key.
- `shopping_sku_id`: Target SKU. [shopping_skus.id](#shopping_skus)
- `shopping_product_id`
  > Parent product for the SKU (for aggregate at product level). {@link
  > shopping_products.id}
- `review_count`: Total number of reviews for this SKU.
- `average_rating`: Average star rating for this SKU (precalculated, one decimal precision).
- `product_review_count`: Total reviews for the parent product (aggregated from all SKUs).
- `product_average_rating`: Average rating for the product overall (across SKUs).
- `updated_at`: Aggregation refresh timestamp for cache invalidation/business needs.

operations.specification: This operation registers a new customer account on the shopping-mall platform. The customer must provide a unique email, strong password, full name, and primary phone number. The system will validate these inputs against the 'shopping_customers' schema, ensuring uniqueness for the email and compliance with password security standards. Upon successful validation and account creation, the system issues a JWT access token and a refresh token for authenticated access. This endpoint supports the customer actor's self-registration flow, incorporating security and validation logic per platform business rules. If any field (such as email or phone) is not unique or does not pass validation logic, the system returns a detailed error response referencing exact schema field constraints. The operation references the 'shopping_customers' table for account data, and leverages audit and session management via related tables.
operations.description:
This API operation enables the registration of a new customer account by accepting required fields defined in the 'shopping_customers' Prisma schema, including email, password_hash, name, and phone. The operation enforces uniqueness validation on the email field as described in the schema and implemented in database constraints. Upon creation, the system issues JWT access and refresh tokens for session management, utilizing the related session and token infrastructure. Account registration is subject to business logic requirements, including password complexity, real name verification, and phone number validation, all of which must conform to schema formats and constraints.

Integration with the shopping_customer_sessions table occurs post-registration to track session information, as customers receive tokens for immediate authenticated use. All validation of input data—such as proper email format and phone structure—relies on the schema-defined field properties and system-enforced rules for the 'customer' actor. Security best practices, including password hashing and audit trail generation, are employed by this endpoint.

Registrations resulting in errors, such as attempted duplicate emails (violating the '@@unique([email])' constraint), are handled gracefully by returning informative error messages referencing the violating schema field. Related operations include subsequent login or token-refresh, both of which consume the tokens issued here. All registration attempts are audited for compliance with platform and regulatory requirements, ensuring accountability as reflected in the schema's audit relations.

Session metadata is also recorded in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' table. Incorrect credentials (invalid email/password, inactive/deleted account) result in an error response referencing relevant schema fields. This operation implements robust account access control and aligns with the customer actor's security model.

This API endpoint authenticates a customer using 'email' and 'password_hash' fields as defined in the 'shopping_customers' schema. If the credentials match an active account, new JWT tokens are generated for session management. The operation references the schema's is_active and deleted_at fields to ensure only eligible accounts can access the system. Audit log and session creation are triggered in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' related table, using metadata such as IP address stored at authentication time.

Security is handled according to platform guidelines—hashing passwords on comparison and strictly matching the schema column formats. If the email is not found, the password is incorrect, or the account is marked deleted (deleted_at not null) or inactive (is_active false), the endpoint returns detailed authentication errors linked to schema field constraints.

Post-login, the endpoint issues JWT access and refresh tokens containing the customer ID, role, and permissions, drawing from the session management infrastructure described in the schema. Security, audit, and compliance requirements are enforced throughout.

It validates the refresh token in the context of the current 'customer' session, as persisted in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' schema, updating session metadata and issuing new tokens. If the refresh token is invalid, expired, revoked, or associated with an inactive or deleted account, an appropriate error response is returned referencing schema session or account fields. Token rotation logic matches security best practices and platform configuration for session management.
operations.description:
This endpoint handles the secure renewal of customer JWT tokens by validating an existing refresh token. It leverages the 'shopping_customer_sessions' and 'shopping_customers' schema to verify token validity, session state, and account activity. Upon validation, new access and refresh JWTs are generated and returned, with the session metadata updated accordingly in the schema. The operation enforces token expiration, revocation, and account validity, referring to is_active and deleted_at fields in the 'shopping_customers' schema for eligibility.

If validation fails due to token expiration, revocation, or customer inactivity or deletion, a detailed error message referencing the relevant schema constraint is returned. Security and traceability are prioritized, as audit logs are created for all successful and failed token refreshes according to the relationships laid out in the schema.

This endpoint is a critical component of the customer authentication flow, working closely with the login and join operations, and must be used after those endpoints have completed. The operation references all necessary schema fields and relationships for a complete and compliant token rotation infrastructure.

The endpoint supports secure customer password reset flows as per business requirements, aligning with audit, compliance, and communication workflows in the schema.

The operation only references schema fields and never exposes any customer data if the supplied email is not matched, to protect user privacy. The process requires minimal but essential seller information, including unique business email and a password; it captures all necessary data for initial authentication and business context creation. This endpoint can only be used for onboarding new sellers; it cannot be used for admin or customer registration. Registration supports required seller-specific fields as dictated by platform compliance and business onboarding logic. Account status will be set to 'pending' by default until admin verification of legal/business credentials completes. Non-unique emails are rejected with an explicit business-level error. operations.description:
This operation registers a new seller in the 'shopping_sellers' table, requiring a unique business email, password (hashed), display name, and contact phone. Additional business verification fields such as business registration and legal entity information are completed after account creation, in separate flows. 

The operation enforces that provided emails are unique and not already registered, in accordance with 'shopping_sellers.email' being a unique indexed column. A password is provided as a plain string during registration and securely hashed before storage in the 'password_hash' field. The initial 'status' for the created seller account is set to 'pending', which triggers downstream compliance and admin review workflows, as mandated in onboarding requirements.

Security is a primary concern: passwords are never stored in plaintext, and registration errors do not reveal whether a given email is already in use. Upon successful creation, the seller is authenticated automatically, with JWT access and refresh tokens issued and returned in the authorized DTO structure.

Seller registration is limited to this endpoint; admin or customer accounts must use their respective endpoints. This endpoint does not permit bypassing post-onboarding verification flows – sellers must be approved by an admin before listing products or receiving payments. Error handling follows strict business patterns, returning actionable error codes for duplicate emails, invalid formats, or password strength violations.

This operation is related to the seller authentication (login) endpoint, the token refresh endpoint, and downstream business onboarding API operations (e.g., business info submission, document upload, compliance checks).

Upon successful authentication, a JWT access token and refresh token are issued as part of the authorized DTO response. If credentials are valid, a new JWT access token and refresh token are generated and returned inside the authorized DTO response struct (IShoppingSeller.IAuthorized).

Account lockouts are enforced after multiple failed login attempts, according to business policy, with any lockout status signaled using structured business error codes. This endpoint does not reveal whether a non-existent email is used for login, to prevent user enumeration. Success returns the complete seller authorization profile, while errors return actionable, business-friendly codes.

This endpoint is related to the registration ('join') and token refresh endpoints, as well as session management APIs. It does not handle password resets (handled via separate flows referencing shopping_password_resets). Audit trails are generated for all login attempts.

This operation is strictly for sellers and is not available to customers or admins, who must use their own dedicated endpoints. Role assignment and status settings must match the permissible values supported by the shopping_admins table. Security measures enforced by this endpoint include confirmation of email uniqueness, the use of secure password hashing (never directly exposed), and dedicated audit logging via related tables. Only actors with sufficient privileges can invoke this operation.

Related operations include: login for admin authentication (handled via a different endpoint), update admin information, suspend/reactivate admin, and enable MFA for an admin account, all of which have their own workflows and endpoints. The request body must reference a refresh token as required for token renewal. MFA settings and session tracking are handled independently of this endpoint; the refresh process itself works only for accounts whose status remains valid in shopping_admins. This operation is audit-logged for traceability, and only valid tokens are processed. operations.description:
Allows an authenticated admin to renew JWT access and refresh tokens. This process checks token validity, admin account status, and ensures the admin has not been suspended or deleted. Utilizes shopping_admins fields for identity validation, while ensuring no sensitive information is leaked in responses. Any misuse or expired tokens are reported with specific error codes.

The operation is mapped directly to the shopping_admins table for account validation, but does not read or mutate any fields other than those required for permission verification and session audit. Session and MFA configuration reside outside of this refresh path. The endpoint is part of the robust authentication model for admin actors.

operations.description:
This API operation enables the registration of a new customer account by accepting required fields defined in the 'shopping_customers' Prisma schema, including email, password_hash, name, and phone. All validation of input data—such as proper email format and phone structure—relies on the schema-defined field properties and system-enforced rules for the 'customer' actor. Security best practices, including password hashing and audit trail generation, are employed by this endpoint.

Registrations resulting in errors, such as attempted duplicate emails (violating the '@@unique([email])' constraint), are handled gracefully by returning informative error messages referencing the violating schema field. Related operations include subsequent login or token-refresh, both of which consume the tokens issued here. On successful authentication—using the data in the 'shopping_customers' Prisma schema and password verification—the operation issues new JWT access and refresh tokens for the customer. Session metadata is also recorded in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' table. Incorrect credentials (invalid email/password, inactive/deleted account) result in an error response referencing relevant schema fields. This operation implements robust account access control and aligns with the customer actor's security model.
operations.description:
This API endpoint authenticates a customer using 'email' and 'password_hash' fields as defined in the 'shopping_customers' schema. If the credentials match an active account, new JWT tokens are generated for session management. The operation references the schema's is_active and deleted_at fields to ensure only eligible accounts can access the system. Audit log and session creation are triggered in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' related table, using metadata such as IP address stored at authentication time.

Security is handled according to platform guidelines—hashing passwords on comparison and strictly matching the schema column formats. If the email is not found, the password is incorrect, or the account is marked deleted (deleted_at not null) or inactive (is_active false), the endpoint returns detailed authentication errors linked to schema field constraints.

Post-login, the endpoint issues JWT access and refresh tokens containing the customer ID, role, and permissions, drawing from the session management infrastructure described in the schema. Security, audit, and compliance requirements are enforced throughout.
operations.summary: Authenticate customer and issue tokens using 'shopping_customers' schema.

It validates the refresh token in the context of the current 'customer' session, as persisted in the 'shopping_customer_sessions' schema, updating session metadata and issuing new tokens. If the refresh token is invalid, expired, revoked, or associated with an inactive or deleted account, an appropriate error response is returned referencing schema session or account fields. Token rotation logic matches security best practices and platform configuration for session management.
operations.description:
This endpoint handles the secure renewal of customer JWT tokens by validating an existing refresh token. It leverages the 'shopping_customer_sessions' and 'shopping_customers' schema to verify token validity, session state, and account activity. Upon validation, new access and refresh JWTs are generated and returned, with the session metadata updated accordingly in the schema. The operation enforces token expiration, revocation, and account validity, referring to is_active and deleted_at fields in the 'shopping_customers' schema for eligibility.

If validation fails due to token expiration, revocation, or customer inactivity or deletion, a detailed error message referencing the relevant schema constraint is returned. Security and traceability are prioritized, as audit logs are created for all successful and failed token refreshes according to the relationships laid out in the schema.

This endpoint is a critical component of the customer authentication flow, working closely with the login and join operations, and must be used after those endpoints have completed. The operation references all necessary schema fields and relationships for a complete and compliant token rotation infrastructure.

The endpoint supports secure customer password reset flows as per business requirements, aligning with audit, compliance, and communication workflows in the schema.
operations.description:

If an active account is found, a secure, time-limited reset token is generated and persisted in the 'shopping_password_resets' schema using 'request_email', 'reset_code', and 'expires_at' fields. The response does not disclose whether the email exists to prevent enumeration.

The operation only references schema fields and never exposes any customer data if the supplied email is not matched, to protect user privacy. Rate limiting, email delivery of reset links, and auditing are enforced per business and platform security policies using the relationships provided in the schema. The operation is closely related to password-update completion endpoints and is the entrypoint for secure recovery workflows for the customer actor.
operations.summary: Initiate password reset for customer using 'shopping_customers' and 'shopping_password_resets' schema.

operations.description:

All error responses reference the exact schema validation that failed.

Business logic enforces password strength and secure handling, with email notification and session invalidation handled separately using schema relationships. This operation is always linked to a prior call to the password reset token initiation, and closely aligns with login and token refresh endpoints for full customer account recovery. Only explicit, existing schema fields are handled at all steps to ensure type and business logic correctness.

operations.specification: Create a new seller account and immediately issue initial JWT tokens. The operation is targeted at the 'shopping_sellers' table, which stores core authentication credentials for sellers, including 'email' (unique, login identifier), 'password_hash' (secure password storage), 'display_name' (business name), 'contact_phone', 'status' (for onboarding workflow), and business logic attributes relevant to onboarding and account setup. The process requires minimal but essential seller information, including unique business email and a password; it captures all necessary data for initial authentication and business context creation. Email uniqueness is validated at account creation. This endpoint is used to sign up new merchants for participation on the platform, automatically creating an authenticated session upon successful registration. This endpoint can only be used for onboarding new sellers; it cannot be used for admin or customer registration. Registration supports required seller-specific fields as dictated by platform compliance and business onboarding logic. Account status will be set to 'pending' by default until admin verification of legal/business credentials completes. Non-unique emails are rejected with an explicit business-level error. On success, a JWT access token and refresh token are returned, encapsulated inside an authorized DTO structure. The API response references IShoppingSeller.IAuthorized, which contains the authorized seller profile and token set.
operations.description:
This operation registers a new seller in the 'shopping_sellers' table, requiring a unique business email, password (hashed), display name, and contact phone. Additional business verification fields such as business registration and legal entity information are completed after account creation, in separate flows. 

The operation enforces that provided emails are unique and not already registered, in accordance with 'shopping_sellers.email' being a unique indexed column. A password is provided as a plain string during registration and securely hashed before storage in the 'password_hash' field. The initial 'status' for the created seller account is set to 'pending', which triggers downstream compliance and admin review workflows, as mandated in onboarding requirements.

Security is a primary concern: passwords are never stored in plaintext, and registration errors do not reveal whether a given email is already in use. Upon successful creation, the seller is authenticated automatically, with JWT access and refresh tokens issued and returned in the authorized DTO structure.

Seller registration is limited to this endpoint; admin or customer accounts must use their respective endpoints. This endpoint does not permit bypassing post-onboarding verification flows – sellers must be approved by an admin before listing products or receiving payments. Error handling follows strict business patterns, returning actionable error codes for duplicate emails, invalid formats, or password strength violations.

This operation is related to the seller authentication (login) endpoint, the token refresh endpoint, and downstream business onboarding API operations (e.g., business info submission, document upload, compliance checks).
operations.summary: Register a new seller account (shopping_sellers) and issue initial JWT tokens.

responseBody.description: Authorized seller profile and authentication tokens (JWT access/refresh), structured for immediate use.

operations.specification: Authenticate an existing seller by validating credentials and issuing new JWT tokens for access and refresh. The operation is mapped to the 'shopping_sellers' table, which holds seller authentication credentials (email and password_hash). This endpoint performs secure password validation using the hashed password stored for sellers, rejecting invalid credentials and enforcing business login policies such as account suspension/lockout and max attempt rate limiting as per 'is_active', 'status', and platform rules. Upon successful authentication, a JWT access token and refresh token are issued as part of the authorized DTO response. The operation does not return explicit authentication failure details that could be abused for enumeration. It is for sellers only; customers or admins must use their corresponding endpoints. The schema ensures secure, auditable, and compliant login according to all platform requirements.
operations.description:

The email must exist and be unique (enforced by schema), and passwords are verified against the stored 'password_hash' using secure password comparison logic. The operation also checks the seller's account status (such as 'active', 'pending', 'suspended') and 'is_active' flag to ensure only eligible accounts can log in. If credentials are valid, a new JWT access token and refresh token are generated and returned inside the authorized DTO response struct (IShoppingSeller.IAuthorized).

Account lockouts are enforced after multiple failed login attempts, according to business policy, with any lockout status signaled using structured business error codes. This endpoint does not reveal whether a non-existent email is used for login, to prevent user enumeration. Success returns the complete seller authorization profile, while errors return actionable, business-friendly codes.

This endpoint is related to the registration ('join') and token refresh endpoints, as well as session management APIs. It does not handle password resets (handled via separate flows referencing shopping_password_resets). Audit trails are generated for all login attempts.

If valid, it issues new tokens using the seller's profile, and returns them in the authorized DTO struct. Invalid or expired refresh tokens are rejected with standardized error codes. It is applicable to sellers only and does not serve customer or admin refresh operations. This workflow complies with all requirements for session token management in distributed authentication systems with rotating token patterns.
operations.description:
This operation allows a seller to refresh their JWT access and refresh tokens using a valid, non-expired refresh token, leveraging session records in 'shopping_seller_sessions'. The API validates that the provided refresh token corresponds to a currently valid, non-expired session for the seller (checked with the 'expired_at' field in the session record). If the refresh token is valid and the session is not expired or revoked, the API issues new tokens (access and refresh) and updates relevant session timestamps (where necessary), returning the new tokens in an authorized response DTO. If the refresh token is expired or invalid, the endpoint returns structured authentication error codes and does not issue new tokens.

This operation is strictly for sellers and is not available to customers or admins, who must use their own dedicated endpoints. All token refresh requests are securely audited and rate limited to mitigate abuse. This endpoint directly relates to the seller session management and login flows, as well as overall account security policy.

For password reset and account unlocking, sellers must use other endpoints managed via the password reset model (shopping_password_resets). Error handling is uniform and does not expose excessive details.

This operation registers a new admin account within the shopping mall backend platform. It is intended for platform setup or when an existing super admin creates a new admin. The admin registration process requires a unique email, a strong password (represented securely by a password_hash in the database), a real name, and an assignment of an initial role (such as 'super', 'support', etc.). The registration also involves business status assignment (defaulting to 'active' unless otherwise specified) as defined in the schema. Admin registration may also include optional account-level attributes, but only fields present in the shopping_admins table are considered.

This endpoint connects directly to the shopping_admins table, referencing fields such as email, password_hash, name, role, and status. Only those fields which are defined in the Prisma schema are to be used in this registration process. All business logic around additional settings or MFA requirements is handled by dedicated endpoints; only the basic account creation logic is implemented here.

Security is critical for admin registration: the endpoint must ensure unique admin emails, secure password hashes, and audit trails of account creation. Registered admins will require separate MFA enablement via other workflows. Account creation issues, such as duplicate email, must return explicit errors.

Prerequisite APIs: None required, but this endpoint should only be accessible by an authorized superadmin/admin actor.

The resulting admin account will be available for login through separate authentication endpoints. On successful registration, a full admin account DTO minus sensitive fields is returned.

Other admin management functions (suspension, override, deletion) are out of scope of this endpoint, which is strictly for new account creation.
operations.description:
This operation enables registration of a new administrator for the shopping mall platform. The shopping_admins table defines the required fields: email (unique identifier for admin login and notifications), password_hash (securely stored password for authentication), name (real name for audit and communications), role (privilege level string for RBAC), and status (account state such as active, suspended, pending).

The endpoint ensures that only unique emails are registered, leveraging the shopping_admins.email unique constraint. Passwords are never stored as plain text, aligning with the password_hash field and security best practices. Additional admin attributes (such as MFA configuration) are handled separately and not within this registration flow.

Upon account creation, the admin is automatically assigned a role and an active status, unless specified otherwise by an authorized superadmin. Role assignment and status settings must match the permissible values supported by the shopping_admins table. If any required field is invalid or missing, the endpoint returns detailed error feedback.

Security measures enforced by this endpoint include confirmation of email uniqueness, the use of secure password hashing (never directly exposed), and dedicated audit logging via related tables. Only actors with sufficient privileges can invoke this operation.

Related operations include: login for admin authentication (handled via a different endpoint), update admin information, suspend/reactivate admin, and enable MFA for an admin account, all of which have their own workflows and endpoints. This operation serves as the dedicated entry point for onboarding new admin accounts on the Shopping Mall platform.

Account login failures (such as invalid credentials or suspended status) must result in explicit, actionable errors as per business requirements.

It is mapped to the shopping_admins table, which contains the necessary fields for authentication: email (unique login identifier) and password_hash (for credential validation). Status and role fields are validated to ensure only active admins are granted access. The operation checks that the status of the admin account is not suspended or pending, before issuing JWT tokens.

The operation is mapped directly to the shopping_admins table for account validation, but does not read or mutate any fields other than those required for permission verification and session audit. operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes (archives) a category tree from the shopping mall platform, rendering its structure and all child categories inaccessible for new business functions. The operation works on the shopping_category_trees table as defined in the Prisma schema. It uses the tree_code as the resource identifier, which is globally unique and strictly enforced at the schema level. Deletion is a soft-delete (archival): it sets the deleted_at field, preserving coherence with existing product assignments and history while blocking further modifications or assignment of new products to categories within the deleted tree. Only admin actors may execute this, as deleting a tree can cause widespread catalog impact.
operations.description:
This endpoint provides administrative capability to archive (soft-delete) an entire category tree, identified by its unique tree_code, within the shopping mall catalog system. In the Prisma schema, tree_code is globally unique and directly identifies a category taxonomy for all product and navigation organization. 

Archiving the tree sets the deleted_at field on the shopping_category_trees record, which in turn disables all associated categories from further use. All category assignments (e.g., to products) and hierarchical relationships remain in the database for compliance and audit retention, but the archived tree and its categories become unavailable for new product assignments, navigation, or categorization features. 

This action is restricted to admin users due to the potentially significant structural impact to catalog navigation and product taxonomy integrity. The operation records a full audit log for traceability. Attempts to delete a nonexistent treeCode or a tree with dependent live category assignments may result in specific error codes or remediation requirements governed by the business rules, such as forced reassignment of affected products prior to archival.

All results exclude categories where deleted_at is not null, ensuring only active branches are returned.

Security: This read-only query is accessible to both authenticated sellers and admins (for management and assignment operations), but may be exposed publicly for unprivileged catalog browsing where appropriate. Admins and sellers can receive extra metadata (such as full path or assignment stats) per business rules, but core output follows category table definitions.

The query leverages existing category fields, ensures strict parent-child context when 'parent_id' is supplied, and includes descriptions and display ordering for all results. Sorting can be customized by 'sort_order', name, or other indexed fields—scalable indexing ensures performance. Edge cases such as orphaned or soft-deleted categories are safely excluded, and invalid queries (e.g., parent mismatch) return helpful structured error responses.

This endpoint may work in tandem with child creation or category assignment endpoints, or with product catalog searches referencing category codes. It is robust to partial matches and large data sets, returning paginated data by default. Client applications should expect total count, current page, and last page estimates for best UX.

The deleted_at column in the schema tracks the soft deletion for historical and audit purposes. Hard delete is strictly enforced only if no active orders or legal/business restrictions exist; otherwise, the process must gracefully handle constraint failures.

This endpoint is subject to security checks: the actor must match the owner for seller-level deletes, or possess adequate privileges for admin-level actions. Any failure due to active orders, regulatory, or referential integrity constraints will return a conflict or validation error according to platform policy. Proper audit log entries should be created for all delete actions, with reasons recorded for future reference. Use of this API affects product visibility across listings, recommendations, and search.

Upon invocation, the system checks for any dependent SKUs or products that utilize this dimension. If dependencies exist, the operation will fail with a constraint violation error, as deleting a dimension in use would cause catalog data integrity issues. If the dimension is not assigned to any current SKUs or products, it is safely deleted from shopping_attribute_dimensions. This is a hard delete, and all directly related attribute values should be cleaned up as well. 

Security restrictions apply: only users with admin privileges may perform this operation. All delete actions are logged in the system audit trail for compliance purposes. The operation should be used infrequently and only with a clear business justification, as it may impact SKU variant definitions and product filtering across the catalog.

Sellers and admins may access images for unpublished, draft, or archived products, pending authorization checks. The endpoint is read-only and does not provide upload or modification capabilities. Pagination parameters and result format follow standard platform conventions and return paginated objects, with each image including full file URI, upload timestamp, and display order if available.

If the productCode is not found or refers to an archived/deleted product, the endpoint will return an appropriate error to prevent information leakage. Related endpoints for product detail queries or image upload/delete may be combined for advanced client workflows.

Exception handling covers business rules: product existence, image count limits, and file format validation. The underlying Prisma schema is shopping_product_images, with required relations to shopping_products by code (unique per product). It performs full validation: verifies product existence, ensures caller owns the product, and that the maximum image limit (10 images per product per business requirements) is not exceeded. The input enforces file type (JPEG or PNG) and size restrictions (5MB) with error feedback if validation fails.

If an image is successfully uploaded, its URI and index order are saved to the shopping_product_images table, and the new image record is returned to the client. Ownership checks and authentication are strictly enforced; unauthorized requests are rejected. If the maximum limit is reached, a specific error message is returned and the operation does not proceed. Only valid, authenticated sellers and admins with relevant rights can access this endpoint.

This operation provides feedback on success or failure, returns the full created image object if successful, and is integrated with business logic for catalog display updates. Attempts to misuse, over-upload, or provide invalid files are blocked according to schema and business policy.

Security and authorization controls limit this endpoint to administrative actors. An appropriate permission check is performed to ensure only authorized admins execute such catalog-structure changes. Because categories are fundamental to browsing, search, and catalog integrity, any delete operation will also update hierarchical relationships of sibling and child nodes, maintain deterministic sort order for remaining categories, and may trigger downstream catalog update events for cache invalidation or UI refresh.

Only users who have inventory management permission for the SKU (owners, platform admins) can access this resource. Read access by sellers is restricted to their own SKUs.

The request supports advanced query parameters for audit/search purposes, including filtering by actor type (customer, seller, admin, system), date range, adjustment range, and free-text search of context notes. Pagination and sorting controls are available to efficiently browse large adjustment log histories. Users should inspect this audit log for troubleshooting stock discrepancies or reviewing compliance with inventory policies. Related error scenarios (e.g., unknown sku_code, unauthorized access) are surfaced with clear error messages.

This is the sole API for appending inventory change events; all increases, decreases, or corrections to SKU inventory must be performed via this endpoint. The operation enforces strict validation against the underlying SKU's existence, actor permissions, and business rules (no negative inventory, reason codes, and audit). The endpoint supports atomic recording and audit-compliance: every change must include actor identity, reason code, before/after quantities, and context notes as needed. Only sellers for their own SKUs, or admins, can make adjustments. Use cases include manual restocking, correction of stock anomalies, order- or refund-driven restocks, and system-initiated adjustments (performed as admin or system).

Append a new inventory adjustment record for a given SKU, documenting an atomic change in inventory (increase/decrease/correction) for auditing and operational accuracy. This API supports all legitimate business needs for changing inventory: restock by sellers, system correction by admin, order/return/refund reconciliation, and anomaly adjustments.

A valid adjustment request must specify the SKU by code, the adjustment amount (positive or negative integer), a business reason code, actor type, and any contextual notes. The server will validate that the actor is authorized to adjust this SKU (seller for own inventory, admin, or system actor). Adjustments that would result in negative inventory are strictly rejected and return a clear error. All fields (quantities before and after, actor, timestamp) are immutably stored on acceptance for compliance. For transactional consistency, the system applies the adjustment atomically and, if required by business rules, triggers downstream alerts or low-stock notifications. Error scenarios include unknown sku_code, lack of permission, invalid adjustment amount, and business constraint violations. Only authorized actors may use this endpoint; all events are audited.
