operations.summary: Search and retrieve all inventory alerts for a specific SKU
operations.description:
Retrieve a list of all inventory alerts for a specified SKU by code. This includes both active and resolved alerts, allowing sellers or admins to monitor supply issues such as low stock, out-of-stock, manual overrides, or detected anomalies. 

The operation supports filtering by alert type, status (resolved/unresolved), date ranges for triggered or resolved events, and search by context note. Querying alerts is crucial for timely restocking and risk management, ensuring that inventory managers are notified of potential issues tracked by the Prisma schema. Result is paginated, with total alert count, alert details, and optional resolution context per alert.

This endpoint references the shopping_inventory_alerts table, which is closely related to the shopping_skus entity through the SKU code and to the underlying inventory monitoring system. Role-based access control can limit visibility: sellers only see their own SKUs, whereas admins have global scope for platform health monitoring.

parameters.name: skuCode
parameters.description: Globally unique business code identifying the target SKU (global scope)

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for inventory alerts related to the SKU, such as alert type, resolved status, and trigger/resolution date ranges.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of inventory alerts and their detailed information for the specified SKU.

A SKU must be created before inventory alerts can exist for that SKU. The SKU is identified by the skuCode parameter in the alert endpoint.

Supports search and filtering by alert type, resolved state, and trigger/resolution dates. The SKU code is required to identify which SKU's alerts will be queried. Alerts help sellers and admins monitor inventory state and take proactive action.

operations.description:
Retrieve full details of a single inventory alert identified by alertId for the given SKU code. This operation allows sellers and admins to review the root cause, timeline, context, and status updates for critical inventory signals related to a product variant.

The operation draws on the shopping_inventory_alerts table from the Prisma schema, ensuring that the requested alert exists for the specified SKU. The full context note, trigger events, resolution actions, actor metadata, and all timestamps are included. This is valuable for post-incident review, audit, or compliance purposes, and supports root-cause analysis or escalation workflows.

Access control ensures sellers may retrieve alerts for their managed SKUs, while admins may retrieve alerts platform-wide for investigation of inventory actions or audit events as tracked in the system.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated and comprehensive list of shopping cart instances belonging to customers. It enables advanced search, filtering, and pagination capabilities, essential for operational dashboard views, self-service customer portals, or administrative analysis. The operation leverages the shopping_carts table as its primary source, joining related customer and item data as needed. It supports searching by customer identifier, creation or update date, and sorting by cart activity. Each list entry supplies high-level context such as the owner's identity, last cart activity, and a summary of cart content volume.
operations.description:
This endpoint is designed to provide system access to the list of all customer shopping carts in the platform. It is particularly useful for administrative or operational roles that require a broad view of customer engagement or troubleshooting of shopping cart behaviors.

The response includes concise summary information about each cart, such as the linked customer, creation and last update timestamps, number of items in the cart, and relationships to customer or product data as necessary for list context. Advanced filtering options enable searching for carts by customer ID, activity date, or other identifying characteristics, supporting both routine reviews and targeted queries.

Security measures ensure that only authorized actors (typically admin or designated operational personnel) can use this endpoint, and that personally identifiable information is handled per compliance policies. Results are paginated with customizable limits and standardized sorting controls. This operation does not expose individual cart item details (see specific cart retrieval for that functionality). Error handling covers cases where query parameters are malformed or system access is not permitted.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of shopping carts with filtering options (shopping_carts table).

requestBody.description: Filter and pagination information for shopping cart listings.

responseBody.description: A paginated list of shopping cart summaries matching provided criteria.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A customer must exist in the system, and their address must be created before their carts can be referenced, listed, or administered through the admin cart listing operation.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detailed information of a single shopping cart by its unique identifier. It is directly mapped to the shopping_carts table and includes all relationships to customer, items, and associated SKUs needed for a full presentation of cart contents and context. The cartId parameter must be a valid UUID and references the shopping_carts.id column. The response structure offers all the details for the cart, including every item, customer context, and relevant timestamps.
operations.description:
This endpoint provides the complete state of a particular customer's shopping cart, addressing both functional requirements for customer self-management and administrative review needs.

The API accepts a unique cartId in the path, which must be a valid UUID as defined in the shopping_carts model. The response includes detailed cart content: all associated cart items (with SKU references, quantities, and item-level timestamps), customer linkage, and key activity milestones. This comprehensive view is essential for client-side representations for order review, customer support investigations, or fulfillment systems that need to convert cart contents to orders.

Security restrictions require appropriate actor privileges: typically authenticated admin or platform operators for global access—normal customers would access their own cart through a separate self-context endpoint. Input validation ensures the cartId is correctly formatted, and robust error handling covers non-existent or unauthorized access scenarios. The design aligns with operational best practices and compliance expectations for data access.
operations.summary: Retrieve the detailed contents and context of a single shopping cart by its ID (shopping_carts table).

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target shopping cart (UUID format, references shopping_carts.id).

responseBody.description: Detailed data for the specified cart, including all items, customer context, and timestamps.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: A customer (and their address) must exist before a shopping cart instance can exist and be retrieved by cartId. Creating a customer address ensures prerequisite customer and address resources for cart retrieval.

operations.specification: This operation updates and replaces all cart items for a specific customer's shopping cart. The cart is represented by its unique UUID identifier. The request must contain the full list of items to set (including skus, quantities, and options if applicable). Upon success, the cart's items are replaced atomically; partial updates are not permitted. This reflects requirements for customers to manage cart content directly, ensuring inventory constraints and SKU validity per the shopping_carts and shopping_cart_items Prisma schema definitions. Authorization and ownership checks ensure only the cart's owning customer can update their own cart.
operations.description:
Atomically replace all items in a customer's shopping cart. The request fully overwrites existing items, removing any previously present but not included in the current request body. This requires validation that all SKUs exist, are available, and requested quantities do not exceed per-SKU limits. Cart updates trigger inventory validation, check cart business rules (such as max quantity per SKU), and ensure cart integrity before saving. The operation is only accessible by the customer who owns the cart, and will error if an unauthorized user attempts the update.

All requests are validated according to the shopping_carts and shopping_cart_items schema definitions. The endpoint does not allow partial merges—clients must send the complete desired cart content. If an invalid SKU, out-of-stock item, or quantity exceeding limits is provided, the operation will fail with a specific error response. Successful updates persist the new cart items and update the cart's modification timestamp.
operations.summary: Update and replace all items in a customer's shopping cart (shopping_carts).

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target cart (UUID format, globally unique per cart).

requestBody.description: Complete replacement list of cart items for the target cart. This follows the IShoppingCart.IUpdate structure, specifying all intended SKUs and quantities.

responseBody.description: Resulting updated shopping cart with all items after the replacement operation completes successfully.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a cart and all its items, identified by its unique cartId UUID. This is a hard removal from the customer's account, reflecting requirements that customers be able to clear or remove their cart entirely. Associated shopping_cart_items are also deleted. The operation maps to the shopping_carts Prisma schema and validates that only the owner customer may erase their own cart.
operations.description:
Permanently remove a customer's shopping cart and all its associated cart items from the platform. This is a hard delete—after execution, the cart and its contents are removed from the system and cannot be recovered by the customer. The operation verifies that the requesting customer owns the specified cart before deletion, preventing unauthorized access or deletion attempts. If the cartId does not exist or does not belong to the authenticated customer, the operation will fail with an authorization error.

This supports customer business logic for clearing cart history or deleting abandoned shopping carts, as outlined in the shopping_carts and shopping_cart_items Prisma schemas. Carts removed through this operation are not recoverable; users seeking to clear cart contents without deleting the cart should use the update endpoint with an empty item list instead.
operations.summary: Delete a customer's shopping cart and all its items (shopping_carts).

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cart to be deleted (UUID format, globally unique per cart).

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated and filterable list of items currently in a customer's shopping cart. It operates on the shopping_cart_items table, allowing clients to search, filter, and paginate items based on SKU, quantity, or cart status. The endpoint supports complex queries to help customers manage and validate cart contents before proceeding to checkout.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve items in a shopping cart by cartId.
operations.description:
Allows a logged-in customer to view, search, and paginate all the items in their shopping cart. Each request supports advanced filtering by SKU, quantity, and other cart item attributes. This endpoint is used by the client or customer app to list cart contents with up-to-date inventory, enabling real-time validation of product availability and status before checkout.

Security: Only the cart owner ('customer' role) can access and modify their shopping cart. JWT authentication is required. All access is audited for compliance.

The operation queries the shopping_cart_items and related shopping_skus tables to present full details for each item, including quantity, SKU information, and error messages if any items are unavailable or exceed allowed limits. Related endpoints include creating (adding) new items and removing or updating item quantities within a cart. Pagination and sorting control cart display for improved usability.

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer's shopping cart (UUID format, global scope).

requestBody.description: Search, filter, and pagination criteria for cart item retrieval.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of cart items with detailed SKU and quantity information.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: The shopping cart must be created by adding at least one item before it can be searched, paginated, or filtered for items.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific item within a customer's shopping cart. It is based on the shopping_cart_items table and returns all available data for the specified cart item, including SKU details, quantity, and related metadata.
operations.summary: Get detailed information about an individual cart item by itemId in a cart.
operations.description:
Retrieves the complete details of a specific cart item identified by itemId, for a given cartId. The endpoint is used by customers viewing their cart or validating the contents before making purchase decisions. The returned data includes SKU code, name, quantity, price, and any warnings regarding stock limitations or SKU status.

Permissions: Only the owning customer may access this information. Cart and item IDs must be valid and exist in the database; unauthorized or invalid access is denied with a specific error code.

The response includes the current quantity, detailed information about the SKU (such as display attributes and current price), and error or warning flags if the SKU is no longer active or stock limits are exceeded. If the item is invalid or removed, the operation returns an error or null object. Related endpoints include item update, removal, and cart summary retrieval.

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the customer's shopping cart (UUID format, global scope).

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cart item (UUID format, scoped to the cart).

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the specific cart item, including SKU and current quantity.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: The cart item must be created by adding an item to the cart before its detailed information can be retrieved.

operations.specification: This operation adds a new item (SKU) to the authenticated customer's cart. It is based on the shopping_cart_items table, which supports linking a cart to multiple SKUs, each with a specified quantity. The operation requires the target cart to exist (referenced by cartId path parameter), a valid SKU to add, and a desired quantity. Business logic enforces inventory and duplicate item checks to ensure a SKU is not added twice, and that stock limits are not exceeded at add time. The endpoint only allows items to be added if the cart and SKU both exist, the SKU is active, and the requested quantity does not exceed max per SKU policy. If the SKU already exists in the cart, the system will increment the quantity instead of creating a duplicate entry.
operations.summary: Add an item (SKU) to the customer's cart (shopping_cart_items table)
operations.description:
Add a product SKU to the currently authenticated customer's shopping cart. The operation works by referencing the cartId path parameter, which maps to the shopping_carts table. It validates the existence and active status of the cart, and then attempts to add the SKU specified in the request body. The business logic uses policies defined for maximum per-SKU quantity to prevent excessive additions. The SKU must correspond to an active, non-archived shopping_skus entry, and inventory validation is performed to block additions if not enough stock remains for the requested amount. If the SKU already exists in the cart, quantity will be incremented instead of a duplicate entry. In case of success, it returns the updated shopping_cart_items entry; on failure, returns errors for item duplication, sku inactivity, or insufficient stock.

User permissions are enforced: only the cart owner may add or change cart content. This endpoint should be called only by authenticated customers, and leverages authorization checks to prevent cross-account access. All SKU and quantity parameters must meet validation, and failures will result in proper business error codes in the response. This operation may be used in conjunction with cart update or remove endpoints for a complete cart management experience.

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target cart owned by the customer (UUID format, required for cart lookup and item addition)

requestBody.description: Information about the SKU to add and the quantity desired. Contains the SKU's id (UUID), and quantity (integer).

responseBody.description: The full shopping cart item entry after addition/increment, including SKU, quantity, timestamps, and cart context.

operations.name: create

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before a SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) can be added to the catalog and referenced in a cart item.
SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) must be created before it can be added to a customer's cart.

operations.specification: This operation updates the quantity or details of an existing item (SKU) in a customer's cart. It is based on the shopping_cart_items table, with itemId as the path parameter referencing a specific cart item. The operation allows customers to change the quantity of SKUs already present in their cart, subject to business constraints such as maximum allowed per SKU, and available inventory. When the quantity is set to zero, the item should be removed from the cart. Any update triggers a re-validation of SKU status and stock. All logic adheres to shopping_cart_items table structure for audit/compliance, and will fail with clear error responses if the cart item or SKU is not found, inactive, or violates business constraints.
operations.summary: Update an existing cart item's quantity or settings (shopping_cart_items table)
operations.description:
Update the quantity or attributes of a SKU already present in a customer's cart. The itemId path parameter identifies the existing shopping_cart_items entry to update; cartId provides context for correct cart ownership. The request body specifies the new quantity and, potentially, updated SKU references. This operation enforces business rules on max quantity per SKU, forces inventory stock verification, and prevents updates to inactive or discontinued SKUs. If the new quantity is zero, the cart item is removed entirely. Only the cart owner may perform this update; cross-account operations are not allowed. The endpoint ensures all parameter validation and gives business error responses if conditions aren't met.

This operation forms part of a complete cart management feature alongside add, remove, and view endpoints. It is intended strictly for authenticated customers managing their own carts. Successful calls return the updated cart item; removal returns no item. Errors signal item not found, unauthorized access, or rule violations.

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target cart owned by the customer (UUID format, provides ownership and lookup context)

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific shopping_cart_items entry to be updated (UUID format, direct lookup for cart item)

requestBody.description: New quantity or updated settings for the cart item, such as SKU id (if permitting SKU change) and quantity. Typically contains new quantity as integer; may include attribute updates if business rules allow.

responseBody.description: The updated cart item entry after modification, including SKU, quantity, timestamps, and cart context.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before a SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) can exist and be referenced within a cart item.
SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) must be created before updating its quantity or attributes in a customer's cart is possible.

operations.specification: This operation permanently removes a specific SKU item from a customer's shopping cart. It targets the shopping_cart_items table, identified by cartId and itemId, and physically deletes the association of the SKU from the cart. This supports robust cart management flows as specified in the shopping mall requirements, ensuring that customers can control the contents of their cart before proceeding to checkout. It enforces business logic such as quantity updates, cart emptiness handling, and ensures referential integrity so that only valid, non-checked-out carts can be modified. The operation reflects customer intent to remove items and prepares the cart data for clean order generation, eligibility, and readiness validation.
operations.description:
This API permanently deletes an individual item from a customer's shopping cart. The operation directly manipulates the shopping_cart_items entity, allowing customers to manage the contents of their physical cart before submitting an order. Cart items are keyed by both cartId and itemId to ensure accurate targeting of cart entries, preventing accidental deletion of unrelated cart data.

Security and authorization are strictly enforced; only the cart owner may remove items from their own cart. Attempts to delete cart items in carts belonging to other users will be rejected with an explicit business error code, supporting compliance and privacy rules. Upon a successful deletion, the system reevaluates the cart state, and if it becomes empty, continues to store the cart for session persistence, per business policy.

If the specified item does not exist in the cart or has already been removed or checked out, the API responds with a clear error message indicating such, aligning with best practices for user feedback. Error handling explicitly differentiates between not-found, already-checked-out, and permission-denied scenarios to aid in front-end UX and debugging.
operations.summary: Remove an item from a customer's cart (shopping_cart_items).

parameters.name: cartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the shopping cart to modify (UUID, owned by the customer).

parameters.name: itemId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the cart item (shopping_cart_items.id) to remove from the cart (UUID).

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This API operation retrieves a paginated and filtered list of guest shopping carts, primarily for administrative oversight, analytics, and platform maintenance. It queries the shopping_guest_carts table, supporting complex queries to search for guest cart sessions by session_key, expiration status, last updated time, or other fields. The operation does not expose guest cart contents publicly (to preserve privacy); rather, it enables platform operators or automated housekeeping flows to manage guest cart lifecycle, monitor activity, or perform periodic cleanup. Pagination, search, and sorting are fully supported to handle large volumes of guest cart sessions efficiently.
operations.description:
This operation fetches an index of active and expired guest shopping carts, returning summary information for each session as stored in the shopping_guest_carts table. Designed for platform administrators and internal operations, the endpoint supports sophisticated search (e.g., by session_key substring), filter (e.g., by expiration date), and sorting (e.g., by last update), ensuring scalable and reliable monitoring or cleanup tasks. No guest cart content or customer identity information is revealed by this endpoint, maintaining data privacy: only session-level metadata is included in responses.

Security considerations require that only admin users may access this endpoint, as guest cart management can impact order migration, session reconciliation, and compliance reporting. Rate limiting and proper access control are expected to be enforced at the service/controller layer. Related endpoints for deleting expired sessions or migrating carts are to be implemented with separate operations.

The business logic ensures cart expiration and deletion policies are respected, and this operation's results are intended for operational analytics, batch processing, and dashboards.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated/admin-filtered list of guest carts (shopping_guest_carts).

requestBody.description: Guest cart session search criteria, with optional fields for filtering by expiration, creation/update time, or substring match on session_key. See IShoppingGuestCart.IRequest for properties.

responseBody.description: Paginated administrative list of guest cart session summaries, without exposing cart item or sensitive user data.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Retrieves a guest cart by its unique identifier, which is a UUID stored in the shopping_guest_carts table. This operation enables external services or frontend clients to fetch all current items, quantities, creation and expiration timestamps, and the related SKU information present in the active guest cart. It is critical for session-based shopping experiences where unauthenticated users can add items to a cart and later merge or clear them upon account login or expiration. The endpoint enforces that only valid, non-expired guest carts are retrievable and provides null when the specified cart does not exist or has expired. Related tables include shopping_guest_cart_items for line items and shopping_skus for SKU data.
operations.summary: Retrieve guest cart by ID from shopping_guest_carts table
operations.description:
This endpoint allows retrieval of a guest shopping cart corresponding to the given guestCartId. The primary use case is to allow session-based (unauthenticated) users to see the current contents of their temporary cart. The guest cart is identified by a session-keyed UUID and stores a list of SKU IDs and their quantities. If the cart exists and is active, its line items, expiration time, and details for all items will be returned. If the guest cart has expired or the ID is not found, the response will be null or a not-found error.

Security: This is a public endpoint with no authentication required, but session collision or brute-force enumeration is mitigated by requiring full UUIDs and rate limiting per IP/device. Only guest-only carts (not associated with logged-in accounts) can be fetched from this endpoint.

This operation integrates with the shopping_guest_carts and shopping_guest_cart_items tables (as described in the schema), as well as shopping_skus for display of product info. No sensitive or personal user data is returned; only SKU, quantity, and cart metadata is provided. It is intended for temporary cart persistence before user registration or login. Related operations include PUT on the same resource for updating cart contents and POST /carts for merging after login.

parameters.name: guestCartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the guest cart session (global scope)

responseBody.description: Guest cart details and all contained SKU items, quantities, created/updated/expiry timestamps. Returns null or not found if cart does not exist or has expired.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: Updates or replaces the contents of an existing guest cart by its UUID. Clients can add, remove, or change quantities of items for session-based carts, which is essential for guest shopping flows before authentication or checkout. The target table is shopping_guest_carts (for the cart metadata) and shopping_guest_cart_items (for the SKU and quantity mapping). The operation requires the new state of the cart (an array of SKU IDs and quantities) and will overwrite current contents. This call is idempotent; repeated updates with the same body will achieve the same result. Carts that do not exist or have expired cannot be updated. This operation is public and only applies to guest (session-based) carts, not user account-based carts.
operations.summary: Update guest cart items and quantities by guestCartId in shopping_guest_carts
operations.description:
This endpoint allows updating or replacing the cart items and their quantities for a specific guest (session-based) cart identified by its UUID. Clients can set the complete new list of SKU IDs and quantities in the request body, and the backend will ensure the cart now matches the provided structure. This is fundamental for managing session-based shopping experiences for unauthenticated customers, enabling full cart modification without requiring a user account.

Security: Public access only; no personal user information exposed. The endpoint is intended for unauthenticated (session/guest) shopping use cases. Rate limiting and brute-force mitigation are recommended at the API gateway or server for this operation. Carts associated with a logged-in user or expired carts cannot be modified through this API. Validation will ensure all referenced SKUs exist and quantity rules are enforced according to business constraints.

Table references: shopping_guest_carts (cart metadata such as timestamps and session keys), shopping_guest_cart_items (line items for SKUs), and shopping_skus (for product validation). Related operations: GET on the same endpoint to fetch current cart state, POST /carts to merge guest cart on login.

parameters.name: guestCartId
parameters.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the guest cart session (global scope)

requestBody.description: Complete set of cart items (SKU IDs and quantities) to set for the guest cart. Must reference valid SKUs and follow cart quantity business rules.

responseBody.description: Updated guest cart object after applying requested changes, with all item details, created/updated timestamp and expiration. Returns null if cart could not be updated (expired or nonexistent).

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation deletes a guest shopping cart identified by its guestCartId from the system. This operation directly targets the shopping_guest_carts table in the database, which maintains carts for unauthenticated/guest users via a unique session key or guestCartId (UUID). It is used to remove expired, abandoned, or user-requested guest carts, clearing all associated cart items and related references. Only the specific guest cart—identified by guestCartId—is deleted; other guest carts or customer carts remain unaffected. All deletion actions are permanent for the guest cart and its items, as this table does not contain soft-delete columns.
operations.summary: Permanently remove a guest shopping cart by its guestCartId from shopping_guest_carts table.
operations.description:
Delete a specific guest user's shopping cart from the system, using the unique guestCartId provided in the path parameter. This operation is intended to expire or remove temporary carts created for non-authenticated users, either programmatically (e.g., after inactivity/expiry) or on explicit user request (e.g., clear cart).

Upon invocation, the operation deletes the guest cart from the shopping_guest_carts table and all associated cart items from shopping_guest_cart_items, as these are linked by the cart's id. This is a hard delete, as there is no soft-deletion logic in the schema; once deleted, the cart and its contents are permanently removed and cannot be recovered by the user.

No authentication is required: deletion of guest carts does not require an authenticated actor, as the guestCartId is assumed to be possession-based via session or cookie. Consumers should ensure guestCartId is securely managed to prevent deletion of other users' carts. The endpoint is public and access-controlled only by knowledge of the guestCartId value.

If a non-existent guestCartId is provided, the operation is a no-op and considered idempotent, returning success with no error if the cart does not exist. If the cart exists but is already expired, it will be cleaned up and associated items cleared. In all cases, no error is thrown for missing/expired carts.

No request or response body is used as this operation is path-driven and has no payload; it simply executes the removal of one guest cart and its item records. This helps ensure temporary/abandoned guest carts do not persist indefinitely and allows for client-driven cleanup when carts are merged on user login.

The endpoint is used to support merging guest carts on user login or to present the full guest cart contents for review, as part of the guest-to-user session migration flow.
operations.summary: Retrieve the list of items in a guest shopping cart by guestCartId from shopping_guest_cart_items table.
operations.description:
Fetch and return all SKUs and their quantities contained within a guest shopping cart, identified by the guestCartId in the path. This operation is commonly used as part of guest-to-user cart migration (e.g., user logs in and wants to merge guest cart with their authenticated user cart), or to display the current contents of a guest cart for editing before checkout or login.

The operation queries the shopping_guest_cart_items table by the guestCartId, joining on the shopping_skus for rich SKU details. For each item, the response includes the skuId, quantity, and metadata about the item (addedAt, updatedAt). The operation is read-only with no authentication required; guests are not required to be logged in. The results support a smooth bridge experience for users transitioning from guest to registered customer by allowing extraction of cart items for merge logic.

Note: If the specified guestCartId does not exist, the operation returns an empty list rather than error. No sensitive or user-specific information is exposed by this endpoint beyond the items belonging to the provided guestCartId.

It maps to the guest cart management use cases that help unauthenticated (guest/session) users inspect a single cart item, validating SKU reference, quantity, and state before checkout or merging into a customer cart upon login. This endpoint is primarily for supporting session-based carts prior to authentication and does not expose customer-linked account information. It corresponds to the shopping_guest_cart_items table in the database, retrieving the item by its unique cart and item identifiers.

This operation allows an unauthenticated (guest) user to retrieve detailed information about a specific item in their session-linked shopping cart for the current device/session. The item is uniquely identified by the cart and item IDs, and the response includes the SKU, quantity, timestamps, and related metadata.

Security: No authentication or authorization is required, as this endpoint is intended for temporary, session-based guest carts only. However, the backend must ensure that only the current session owner can access the referenced cart/item pair, typically validated using a secure session token or cookie-based identifier.

The operation is closely tied to the shopping_guest_cart_items entity in the Prisma schema, which strictly ties each cart item to both the guest cart and the target SKU. It does not permit direct manipulation or exposure of personal information or customer carts.

Business logic includes validation of the cart and item association, ensuring the item exists, is not expired, and is not soft-deleted. Errors should be handled with clear messages for missing or invalid items.

Other endpoints in the guest cart domain include adding items (POST /guestCarts/{guestCartId}/items), updating/removing items, and listing all current guest cart items. This operation provides read-only introspection for a single cart item to aid in pre-authenticated shopping workflows.

The operation supports typical guest shopping flows, permitting selection of a SKU, specifying quantity, and immediate persistence to the guest cart. It corresponds to an insertion row in the shopping_guest_cart_items table, with complete request and response validation based on SKU availability, cart state, and stock. If the item already exists in the cart, the quantity should be updated per business rules rather than duplicating entries.

This operation allows guest (non-authenticated) users to add a specific SKU item to their cart prior to registration or login. The endpoint expects the target guest cart's unique identifier and the request body to specify the SKU and quantity. The operation ensures that all business and inventory validation is performed before appending or incrementing an item in the cart.

Security: This endpoint is strictly unauthenticated for temporary carts not associated with customer accounts. Only the current session owner should be able to add items to their own cart. Appropriate anti-CSRF and abuse controls are recommended.

The request is validated against the shopping_guest_cart_items data structure and must reference a valid, active SKU available for purchase. If the item/SKU is already present, the quantity is incremented in place unless business rules specify otherwise (e.g., enforce a max per SKU per cart). Stocks are not reserved at this stage but should be checked for feasibility.

Other operations in the guest cart domain include listing items, updating/removing items, and merging to a customer cart at login. Error handling must return clear validation messages for unavailable SKUs, exceeded quantities, or invalid cart/session states.

operations.specification: This operation allows a guest user to update the quantity of a specific item in their temporary shopping cart. It operates on the shopping_guest_cart_items table, which represents items in an unauthenticated guest cart. Only valid SKUs and positive quantities are allowed. Quantity validation and stock checks are enforced at the application level. This endpoint is frequently used during the guest checkout or cart review process to adjust purchase intent before login or registration. The operation fully validates that the cart and the item both exist with the provided guestCartId and itemId, and that the new quantity does not exceed maximum allowed per SKU per business policy. It updates timestamps for change tracking and triggers stock revalidation logic. If the new quantity is set to zero, the recommended practice is to use the DELETE endpoint instead.

Update the quantity and details for a specific item within a guest's shopping cart, identified by both the guest cart ID and the unique item ID for the targeted SKU. 

This endpoint enables unauthenticated (guest) users to change the quantity of a SKU they have previously added to their temporary cart, provided the SKU remains available and in stock. The application enforces business logic to ensure requested quantities do not exceed maximum limits and validates current stock for the associated SKU. If the requested item does not exist or is already removed from the cart, the operation will return a not found error. 

All updates to cart item quantities are instantly reflected in the cart state and will trigger a revalidation of business rules (e.g., per-SKU limits, inventory checks). This operation is idempotent—repeated updates with the same values do not create duplicates or additional cart entries. Further, all updates are immediately persisted for the guest session and will be merged into a user account cart if the guest logs in.

The targeted item is identified through both the guestCartId (session key) and the unique itemId within that cart. The endpoint validates that both the cart and the item exist for the current session before removing the item. If the item does not exist or has already been deleted, the operation will respond with a not found or no action taken result. This operation is used to support standard guest shopping cart workflows, such as removing SKUs that are no longer of interest or unavailable.
operations.summary: Remove an item from the guest cart
operations.description:
Remove a specific SKU/item from a guest's temporary shopping cart, using both the guestCartId and itemId to ensure accurate targeting. 

This endpoint is used when a guest wishes to remove an unwanted or unavailable SKU from their session-based cart prior to checkout or account registration. The operation confirms that the specified cart and item exist, enforcing data integrity and session security. It will not affect other items in the cart, and if the specified item is not found, the system will return a not found error or simply confirm no changes were necessary. 

The removal is immediate and irreversible within the guest session. All removals will be reflected instantly in the cart summary and will be accounted for if the cart is later merged into a registered user's account upon login or sign-up. This endpoint helps ensure that cart expirations, out-of-stock logic, and guest-to-user cart merging are implemented with high accuracy.

This operation enables customers to retrieve a paginated, searchable list of SKU items saved in their shopping wishlist. It supports advanced filtering, sorting, and search options based on product attributes, availability, and customer preferences. The operation interacts directly with the 'shopping_wishlists' table for wishlist meta information, and through relations to 'shopping_wishlist_items' and 'shopping_skus' for detailed item retrieval and attribute resolution. Results are scoped to the authenticated customer's wishlist, ensuring privacy and data integrity.

The operation provides optional filtering by product name, brand, stock status, and user-specified tags or categories. Pagination supports configurable page sizes, with performance optimization for wishlists containing large numbers of items. Data returned includes a summary of each wishlist entry, associated product/variant metadata, and the most recent update timestamp for accurate display. Edge cases, such as wishlist items referencing unavailable or archived SKUs/products, are handled gracefully with proper state representation.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated, filtered list of wishlist SKUs for the authenticated customer
operations.description:
Allows a logged-in customer to view the contents of their wishlist as a paginated collection with optional search, filtering, and sorting. Each wishlist item entry represents a SKU the customer has added to their wishlist, and includes relevant product and variant information summarized for efficient display. 

Access is restricted to the authenticated customer; other roles and actors are not permitted to view or modify another user's wishlist through this endpoint. The operation integrates wishlist data with associated product and SKU metadata, respecting the integrity of the underlying schema. 

Sensitive or unavailable products (e.g., out of stock, archived, or deleted SKUs) are accurately represented, and the API supports edge cases where wishlist items have become unavailable. Security considerations include ensuring users cannot enumerate or access wishlists not owned by them. Related endpoints may cover adding/removing wishlist items, which are outside the read/search scope of this operation.

The response includes only summary-level SKU and product data for quick rendering, and details the most recent update to each wishlist item for sorting or display purposes.

requestBody.description: Filter, search, and pagination options for retrieving wishlist SKUs (by name, SKU code, product attributes, tags, page size, etc.)

responseBody.description: Paginated summary listing of wishlist SKUs for the authenticated customer, including status of items and relevant product/variant metadata.

This operation retrieves a specific wishlist by its unique identifier, as maintained in the 'shopping_wishlists' table. The wishlists are directly tied to customers, and access is restricted to the wishlist owner. The operation includes all associated wishlist items, product and SKU metadata, as well as timestamps for creation and latest updates.

The API ensures strict privacy: only the authenticated user owning the wishlist can view its contents—there is no cross-user access. All wishlists are managed by individual users, and the response aggregates the wishlist meta information along with the current set of SKU items, supporting integration into personalized user dashboards.

Edge cases, such as attempting to access a deleted or non-existent wishlist, yield appropriate error responses with descriptive messages. This operation is typically consumed in profile or account-specific contexts rather than in public or admin dashboards.

Fetches a specific wishlist for the authenticated user, identified by its unique wishlistId. The API returns comprehensive information about the wishlist, including its metadata and all contained SKU items, with associated product summaries relevant for account or dashboard display. 

Access is strictly limited to the wishlist owner (authenticated customer role), ensuring data security and privacy. Administrative and seller actors cannot use this endpoint to access or enumerate customer wishlists.

If the specified wishlist is deleted, does not exist, or does not belong to the authenticated user, a suitable error is returned. The detailed view supports client rendering of wishlists for customer accounts and can be used to power account overview pages or personalized suggestions. Cross-user access and unauthorized enumeration are prohibited.

This API operation allows a customer to update an existing wishlist identified by its unique wishlistId. The wishlist can be modified to change its properties such as the update timestamp or display name, in accordance with the system's business rules.

Access to this endpoint requires the customer to be currently authenticated and to own the wishlist being updated. The update follows the shopping_wishlists schema as defined in the Prisma DB, which ensures that users can modify only their own wishlists. Attempts to update non-existent or unauthorized wishlists will result in appropriate error messages.

Changes to wishlists through this API are audited and tracked, contributing to overall data integrity and user accountability. The endpoint helps customers effectively manage their wishlists and keep changes synchronized with their account preferences.

This API operation allows a customer to delete their own wishlist, referenced by the wishlistId parameter, in the shopping_wishlists table. The deletion is performed as a soft-delete—filling in the deleted_at timestamp field instead of permanently erasing the data—so that audit trails and regulatory requirements are satisfied.

Authentication is mandatory, and the system will validate that the customer requesting deletion owns the relevant wishlist. If the wishlist does not exist or does not belong to the user, the system will respond with an error. In accordance with audit and compliance requirements, deleted wishlists are marked as such for traceability rather than removed.

Proper authorization is enforced to ensure only the owner can remove their wishlists, maintaining the security model established in the database schema. This operation complies with best practices for personal data retention, user empowerment, and business integrity.

Each wishlist is associated with one customer, and items correspond to SKUs in the product catalog. The operation is essential for displaying the current contents of a user's wishlist and driving 'move to cart' interactions.
operations.description:
Query wishlist items for a specific wishlist by its unique identifier. This operation enables customers to view the contents of their wishlist, including product SKUs, variant information, and addition timestamps.

This endpoint provides pagination and filtering options to support large wishlists and can be extended with search criteria (e.g., filter by product name or SKU code). Only customers can retrieve their own wishlists; attempting to access a wishlist owned by another user will result in an authorization error.

The data structure returns an array of wishlist items with full SKU details, enabling integration with the shopping catalog for displaying product images, names, and prices. Security ensures customers cannot access or modify others' wishlists. Related APIs include wishlist creation, item addition/removal, and wishlist deletion.

This enables validation that users can only access their own wishlist entries. The endpoint returns the wishlist item with full associated metadata.

The combination of wishlistId and itemId ensures both correct scoping and secure access control. Only authenticated users who own the specified wishlist can fetch associated items; access is denied otherwise. Returns the wishlist item with necessary foreign key references to enable deeper catalog lookups or move-to-cart actions.

This operation is critical for enabling seamless user experiences around wishlist item management and transitions to purchase flows.

Security is enforced so only the wishlist owner can add items, and the response returns the updated wishlist item information upon success. All writes trigger audit logging for personalization and compliance.

The operation will permanently delete the specified item from the wishlist and prevent its appearance in the user's wishlist view. Removal is only permitted for the authenticated customer who owns the wishlist. The operation will not affect the underlying SKU or the wishlist entity itself; it only removes the association between the wishlist and the indicated item. If either the wishlist or the item does not exist, or if the user does not own the wishlist, a proper error is returned. The deletion is a hard removal as there is no 'soft delete' field for items on wishlists in the schema.
operations.description:
This API operation enables a logged-in customer to delete a specific item from their wishlist. The endpoint requires the wishlist and item identifiers as path parameters. The operation validates that the requester is the owner of the wishlist via their authenticated customer session, then proceeds to delete the wishlist item entry. If the wishlist or item does not exist, or belong to a different customer, the operation fails with an appropriate error message. The underlying SKU remains unaffected; only the link between the wishlist and the SKU is removed. No soft-deletion is performed as the schema does not support this for wishlist items.

Security enforcement ensures that no customer can remove items from another user's wishlist, and the operation is not available to sellers or admins. Usage is tracked via standard audit logs attached to customer actions. This serves the core business goal of allowing flexible management over users' wishlist preferences and maintains accuracy of their favorites list. Errors are handled gracefully with clear feedback.

Typical usage involves customers managing their wishlists, removing items they are no longer interested in, especially before making cart decisions or as SKUs become unavailable. It is based on the shopping_orders table and includes relational joins to provide summary information about each order. Query parameters such as order status, date range, order_code, or product name can be passed in the request body to refine results. Results include pagination metadata for seamless user experience in applications and UIs handling histories or reporting. Security rules ensure only the current customer's orders are returned, and order data for other actors are not exposed. The response conforms to business rules described in the requirements, including search on order reference codes and full history display.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows authenticated customers to search and retrieve a paginated list of their orders by applying complex filter conditions, sorting, and pagination controls. The list supports filtering by status (such as completed, pending, cancelled), order_code for business traceability, and allows limiting results to certain date ranges. The query is submitted in the request body following the IRequest pattern, making it possible to extend with additional filters as business requirements grow.

The operation ensures customers can only fetch their own orders, never another account's data. Results return essential order information such as order_code, total_price, status, key timestamps, and summary details for display on history screens. Sensitive data and PII from related customers or sellers are excluded from the result for privacy compliance.

Error handling is robust: if a requester is not authenticated or requests orders they do not own, the API returns a clear error. Pagination, search, and sorting are all supported by the IRequest DTO, and UI can traverse through multiple pages of orders efficiently. The implementation serves common use cases such as order history lookups, after-sales tracking, and download/export of order summaries.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a filtered, paginated list of the authenticated customer's orders

The response includes the complete order entity and related data as per the Prisma schema—specifically, information on order lines, splits (for orders with multiple sellers), payment attempts, fulfillment/shipment status, and all historical status transitions.

The API uses strict access control: a customer may only request their own orders, a seller may only see orders for products they own, and admins may access any order in the system. Security checks are performed at the application layer based on actor type and order ownership, with forbidden access for unauthorized requests.

The path parameter orderCode corresponds to the order_code column in shopping_orders, which is globally unique and human-readable (e.g., ORD-20240001). When the specified code is not found, a clear error is returned. The endpoint is intended for use in account order history, order tracking, and customer support contexts. This endpoint enables authorized actors (customer, seller, or admin, depending on context) to retrieve all information for a specific order based on its unique business order code. The response includes the complete order entity and related data as per the Prisma schema—specifically, information on order lines, splits (for orders with multiple sellers), payment attempts, fulfillment/shipment status, and all historical status transitions.

The API uses strict access control: a customer may only request their own orders, a seller may only see orders for products they own, and admins may access any order in the system. Security checks are performed at the application layer based on actor type and order ownership, with forbidden access for unauthorized requests.

The path parameter orderCode corresponds to the order_code column in shopping_orders, which is globally unique and human-readable (e.g., ORD-20240001). When the specified code is not found, a clear error is returned. The endpoint is intended for use in account order history, order tracking, and customer support contexts. Associated data (order lines, splits, addresses, payment attempts, shipments, etc.) is included using Prisma's relationships and the response type IShoppingOrder.

parameters.description: Globally unique business order code of the target order (global scope), e.g., ORD-20240001.

responseBody.description: Detailed information about the target order, including all related entity data such as lines, addresses, payment attempts, status history, and shipments.

operations.specification: This operation creates a new order on the shopping mall platform when a customer completes checkout. It takes a business-validated summary of the cart, customer, shipping address, and selected payment method, and atomically creates a new order in the shopping_orders table. Upon success, it assigns a globally unique order_code, initializes the status, allocates related order lines, splits (for multi-seller orders), and attaches addresses and payment attempt records. Inventory validation is executed and stock is reserved as part of the process. Security and business rules—such as stock checks, duplicate prevention, and customer/seller assignment—are enforced per the requirements. All data mapping strictly follows the Prisma schema.
operations.summary: Create a new order in the system when a customer performs checkout (shopping_orders).
operations.description:
This endpoint processes a completed customer checkout and translates it into a new order in the shopping_orders table. The operation accepts a well-structured order creation payload (IShoppingOrder.ICreate) containing the customer's ID, delivery/billing addresses (either selected or entered anew), product SKUs and quantities, total pricing, selected payment method, and any relevant contextual/coupon codes.

Upon validation and business checks (e.g., inventory, eligibility, address), the API atomically creates the new order with one or more order lines (for each SKU), computes seller splits if multiple sellers are present, and reserves inventory. It generates a globally unique order_code, sets the order status to the initial workflow state (such as 'pending'), and creates references to status history and payment attempt entities. On success, the API returns the entire created IShoppingOrder instance. Inventory is locked as necessary to prevent overselling, and security checks enforce correct actor usage and business constraints.

Edge and error cases such as insufficient inventory, invalid address, or payment method failure trigger appropriate error responses. The operation is open to authenticated customers only and is the central entry point for order creation in the shopping platform.

requestBody.description: Comprehensive information about the new order: customer, SKUs, delivery/billing address, pricing, payment option, and all line items, adhering to the IShoppingOrder.ICreate schema.

responseBody.description: The newly created shopping order, containing all relevant relationships and business context.

operations.specification:
This operation permanently removes a shopping order from the system based on its unique order code. Since the 'shopping_orders' table in the Prisma schema includes a 'deleted_at' field, the operation performs a soft-delete, updating this field to indicate logical deletion while retaining the order record for audit and compliance purposes.

This endpoint is used when a customer, seller, or admin needs to delete an order (for instance, cancellation prior to fulfillment), subject to the business rules established in functional requirements. The operation enforces all eligibility and business constraints, ensuring that orders under certain statuses (e.g., fulfilled, paid, under refund process) cannot be deleted to prevent data loss or regulatory noncompliance.

The operation is fully traced, with all deletion events recorded for future reference, and the response reflects the soft-deleted status as per compliance needs.
operations.description:
Performs a soft-delete on an order identified by its unique business order code, marking it as deleted in the system but retaining all data for compliance and future audits.

The operation checks business rules before allowing deletion, including verifying whether the order is eligible for deletion or cancellation (e.g., only orders in certain states such as 'pending' may be deleted). Any attempt to delete an order not meeting these criteria is rejected with a specific error message, as mandated by the platform's business logic.

All deletion actions are recorded in the audit trail, and the order remains accessible for read-only compliance, audit, or reporting activities. Hard deletion is never performed to ensure data retention standards are maintained.

It operates on the shopping_order_lines table in the Prisma schema, enabling clients to query order line items directly by specifying the unique order code belonging to the parent order (shopping_orders) with optional query parameters for status, SKU, seller, fulfillment state, and creation date ranges. Pagination and sorting can be performed by unit price, status, or creation timestamp, facilitating extensive list management and order review workflows for both customer and admin actors. This endpoint fully supports business requirements for item-level order detail retrieval needed for order history, admin review, and seller fulfillment processes.
operations.description:
This API operation enables detailed retrieval of all line items belonging to a specific customer order, identified by its unique business order code (order_code, globally unique). Clients use this endpoint to retrieve all SKUs, their quantities, status, per-unit pricing, and fulfillment information under the given order. The list can be filtered and sorted by multiple fields, such as SKU, seller, fulfillment status, and order line status.

Security logic ensures that customers may only access line items for their own orders, while sellers and admins may review order lines for relevant authorization scopes. Rate limiting applies for bulk queries, and sensitive commercial information is filtered appropriately by actor type.

Related business logic includes support for order audit history, returns, and fulfillment by sellers (since lines drive fulfillment and refund eligibility). The endpoint leverages indexed queries for optimal performance on typical customer (recent orders) and admin (search/filter across large volumes) use cases. Error handling distinguishes between invalid order codes, permission errors, and unsupported filter parameters based on precise Prisma schema mappings.

operations.specification: This operation allows adding a new order line item to an existing customer order, identified by the order's unique order_code (ORD-...). The target is the shopping_order_lines table, and it is used to append a new line to an in-progress order before checkout completion. The request provides SKU, quantity, pricing, and product reference, and ensures the line is linked to the correct parent order. Business logic enforces that order must not yet be in a finalized or payment-confirmed status, and all ordering rules (stock availability, SKU validity, ownership, etc) are validated. Soft-deleted orders cannot have lines added. This operation is primarily used in cart editing flows or before final order placement.

operations.description:
This endpoint is used to append an additional SKU line item to the list of products/services on an open shopping order, typically prior to order finalization and payment. The new order line captures the SKU reference, desired quantity, calculated or offered unit price, and links back to the parent order.

The business rules check that the specified order (by orderCode) is in an editable state (not expired, deleted, or paid). Inventory is validated for the SKU, and only valid SKUs from active products may be added. The system ensures duplicate SKUs are not added to the same order.

Security requires that only the account owner (customer) or platform admin can add lines; sellers are not permitted to modify order items at this stage. Edge cases include handling attempts to add lines to orders in a non-editable or finalized state, or with invalid SKU/quantity, and responding with appropriate errors. This endpoint is a core utility for cart-to-order transitions and manual admin order edits.

This operation allows authorized users (admin, seller for their orders, or customer for their own order) to retrieve a paginated list of all status change events for a designated order from shopping_order_status_histories. The endpoint expects the unique order_code as a path parameter, resolves the corresponding order in shopping_orders, and then performs a joined query on shopping_order_status_histories to collect all transitions, including their timestamps, actors, from_status, to_status, and optional event notes.

Filtering parameters in the request body enable advanced search—for example, by specific status transitions, triggering actor, or a date/time window. The response contains paginated status history entries which are useful for customer transparency, seller operational review, or administrative audit. Access is gated so that customers only retrieve their own order histories, sellers only see those tied to their products, and admins may access any order's status transitions. Edge cases and error handling are present: if the order_code does not exist, or the requester lacks permission, a detailed business error is returned.

The details are composed from the shopping_order_status_histories schema, referencing the associated order from shopping_orders by order_code. This enables both deep forensic analysis (e.g., for fraud or shipping errors) and informative UI displays (e.g., order tracking timelines for customers).

Only actors with proper visibility to the order in question (customer who owns the order, the relevant seller, or platform admin) should be authorized. The operation does not expose confidential business logic, but ensures complete traceability as required by audit and compliance.

Access to this endpoint must be secure and properly scoped to avoid leaking data from orders that do not belong to the requesting actor. All status event details align strictly with underlying order and status schema documentation.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a paginated list of all order fulfillment records linked to a specific order. It uses the shopping_order_fulfillments, shopping_order_lines, and shopping_orders tables as defined in the Prisma schema. The endpoint provides advanced filtering, search options, and supports pagination, making it suitable for customer, seller, or admin actors to understand the complete shipping and fulfillment status of all items in an order. It is essential for scenarios involving partial fulfillment, split shipments, or multi-stage delivery workflows typical in marketplaces.

The endpoint implements security rules based on role, ensuring that customers can only access their own orders, sellers see only fulfillments they are responsible for, and admins can access any record. Response contains fulfillment data matched to the order context, and may optionally include status, address, or history information depending on implementation.
operations.description:
Fetch a paginated and filterable list of all fulfillment actions taken for a specified order. Users leverage this functionality to track the shipping and delivery events corresponding to each order line, including partial shipments, returned items, or unfulfilled lines remaining. 

This API aggregates data from shopping_order_fulfillments referencing shopping_order_lines, which must themselves belong to the specified order (via order_code on shopping_orders). Security implementation ensures that data visibility adheres to actor role restrictions: customers only see their orders, sellers see only their fulfillments, and admins have global visibility. All standard paginated retrieval behaviors apply, and optional filtering parameters may be supported in the request DTO in future versions.

The operation is crucial for audit, support, and customer notification workflows, as well as providing full transparency on the order's post-purchase status. Error handling must protect against unauthorized data access and handle cases where orders or fulfillments do not exist.

operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of refund/cancellation requests (shopping_refund_requests)
operations.description:
This API provides advanced search capabilities for refund, return, and cancellation requests. The request body supports filters on request type, status (pending, approved, declined, etc.), initiating actor, associated order, and time periods. Pagination and sorting options are included to support high-volume admin workflows and customer self-service scenarios.

Results include summary information about each request as defined in the Prisma schema, facilitating quick review. This operation supports business needs such as refund queue management, status monitoring, and audit reporting. The response provides a paginated list of refund requests with associated meta information.

Security is critical: results are filtered to only those requests the current actor is permitted to access (own refunds for customer, seller's order refunds for seller, globally for admin). Path parameters are not used; all filtering is via request body.

If no requests match the filters, an empty result set is returned. The operation's implementation aligns with the shopping_refund_requests schema comments and supports integration with related tables for joined/expanded details.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific refund, return, or cancellation request initiated by a customer or escalated by a seller/admin. It is centered on the Refunds table (shopping_refund_requests) and supports viewing all properties (type, status, reason, context), as well as relations to request items, parent order, actor, attached documents, and complete status history for audit/compliance flows. operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information about a specific refund request from the Refunds table (shopping_refund_requests).
operations.description:
This operation fetches all details of a single refund, return, or cancellation request for an order as recorded in the Refunds table (shopping_refund_requests) in the system. It provides complete properties of the refund request, including its type (refund, return, cancellation), requestor and actor context, business reason, workflow/status fields, timestamps, and audit traces.

Refund request state transitions, status history logs, attached documents or supporting evidence, and associated order lines/items are included—allowing full tracking for customer service, admin arbitration, or seller communication. Security is critical: only the requestor, associated order/admin, or parties with explicit access rights may access private refund details. Unauthenticated or unrelated actors are forbidden from receiving sensitive data. Detailed error handling ensures the existence of the refund request, access permission, and logic against exposing ineligible data.

This API forms the backbone of after-sales flows and should be integrated with business logic for eligibility, status tracking, and documentation. Related operations include refund request creation, refund item editing, status update, and admin override endpoints.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target refund request (UUID in shopping_refund_requests.id)

responseBody.description: Detailed information of the refund request including all business, item, and audit fields.

It creates a record in the Refunds table (shopping_refund_requests) with all required business fields, including request type, affected order, reason, and context. All business logic validations of eligibility, duplicate/preventing requests, and item selection are handled by the service. Attachments and linked refund request items may be specified for granular refund lines. This operation is foundational to supporting compliant after-sales workflows, dispute processes, and automated or manual escalation logic.

operations.description:
This operation enables eligible customers, sellers, or admins to create a new refund, return, or cancellation request associated with an existing order. The request must include all mandatory business fields defined in the Refunds table (shopping_refund_requests), such as order linkage, requestor information, request type (refund, return, cancellation), the business rationale, and structured context if needed.

The operation will enforce all eligibility, prevent duplicate or erroneous submissions (such as multiple refund requests for a single order line), and tie any provided refund request items to individual order lines. Supporting documents or image attachments (via linked entities), as well as audit traceability, are handled as part of the operation. Security is paramount: only authenticated and authorized users may submit refund requests, and validations ensure order and item ownership, adherence to platform policy, and compliance tracking.

Error scenarios (such as submitting a refund for an ineligible or non-owned order) trigger business error responses as per compliance requirements. Related endpoints include refund info retrieval, status update, item and attachment manipulation, and admin override/dispute intervention systems.

responseBody.description: Full detailed record of the newly created refund/return/cancellation request with all core fields and audit fields as per Refunds table.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes (archives) a refund, return, or cancellation request in the shopping platform by updating its deleted_at field. The operation targets the shopping_refund_requests table in the Prisma schema, which represents user-initiated or escalated refund/cancellation/return processes. Hard delete is not performed to ensure business continuity and compliance—instead, a soft delete marks the request as removed from active processes. Only authorized/admin actors or the originator of the request are permitted to perform this operation, and critical business and legal checks are enforced before deletion is allowed. All deletion activities are fully logged.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows an authorized actor (admin or original requester) to archive (soft delete) an existing refund, return, or cancellation request by populating the deleted_at timestamp. The soft delete operation ensures auditability and compliance with legal recordkeeping, instead of physically removing the database record. The API validates that the refund request is eligible for deletion (not currently under review or in a locked business status), and only the owner (customer/seller who initiated it) or an approved admin may delete the request.

The operation audits every deletion event with actor, timestamp, and reason, and logs all unsuccessful deletion attempts for compliance review. Related endpoints may include listing or querying deleted records, restoring records (if business policy allows), and audit-log access for legal disputes. Attempts to delete ineligible or system-locked requests will return a detailed error. The operation references the shopping_refund_requests table and strictly follows all business constraints on deletion eligibility.

This operation enables actors to search, filter, and page through refund items pertaining to the original refund request, referencing the shopping_refund_request_items table in the Prisma schema. Each refund item provides full context: the associated order line, SKU, quantity, business reason if set at item level, status, and creation/modification timestamps.

Security and permissions: The endpoint is available to authenticated users with legitimate interest in the refund (customer who initiated, seller of the orders involved, or admin overseeing disputes). The business logic ensures that only those with appropriate access to the parent refund request may query its items, with additional constraints for sensitive order details.

Business workflow connections: Listing refund items supports both UI and automated workflows—such as reviewing pending claims, processing partial approvals/denials, and auditing refund eligibility by status and linkage. Filtering capabilities let actors focus on items needing manual action or escalation, while pagination ensures efficiency on large/multi-item requests. Errors for missing or ineligible refundRequestId are handled with explicit business codes and user guidance.

operations.specification: This operation allows the addition of a new refund request item to an existing refund request in the shopping platform. It is strictly associated with the 'shopping_refund_request_items' table, representing the linkage of specific order line items to a customer's active refund, return, or cancellation case. It enables itemized handling of individual order lines (SKUs) for refund eligibility, supporting per-SKU quantity and optional business reason overrides distinct from the overall request. The operation ensures only authorized actors (typically the refund requester) may add items to pending refund requests. The API validates that the parent refund request is eligible for modification and that each item added is unique and within valid quantity constraints.
operations.description:
This API endpoint enables a user to add a new refund request item under an existing refund request, typically after the initial refund request has been created but before it is finalized. The operation is designed for use-cases where a customer needs to append additional SKU(s) or specific order line(s) to the open refund process, or when additional issues with an order arise after the original submission. 

The endpoint enforces eligibility by confirming that the refund request identified by the required path parameter is still in a modifiable state (not completed or closed), and checks that the item being added (identified by order line) is not already present as a refund request item for this refund request. Item quantities must not exceed the quantity available in the corresponding order line. If the business reason for this item differs from the parent's business reason, it can be specified here for clarity. 

Security and authorization are enforced such that only authorized actors (typically the original requester, such as the customer, or an admin if the process is escalated) may add items. The operation references and validates relationships to the refund request, order, and order line via internal business logic, ensuring business rules and data constraints are satisfied. Relevant error scenarios include attempts to add duplicate items, exceeding allowable quantities, or modifying non-editable refund requests.

This provides flexible support for rectifying mistakes or adjusting item-level details before escalation or final approval of the parent refund request.
