operations.description:
This API operation permanently removes a specific refund request item from an existing refund request, provided both the overall request and the item are eligible for deletion according to business rules. The refundRequestId in the path identifies the parent refund request, and itemId identifies the refund item that will be deleted. This operation is typically used when a customer or admin decides to remove a particular item from a pending or draft refund or return, given that the refund or return process has not yet been completed or irrevocably processed.

For security, only actors who own the refund request item (such as the requesting customer) and administrators may delete refund items. Audit logging is enforced for all deletions, and attempts to delete a processed or ineligible item will result in a clear error. This operation references the shopping_refund_request_items table, which connects refund requests to specific order lines and supports partial item-based refunds. Related refund statuses and summaries are recomputed after deletion, with error responses in case of integrity constraint violation.

The API is related to refund request item management and is often used in conjunction with refund request composition or update flows. If a refund processing decision or payment has already occurred, deletion is disallowed. All changes are audited and retrievable via the refund management audit trail.

The refundRequestId path parameter indicates which refund request's files will be retrieved. The operation supports advanced search, filtering, and pagination criteria via a structured request body and returns a paginated summary structure for all attachment records. This is used for auditor, admin, or customer self-service review of attached evidence prior to administrative action on the refund case.

Authorization is restricted to users who are owners of the refund request or administrative actors. Data is sourced from the shopping_refund_attachments table, joined with the file entity and indexed for efficient query by attachment_type, date, or description. Supports business flows such as dispute evidence checks, refund review, or legal audit. Related endpoints include refund attachment upload, deletion, and download operations.

When used in combination with administrative flows or compliance processes, this endpoint enables full traceability and review for all evidence associated with a given refund request.

operations.specification: This operation allows authorized actors (customers, sellers, admins) to upload a new attachment to an existing refund request. It interacts with the shopping_refund_attachments table, which maintains files and evidence associated with return, refund, or cancellation workflows. Valid attachment types include photos, scanned documents, and other supporting evidence required by business policy. It requires the refundRequestId as a path parameter to associate the new attachment and a structured request body specifying file metadata, type, and URI. The system enforces file size, type, and per-request limits as specified in business rules. File storage is handled externally; the attachment record links to the persistent file URI.
operations.description:
Upload a new evidence file or attachment to a pending refund or return claim. Customers, sellers, or admins may provide documentation such as receipt images, defect photos, or shipping invoices to support the case.

This operation first validates that the refund request exists and is accessible to the actor, who must be either the customer who filed the request, a seller listed on the order, or an admin. File type, size, and quota are checked against policy constraints. On success, the operation records the attachment metadata (file URI, type, and size) and links it to the refundRequestId.

The physical file upload is presumed to be completed in advance; this API only registers the metadata and logical attachment link. It returns metadata for the new attachment, which can then be accessed or later reviewed by actor or admin. The operation enforces security, audit trail, and business logic in accordance with the shopping_refund_attachments schema.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a specific attachment from a refund request. It operates on the shopping_refund_attachments table, which links file attachments (e.g., evidence documents, photos) to a parent refund request within the refund management system. Only the owner of the refund request or an appropriate admin/seller actor can invoke this deletion, in accordance with business logic and audit requirements. The operation physically removes the association and underlying attachment for the specified request/item attachment, provided they exist and are eligible for removal.
operations.summary: Permanently delete an attachment from a refund request (shopping_refund_attachments).
operations.description:
This operation deletes an attachment belonging to a specific refund request, removing both the link and the stored file reference from the refund process. It strictly enforces authorization by verifying that only the actor who created the refund request, or platform administrators, can perform deletion.

The operation checks that the targeted attachmentId is actually linked under the provided refundRequestId before deletion is allowed, ensuring there is no accidental unlinking across requests or orphaned references. Both refundRequestId and attachmentId must be valid UUIDs and correspond to an existing parent-child relationship for the deletion to succeed.

Business audit and compliance rules dictate that deleted attachments be recorded in system logs. Any attempt to delete an attachment not owned by the actor, or which is not linked to the specified refund request, triggers an error. Attachments may not be deleted from closed or administratively locked refund requests unless executed by an admin actor. Actual file blobs will be deleted from storage as part of this operation to maintain storage integrity.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the full status change history for a refund request by querying the shopping_refund_status_histories table. It is valuable to actors who need to audit or track progression of a specific refund, including all business decisions, actor transitions, and contextual updates. The response provides a paginated, chronological list of all state transitions made for the given refund request.
operations.summary: Retrieve the paginated status history for a refund request (shopping_refund_status_histories).
operations.description:
Retrieves the chronological list of all status changes applied to a specific refund request. This includes every state transition, the actor who performed it (customer, seller, admin), timestamp, and any attached context or notes. Enables compliance and support teams to review the full workflow of a refund/return/cancellation case.

The operation supports advanced filtering by actor type, specific statuses, and date ranges when supplied in the request body. Pagination parameters allow results to be batched and sorted for efficient navigation in case of extensive audit trails. Consumers of this endpoint typically include admins reviewing compliance, sellers overseeing requests involving their products/orders, and customers tracking the lifecycle of their refund claims.

The input refundRequestId must identify an existing refund request, and the caller must be authorized for the underlying business context. Any status history found is returned in order from oldest to newest unless sorting options are specified. Error responses occur if the request does not exist, or if the actor lacks permission to view the refund's history.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target refund request to retrieve its status history (UUID format, global scope).

requestBody.description: Criteria for filtering, sorting, and paginating the list of refund status histories. This may include actor type, specific status transitions, date ranges, and sort order.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of refund status history entries matching the specified criteria, including all transition details, actors, and contextual metadata.

operations.name: index

prerequisites.description: A refund request must be created before its status history can be retrieved. The refundRequestId used in this operation comes from the created refund request.

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves a specific status history entry for a refund request. It operates on the shopping_refund_status_histories table, which logs all status transition events for refund requests. The endpoint allows audit, debugging, and user-facing display of the status history, enabling retracing of business workflows for refund/return cases.

The refundRequestId parameter identifies the refund request parent, while the statusHistoryId parameter is the PK of the target status history record. Both IDs are required for a unique lookup. The operation enforces permission requirements: only the requesting customer, participating seller, or admins with adequate rights can access the status history of a refund they are authorized to view. Access to sensitive context provided in transition logs must be filtered/hidden where business rules require it (for example, customer seeing an admin rationale).
operations.summary: Retrieve a specific refund request status transition history entry (shopping_refund_status_histories table).
operations.description:
Provides detailed information for a status transition event from the refund workflow's audit trail. Typically used for displaying the full context of refund approval/escalation steps, including the actor, timestamp, previous/new statuses, and rationale provided.

Only allowed actors (the refund applicant, participating seller, or admins) are permitted to access the entry. Sensitive notes or context must be filtered based on user type, with customer/seller seeing only business-appropriate commentary, while admin can view all audit details.

Related operations for viewing the entire history can be implemented as a collection endpoint on /refunds/{refundRequestId}/statuses. This endpoint is for individual entry lookup, and returns all available fields subject to visibility rules.

If the record does not exist or the actor is not authorized, an error must be returned (not found or forbidden as appropriate).

parameters.name: refundRequestId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the refund request (global scope).

parameters.name: statusHistoryId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific status history entry (scoped to refund request).

responseBody.description: Detailed status transition event for the refund request, including timestamp, actor, previous/new status, and rationale/context (as permitted for the caller).

operations.specification:
This operation returns a filtered and paginated list of approval/rejection records associated with a specific refund request, corresponding to the shopping_refund_approvals table. Refund approval records log every admin or seller approval/rejection act for status changes, providing traceability and enabling business/audit views of the decision history for a refund case.

The refundRequestId parameter identifies the refund process being audited. Caller must be an authorized party (refund applicant or admin). For complex audit/operations tracing across many records, this endpoint supports search, sort, and pagination using a structured request body.
operations.summary: Search and list approval/rejection actions for a given refund request (shopping_refund_approvals table).
operations.description:
Enables authorized users or admins to retrieve a paginated list of all seller and admin approval or rejection records tied to a particular refund request. This supports business audit, regulatory review, and dispute investigation by exposing an authoritative record of all actions taken on refund status transitions.

The endpoint supports advanced filtering—by actor, action type (approval/rejection), and time window—as well as paginated delivery of result sets using request parameters. Access is limited to authorized actors to ensure privacy, and sensitive rationale/notes are selectively shown based on the actor requesting the data (full detail for admin, business-safe versions for customers).

Related operations include GET for single approval records and PATCH with search criteria across multiple refund requests for admin/business analytics. Errors are returned if the refund request does not exist or the actor lacks permission.

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the refund request this approval action belongs to (global scope).

requestBody.description: Paging, filtering, and search criteria for refund approval records (actor, action, date, etc.).

responseBody.description: Paginated, filtered list of all approval/rejection actions with selected audit context, filtered according to actor privilege.

The API requires both the refund request ID and the approval ID as path parameters to accurately locate the approval action. This endpoint enables clients or admins to fetch full details of an individual refund approval, including actor, action status, rationale, and related audit timestamps. The operation is essential for examining the approval history, compliance processes, or resolving refund workflow disputes. It is strictly a read-only operation and is fundamental to providing traceability in refund request workflows.
operations.summary: Retrieve details of a specific refund approval action for a refund request (shopping_refund_approvals table).
operations.description:
Retrieve complete information for a single approval action related to a customer refund request. This endpoint fetches all attributes—such as the approval actor (admin or seller), action type (approved or rejected), notes, and associated timestamps—from the shopping_refund_approvals table. 

This API provides critical visibility into the approval decision chain for a given refund process, allowing compliance and support teams to audit, troubleshoot, or present decision trails to external stakeholders when necessary. It is particularly relevant to admin actors monitoring refund escalations, as well as platform logic that needs an authoritative record of user or admin decisions. Read-only access minimizes risk of accidental changes, and strictly enforced parameter validation ensures only designated actors can retrieve approval records.

This endpoint expects both the refundRequestId and approvalId as URL path parameters. Both values must be provided as UUID strings, referencing the composite unique indexing and foreign key integrity defined in the Prisma schema for robust security and data traceability.

responseBody.description: Full refund approval object as defined in IShoppingRefundApproval, detailing actor, action type, audit trail, and business context.

The API aggregates override records—such as force approvals, forced rejections, or business/legal escalations—providing a compliant, audit-friendly timeline. By requiring the refund request ID as a path parameter, this PATCH endpoint allows targeted queries and supports advanced filtering, pagination, and sorting through the request body. The design is tailored for administrative actors overseeing disputed or complex refunds, fulfilling rigorous trace and compliance requirements.
operations.summary: Search and page through all admin refund override actions for a given refund request (shopping_refund_admin_overrides table).
operations.description:
Search and retrieve a paginated listing of all override/escalation actions performed by platform admins against a particular refund request. This endpoint surfaces complete details—including override type, business/legal reason, timestamp, admin actor, and detailed context—for every override action, as modeled by the shopping_refund_admin_overrides table.

Built for compliance, dispute management, and regulatory inquiry, this API supports advanced query patterns: filter override actions by type, actor, time range, or business rationale, paginate large volumes of records, and deliver full context for each override. This allows platform teams, auditors, and legal reviewers to quickly assemble a chronological timeline for any refund dispute or intervention, supporting evidence-based resolution and proactive monitoring.

The refundRequestId path parameter targets the precise refund request under review, and requestBody structures enable flexible search and secure filtering. Results are always paginated for reliability and performance in audit scenarios.

The operation is typically used by platform admin users engaged in audit investigations, dispute resolutions, or regular compliance reviews. Only admin actors with appropriate privileges can access this endpoint, and the data returned reflects all relevant fields (except sensitive business context may be redacted according to policy).

operations.specification: This operation provides advanced search of shipments within the shopping mall platform. operations.description:

It handles complex queries over the shopping_shipments records, allowing filters such as shipment status, carrier company, code, seller, scheduled or dispatched time frames, and other relevant logistics parameters.

The search supports both administrative users (platform-wide visibility of all shipments) and sellers (restricted to their own shipments). The endpoint enforces result pagination and provides options for sorting by various dates or business status fields for effective logistics management.

The operation is designed to provide a complete snapshot of shipment state for tracking and audit purposes. The shipment code is a human-friendly identifier that ensures business traceability without exposing internal IDs. All retrieval strictly excludes soft-deleted records (deleted_at is null) following the business restrictions of the schema and requirements.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information for a specific shipment by code from shopping_shipments.
operations.description:
Retrieve a single shipment's details by its unique code. This endpoint returns all essential shipment fields such as status, carrier company, dispatch and delivery dates, and associated metadata, for both customer and operations use cases.

Authorization is generally required for viewing shipment details, with role-based restrictions: customers may only view their own shipment codes; sellers may view only those for their products; admins may access all shipments. This aligns with business logic in shopping_shipments and the requirements for secure, auditable tracking.

Full tracking and historical status information are not included here but may be retrieved using subsidiary audit endpoints. Error responses occur if the shipment code does not exist or is not accessible by the actor context, matching platform security standards.

Business rules enforce that only actors with rights to the shipment (owning seller or admin) can update, and soft-deleted records are not modifiable. This update operation follows platform-level audit and security best practices per business requirements and the schema.

Only authorized sellers (who own the shipment) and administrators are permitted to update this record. The request body structure references the update DTO, mapping schema fields to updatable shipment attributes per platform requirements. Authorization and validation logic ensure correct application of business rules.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a shipment record identified by its unique business code from the shopping_shipments table. Deletion is only allowed if the shipment has not yet been dispatched or delivered, ensuring compliance with business process controls. The operation is designed to facilitate correction of data or operational errors prior to actual shipment activities. It is associated with the shopping_shipments table and enforces authorization checks to prevent removal of shipments that are in critical fulfillment status.
operations.description:
This API endpoint allows an authorized actor to remove a shipment record from the system before any dispatch or delivery actions have been taken. The operation performs a hard delete because the shopping_shipments table supports a deleted_at soft-delete field, but the intended usage is to erase shipments that are not relevant for business and legal compliance once a shipment has been physically sent. 

Only users with administrative privileges or shipping managers who have ensured the shipment has not been dispatched may execute this operation safely. Attempting to delete shipments that have been dispatched or delivered will result in a business logic error, preserving audit integrity and fulfillment tracking.

The operation validates that the provided code corresponds to a valid, not-yet-dispatched shipment. Security checks must ensure that only users with proper privileges (typically admin or fulfillment supervisor) may execute this operation. Related records in subsidiary tables such as packages and tracking data are handled according to business retention rules. Proper error and audit logging is enforced in order to support regulatory and operational post-mortem analysis.
operations.summary: Permanently remove a shipment record by its unique code from the shopping_shipments table, prior to any dispatch or delivery.

parameters.description: Unique business code identifying the target shipment (global scope) to be deleted. Example: SHPT-2025-0001

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a filtered, paginated list of all shipment packages associated with a specific shipment, identified by its business code in the shopping_shipments table. The operation executes advanced search, filtering, and sorting over package-level details—such as tracking numbers, package label, status, delivery dates, and courier data—across all packages belonging to the referenced shipment. It is built for audit, troubleshooting, and fulfillment tracking workflows and is grounded in the shopping_shipment_packages model, with the parent shipment identified by its unique code.
operations.description:
This API endpoint allows administrators, shipping managers, and authorized operators to search and browse all shipment package units for a single shipment. The operation supports flexible search filters (package status, label, tracking number, sequence, delivery state), pagination, and sorting to enable end-to-end visibility of packaging and fulfillment for a single shipment. Package details support audit and real-time operational troubleshooting.

Path parameter validation ensures that the provided business code exists in the shopping_shipments table and filters only packages attached to that shipment. Search and sort options are customizable through the request body (IShoppingShipmentPackage.IRequest), allowing for highly granular package inspection within a shipment.

Security considerations restrict access to admin actors to preserve delivery performance and package integrity. API responses conform to data privacy and operational standards for shipment package information. This endpoint supports core operational metrics for logistics performance tracking and exception management.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve paginated, filterable list of all packages related to a shipment by code.

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Unique business code identifying the shipment (global scope) whose packages are to be indexed. Example: SHPT-2025-0001

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for shipment packages (status, tracking number, sequence, delivery dates, etc.)

responseBody.description: Paginated list of shipment package summary objects matching search criteria, tied to the specified shipment code.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
This operation retrieves detailed information about a specific shipment package, allowing platforms, sellers, or customers to track the status and contents of a single package within the broader shipping process. This operation is associated with the shopping_shipment_packages table in the Prisma schema, which maintains all package-level tracking, fulfillment, and status details for shipments. The information returned includes the package's label, position within its shipment, carrier-assigned tracking number, current status (including delivery, lost, damaged states), weight and dimensions, and all relevant business and logistical metadata.

This endpoint enables granular tracking for scenarios involving split shipments, multi-package fulfillment, and real-time status display to users. Sensitive shipment data (such as carrier assignment or tracking numbers) is only accessible by authorized roles: sellers that own the shipment, the involved customer, and platform admins.

Security is a significant concern: only those with a legitimate business need (buyer, seller, admin) may retrieve package details. Direct package retrieval aids in troubleshooting lost or delayed shipments, handling customer inquiries, and integrating with external courier APIs. The operation must enforce that the provided shipment code and package label exist, belong to the same shipment, and that the requesting actor is authorized. This API returns hard-failure errors for unauthorized or non-existent packages, or for requests on packages belonging to another user or seller.

Related API operations include listing all packages for a given shipment and updating status via internal business events or third-party signals.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information for a specific shipment package by shipment code and package label (shopping_shipment_packages table).
operations.description:
This API operation retrieves the full set of details for a single shipment package based on the provided shipment code and package label path parameters. The underlying database table is shopping_shipment_packages, which stores package-specific data such as tracking number, label, dimensions, sequence in shipment, package status (pending, ready, shipped, delivered, lost, damaged), and audit timestamps.

The detailed package information includes all fields defined in the shopping_shipment_packages schema and is returned only if the shipment code and package label together uniquely identify a valid package. Security and data privacy are strictly enforced: only the customer who placed the order, the seller fulfilling the shipment, and authorized admins are permitted to access these details. Attempts to access unauthorized or non-existent packages will result in explicit error responses.

This operation is typically used to power user package tracking UIs, enable support for split or multi-package shipments, and deliver targeted notifications about shipping events (such as package scanned, out for delivery, delivered, or exceptions). If the shipment or package has been soft-deleted, this operation will not return package details and may return a 404 or business error.

Integration with related shipment APIs is facilitated by using the same package and shipment identification pattern; related endpoints include shipment-level detail retrieval, tracking event patch, and admin shipment audit.

parameters.name: packageLabel
parameters.description: Unique business identifier label of the target package within the shipment (scoped to shipment).

responseBody.description: Full details of the target shipment package as stored in shopping_shipment_packages, including tracking, status, dimensions, and event timestamps.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
This operation enables advanced tracking event search and retrieval for all tracking instances associated with a specific package in a shipment. It supports deep investigation into the status, location, and logistical lifecycle of one shipment package by returning all carrier/courier tracking entries as well as business and system event logs. The primary association is with shopping_shipment_trackings (for tracking status and last updates), as well as potentially associated tracking event logs for each instance. Typical use cases include customer self-service shipment tracing, seller troubleshooting of in-delivery issues, and admin-level auditing.

This PATCH operation is required (rather than GET), as it can perform complex search, filtering, or pagination over a potentially large number of tracking events and related status updates. The search request supports filtering by tracking source (courier, warehouse scan, manual, etc.), status, or event time window, and sorting, allowing for power-user and administrator scenarios where bulk insights or analytics are needed.

Access control mirrors package data protections: only the customer who ordered the shipment, the seller of the items, or platform admins may search tracking events. Error handling must rigorously check that codes/labels are valid and properly related, and restrict data based on business actor identity. This operation forms a core part of real-time shipment status dashboards for end-users and support staff.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve all tracking instances with events for a shipment package (shopping_shipment_trackings table) with advanced filtering and pagination.
operations.description:
This endpoint enables clients to search and paginate through all tracking entries and their detailed event logs associated with a specific shipment package. It operates principally on the shopping_shipment_trackings and shopping_shipment_tracking_events tables, allowing for granular examination of both carrier/courier tracking data and internal shipping lifecycle events.

The request body (IShoppingShipmentTracking.IRequest) supports filters for tracking source (e.g., courier, warehouse scan), event window (start/end date), status (in_transit, delivered, delayed, lost), and custom business tag, along with pagination and sort properties. The result (IPageIShoppingShipmentTracking) is a paginated array of tracking instances, each including current status, last known location, and all historical event records, suitable for both real-time user tracking and operational or admin analytics.

Strict access controls are enforced: only users with a direct business relationship to the shipment (buyer, seller, admin) are allowed results. Non-existent or mismatched codes/labels will result in failed lookups. This operation supports shipping dashboards, logistics analytics, and support workflows where incident investigation for lost or delayed packages is necessary.

parameters.description: Unique business identifier code for the target shipment (global scope).

parameters.name: packageLabel
parameters.description: Unique business identifier label of the target package within the shipment (scoped to shipment).

requestBody.description: Filtering, sorting, pagination, and advanced tracking query parameters for shipment tracking events.

responseBody.description: A paginated result set of all matching tracking instances, each with status and event event histories, for shipment package.

This operation allows authorized actors to retrieve real-time tracking information for a shipping package within a given shipment. operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of all tracking events associated with a specific shipment package and tracking source, as defined by the shipment code, package label, and tracking source path parameters. It operates primarily on the shopping_shipment_tracking_events table, which stores an immutable, append-only log of all scan, status, and carrier callback events for each tracking reference. It joins with shopping_shipments, shopping_shipment_packages, and shopping_shipment_trackings to ensure full relationship integrity. The endpoint enables fine-grained, audit-level access to shipping activity for logistics transparency, exception investigation, and compliance. Only authorized actors for the shipment (customer, seller, admin) may access this resource. The operation supports pagination, full-text search on event code/status/location, and sorting as defined in the request schema.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve tracking events for a specific package tracking instance (shopping_shipment_tracking_events).
operations.description:
This operation provides a filtered and paginated event log of all tracking updates, scan events, and status changes for a given shipment package reference and tracking source. The lookup is resolved by joining on the shipment code, package label, and tracking source, ultimately resolving the tracking instance (shopping_shipment_trackings.id) and returning all associated tracking event records from shopping_shipment_tracking_events.

Typical use cases include displaying shipment tracking history to customers (e.g., delivery progress screens), enabling seller support for delivery disputes or exceptions, and providing administrators with a full audit trail for compliance and incident management. The returned list contains carrier and system-generated tracking milestones, location data, time stamps, and event details as stored in the Prisma schema fields.

Actor authentication is enforced: only parties associated with the shipment (purchasing customer, responsible seller, or admin) may access this endpoint. Rate limiting is applied to prevent excessive carrier polling or brute-force enumeration. Expected error scenarios include unresolved or expired package labels, tracking source mismatches, permission denials, and unsupported event queries.

Related endpoints: use the GET tracking instance endpoint for aggregate status and summary before drilling down to full event history. The search supports filter, sort, and pagination criteria as defined in the request schema.

operations.specification: This operation provides a filtered, paginated search over customer product reviews in the shopping mall platform. It primarily serves the use case where a customer, seller, or admin wants to retrieve a list of reviews based on various filters and sorting criteria. The data is sourced from the shopping_reviews table in the Prisma schema, which uniquely associates each review with a customer, SKU, and order line, and tracks star rating, comment, state, and audit fields. This endpoint supports review aggregation, moderation, search-by-rating, report export, and analytics. Pagination, search, and advanced filtering are supported via the request body. Only reviews in a visible, non-deleted state are included unless otherwise specified in the query. Authorization is enforced by reviews' foreign keys and role-based access.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve filtered, paginated list of product reviews (shopping_reviews)
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of product reviews submitted by customers for products and SKUs on the shopping mall platform. This operation allows searching by review state, star rating, associated product or SKU, customer ID, order line, keywords within comments, and date range. The response includes review summary information for admin, seller, or customer display, showing each review's unique identifiers, rating, truncated comment, state, creation/update dates, and author details per role permissions.

Pagination and sorting are fully supported via the request body parameters, with page size and offset controls. Security is enforced according to the actor accessing the endpoint—admins may access all reviews, sellers those for their products, and customers only their own. Integration with review moderation and abuse workflows is supported. Errors include unauthorized access, invalid parameters, and exceeded page size limits.

requestBody.description: Review search and filter criteria including pagination and advanced filters

responseBody.description: Paginated list of review summary information matching search criteria

operations.specification: This operation creates a new customer review for a specific SKU associated with an order. It integrates with the shopping_reviews table, enforcing the business rule that only customers who have completed delivery for a purchased item (order line) may submit a review for that SKU. The API captures a star rating between 1 and 5, a required textual comment, and may optionally support file/image/video attachments by referencing the review attachments system. Review eligibility is strictly validated on the server by verifying the mapping between the authenticated customer, the target SKU, and the corresponding order line. The operation also initializes the review state as 'visible' or may enter 'pending_moderation' depending on automated policy checks or suspicious content flags. Duplicate reviews per order line and SKU are prohibited by database unique constraints.
operations.description:
This endpoint allows a customer who has received an order to submit a new review for a specific SKU purchased as part of that order. The review must include a star rating (1–5), a written comment (10–2000 characters), and can optionally include up to five images or videos as attachments, each less than 5MB. The customer must be authenticated and have valid eligibility for the review: only SKUs actually delivered to the customer (one review per SKU per order line).

Upon submission, the API creates a new record in shopping_reviews, linking the review with the customer, SKU, and order line. It checks for duplicates and blocks submissions violating the one-per-order-line rule. Attachments are registered via subsidiary tables and checked for file type and size. The initial state of the review is typically 'visible,' but may be set to 'pending_moderation' if content is flagged for abuse or requires admin review.

Only authenticated customers may create reviews via this endpoint. Sellers and admins do not have access to this operation. The API responds with complete review details, including unique identifiers, timestamps, and links to any associated attachments.
operations.summary: Create a new review for a SKU in an order (shopping_reviews table)

requestBody.description: Review submission payload including rating (1–5), comment, SKU and order line associations, and optional attachments. Attachments must be referenced as URIs within constraints.

responseBody.description: Created review entity, including all fields, relationships, and attachment references.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing customer review for a specific SKU within an order, in the shopping_reviews table. Only the review's comment, rating, and attachments (if within the allowed editing window—by default, 7 days from original creation) may be modified via this API. The system enforces the unique relationship between customer, SKU, and order line to confirm authorship, and will block edits attempted outside the permitted window, returning an explicit error code if expired. Updated review content is subjected to the same validation and moderation checks as original submissions, including content length, rating value range (1–5), and optional attachment compliance. Upon success, the API returns the revised, current review record.
operations.description:
Allows an authenticated customer to update their own review for a given SKU in a specific order line. The review can be edited only within a defined period after initial submission (default 7 days); outside this window, edits are blocked. The allowed fields for update are the numerical rating, the written comment, and the associated attachments (e.g., up to five images/videos under 5MB each). Attempts to change the review after the window expires will result in error code 'REVIEW_EDIT_WINDOW_EXPIRED.'

The API first validates review authorship, order eligibility, and update permissions. It then applies changes to the review in the shopping_reviews table and updates any attachments in the related records. Updated reviews must pass the same content and moderation validations as new submissions. The operation returns the updated review entity, including identifiers, new content, and any attachments.

Only the original customer author may use this endpoint. Reviews in 'removed' or 'under_review' state are not eligible for update without admin intervention.

This operation executes a hard deletion: the review record and its associated attachments are physically removed from the database, in accordance with applicable business and compliance rules. It is designed for use by the review's author (the customer, within the allowed editing window) or by privileged platform administrators, such as in cases of moderation or compliance actions.

This API endpoint deletes a customer review from the system by reviewId, removing the review record and all its related attachments. The review must exist in the shopping_reviews table and meet the criteria for deletion: either the customer is the original author and within the permitted edit/remove window, or an admin is performing a compliance or moderation removal.

Security considerations require strict authorization: customers may only delete their own reviews within policy limits, and actions outside this window are restricted to users with admin privileges. Attempts to delete reviews outside these rules will return an appropriate error code and rationale.

Once this operation succeeds, the review and its references are no longer available in search, product displays, or aggregation calculations. Hard deletes are permanent and cannot be reversed, respecting any audit or legal retention policies in effect. Error handling ensures that if the review does not exist or the actor lacks permission, clear business error codes are returned to the client.

The review must exist in the shopping_reviews table and meet the criteria for deletion: either the customer is the original author and within the permitted edit/remove window, or an admin is performing a compliance or moderation removal.

Security considerations require strict authorization: customers may only delete their own reviews within policy limits, and actions outside this window are restricted to users with admin privileges. Attempts to delete reviews outside these rules will return an appropriate error code and rationale.

Once this operation succeeds, the review and its references are no longer available in search, product displays, or aggregation calculations. Hard deletes are permanent and cannot be reversed, respecting any audit or legal retention policies in effect. Error handling ensures that if the review does not exist or the actor lacks permission, clear business error codes are returned to the client.

Attempts to access attachments for non-existent or unauthorized reviews result in detailed business error messages. Data returned excludes files marked as deleted unless specified.

Related APIs include PATCH /reviews (for review searching) and GET /products/{productId}/reviews for broader context. This endpoint is essential for transparency in the feedback process and compliance with content moderation requirements.

operations.description:
This API operation retrieves the metadata and download URI for a single attachment associated with a specific review. Clients may use this to fetch images, videos, or documents included as part of a customer review.

Strict authorization is enforced: only the review author (customer), business admins (admin), or relevant seller-side actors (seller) may access the attachment resource. Soft-deleted records are excluded, and requests for non-associated attachment/review pairs are treated as not found.

If validation fails (review not found, attachment missing/deleted, or auth failure), an error is returned. The response includes the attachment's metadata and its secure URI (string). Attachments are always associated to their parent review and never exposed if the review is deleted or locked for moderation. All accesses are audited.

This operation references shopping_reviews and shopping_review_attachments. Fine-grained error handling is recommended.

The review must be active and visible. Only reviews owned by the authenticated customer or by admins may have attachments created. Files and metadata (type, URI, size) are validated against all constraints—including type, size, and per-review attachment limits. Records are inserted into shopping_review_attachments and returned to the client. Auditing is mandatory.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a file attachment from a customer review. The attachment entity is uniquely identified by a combination of the review's UUID ('reviewId') and the attachment's UUID ('attachmentId'), both of which are path parameters. This operation is tied to the 'shopping_review_attachments' Prisma table, which stores file metadata and references the parent review. Hard deletion is performed as there is no soft-delete field in the schema for attachments (only an optional 'deleted_at' timestamp is present for audit purposes). Ownership and permission checks confirm that the requesting actor is the review owner (for customers) or a platform admin. The attachment URI and file metadata are removed from all review displays; if the last attachment is deleted, the review remains but the media section is empty. Related operations include creating new attachments, deleting the parent review, or uploading new evidence for moderation. Error scenarios cover attempts to delete non-existent or unauthorized attachments.
operations.description:
This operation allows a customer (who created the review) or an admin to permanently remove an attachment (such as an image or video) from a specific product review. The review is identified by its unique 'reviewId' UUID, and the attachment is specified by its unique 'attachmentId' UUID, ensuring only the correct file is deleted.

Removal of an attachment is immediate and cannot be undone; if the attachment file is shared elsewhere on the platform, it is only removed from the current review context. Security checks ensure that only the owning customer or an authorized admin can perform this deletion. The operation is especially important for compliance with user privacy, copyright, and moderation requests (such as removing inappropriate or private content).

This operation interacts closely with the 'shopping_review_attachments' Prisma table, which links files to reviews using the defined UUIDs. All deletions are logged for audit history. Error cases include deletion of attachments that do not exist, belong to another user, or have already been deleted; these return a not found or forbidden error. Related operations include adding attachments when editing or creating reviews and admin-initiated moderation workflows.

It is associated directly with the 'shopping_review_moderations' Prisma table, which logs every moderation event, the actor (admin), timestamp, and rationale. Advanced filtering by moderator, action type, affected review, and date range is supported via request body parameters. This endpoint is intended for use by platform admins for compliance, audit, and monitoring purposes. The response includes detailed moderation history for each review, allowing searching and analysis of moderation patterns and state changes over time. This operation does not allow modifications or deletions; it is strictly read-only for audit and review lifecycle tracking.
operations.description:
This operation enables platform administrators to search and review the complete moderation history applied to customer product reviews. Each record corresponds to a moderation event (such as approval, removal, flag, or restoration) and details the acting admin, action taken, associated review, rationale, and timestamp. The operation supports advanced filtering, including moderator identity, action type, affected review ID, and custom date windows for compliance investigations.

Moderation logs are critical for audit and transparency: all moderation decisions taken on reviews are persisted in the 'shopping_review_moderations' Prisma table, offering a detailed trail for compliance and business oversight. The operation returns a paginated response using the IPageIShoppingReviewModeration.ISummary DTO, optimized for list and reporting views.

Security is enforced to ensure that only users with admin privileges can access this endpoint. No modification or deletion of moderation logs is possible through this API; other endpoints support edit and delete actions as required. The operation is closely related to admin dashboards and reporting systems, allowing detailed cross-referencing and compliance verification.

This endpoint is essential for administrative or legal transparency, enabling full traceability of review moderation decisions on the platform. Only admins or actors with elevated permissions can access this operation, as it exposes sensitive audit log information.

The moderation record must be uniquely identified based on the context of the review and moderation IDs, following the composite unique constraints in the schema. The related reviewId and moderationId must both be supplied in the path for correct lookup and context disambiguation. The response provides full information needed to support audits, appeals, and compliance reviews associated with moderation activity.

This operation retrieves a paginated list of abuse reports associated with a specific product review. The underlying data is managed by the shopping_review_abuse_reports table, which captures individual abuse report entries by customers against a given review. This endpoint provides review owners, moderators, and administrators with visibility into potential abuse, spam, or inappropriate content reports. The interface supports searching, filtering, and paginating through potentially large numbers of abuse reports per review. 

The endpoint accepts a PATCH request at /reviews/{reviewId}/abuseReports, referencing the parent review's unique identifier in the path parameter. It returns abuse report summaries without full review details for performance and security reasons. The request body allows the client to specify advanced filtering settings and pagination options—such as state, report type, date ranges, and sorted results. Authorization logic ensures only users with appropriate privileges (review author, admin, or content moderator) can view the full listing of abuse reports. Care is taken to expose only necessary details for each abuse report, adhering to privacy rules. This operation interacts directly with the shopping_review_abuse_reports table and supports efficient moderation workflows.
operations.summary: Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of abuse reports for a specific review (shopping_review_abuse_reports)
operations.description:
Retrieve and search all abuse reports associated with a product review to support moderation and transparency workflows.

This operation enables qualified actors to view who has reported a review, for what reason, the type of abuse, and the current moderation state for each report—while ensuring sensitive reporter details are masked or only visible to administrators in accordance with business rules. Multiple filtering options are available: type of abuse (e.g., spam, hate speech), date of report, and moderation status (open, processed, dismissed, removed). Pagination is provided for scalability and performance when handling reviews with a high number of reports.

The endpoint is used in conjunction with review detail endpoints and report abuse actions, enabling a complete moderation and transparency cycle for both review authors and platform admins. Error scenarios are handled according to authorization (permission denied), missing review reference, or invalid filtering options. Only reports not soft-deleted or hard-removed are returned.

The endpoint returns the complete record for this specific abuse report, including the reporter (masked or anonymized as needed), report type, reason/comment, timestamps, state, and the result of any moderation action taken. This is used in review moderation, abuse investigations, or administrative audits.

The path parameters ensure the abuse report is uniquely identified within the context of the target review, fully supporting composite uniqueness. Authorization is required and limited to platform administrators or designated moderators to protect privacy and support compliance. The endpoint is designed for GET requests at /reviews/{reviewId}/abuseReports/{abuseReportId}. Related endpoints include listing all abuse reports for a review and updating the report state.

The operation is most often used in admin dashboards or abuse investigation queues. Error responses are provided if access is denied, if the report or review does not exist, or if the requestor lacks permission to view sensitive details. Each report includes a report type such as 'spam', 'hate_speech', 'off_topic', or other valid codes, and may contain an optional explanatory comment. The abuse report is appended to the review for moderation and administrative actions, with auditability and traceability ensured via the schema's state, timestamps, and actor references. The business logic ensures only customers can report reviews, and that reports are correctly tied to the given review.

Submit a new abuse report against a specific review, linking the report to both the customer and the targeted review. The operation creates a record in the shopping_review_abuse_reports table, which captures the report type—such as 'spam', 'hate_speech', 'off_topic'—along with the reporting customer's ID and an optional comment. Only authenticated customers are eligible to submit such reports, and each report's creation timestamp, state, and content are auditable for platform compliance. Validation is enforced on the business domain, ensuring that duplicate reports or invalid report types are rejected based on enum constraints from the Prisma schema.

This operation is critical for facilitating community moderation and content compliance, as all abuse reports trigger a moderation workflow by admins per business requirements. Submitting an abuse report does not immediately hide the review but flags it for further review. All reports are soft-deletable and retain full audit trails, as described in the shopping_review_abuse_reports schema documentation.

Related endpoints include the ability for admins to process, resolve, or dismiss submitted abuse reports through moderation workflows. Unauthorized or invalid attempts to submit an abuse report (such as by non-customers or against non-existent reviews) are met with clear errors, as defined by schema constraints and business rules.

operations.specification: This operation enables a customer to update or supplement their abuse report for a specific review. It targets an existing abuse report identified by abuseReportId, linked to a review via reviewId. The Prisma schema shopping_review_abuse_reports enforces the connection and manages state transitions (such as 'open', 'processed', or 'dismissed'). The operation allows the customer to modify the report details, such as the explanatory comment or, if permitted by moderation rules, report type. All changes are fully audited and timestamped, maintaining compliance and traceability per business requirements. The update flow is governed by moderator workflow constraints: e.g., reports moved to state 'processed' by admins may no longer be editable by the reporter. Schema constraints enforce actor permissions and restrict updates to valid enumerated values.
operations.description:
Update an existing abuse report on a specific review. The operation supports modifications of comment or report type, provided the report is in an editable state (normally 'open') and the modification does not violate moderation rules. The shopping_review_abuse_reports table connects the report both to the target review and to the customer reporter, ensuring updates are audit-logged and all business rules are enforced.

Edit permissions are enforced based on the report state: once processed or dismissed by admins, further updates are typically blocked. All updated fields are validated against the schema, and the audit log retains both the original and updated values for compliance. This ensures complete traceability of abuse report handling throughout its lifecycle.

Error responses are generated for attempts to update non-existent, unauthorized, or immutable reports (such as those already resolved by moderation). Related operations include abuse report review and moderation endpoints for admin actors.
operations.summary: Update an existing abuse report for a specific review (shopping_review_abuse_reports).

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the review to which the abuse report belongs (UUID).

parameters.name: abuseReportId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the specific abuse report to update (UUID).

requestBody.description: Updated details for the abuse report, such as new comment or report type, respecting editing rules and current report state.

responseBody.description: The updated abuse report object reflecting the latest changes, including audit metadata, new state, and all business-allowed changes.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: An abuse report must exist before it can be updated; this ensures the target abuse report for the review exists and is in an updatable state.

operations.specification: This operation performs a hard delete of a specific abuse report associated with a product review. It directly manipulates the shopping_review_abuse_reports table, permanently removing the selected report identified by both the review's UUID and the sequential abuse report UUID. Unlike soft delete operations seen elsewhere in the system, this endpoint is used for administrative enforcement—such as conclusively dismissing resolved, fraudulent, or inapplicable abuse flags—in accordance with compliance, audit, and moderation policies.
operations.summary: Permanently delete an abuse report from a specific product review (shopping_review_abuse_reports).
operations.description:
This API operation allows a privileged actor—such as an admin moderator—to permanently remove an abuse report record from a specific review. The underlying business scenario typically involves finalized moderation, fraudulent reporting, or legal takedown, making this a destructive action recorded for platform compliance. 

Security considerations mandate that only privileged actors (admin) can perform this operation. All deletions trigger an audit trail in the admin operations log for later investigation or regulatory review. The corresponding abuse report will no longer be visible to any actor, and any resolution or associated moderation actions are retained separately in platform logs.

This operation references the shopping_review_abuse_reports table, requiring both the parent reviewId (UUID) and the abuseReportId (UUID). Both values are mapped 1:1 to ensure only the targeted abuse report for the correct review is deleted. If either UUID is invalid or not found, the operation returns a not found or permission denied error. No soft delete or recovery is provided through this API.

Integration with related API operations may occur when reviewing or resolving escalated review abuse complaints; typically, related GET endpoints for review or abuse report details are used in tandem when preparing for this action.

parameters.name: reviewId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target review (UUID, must match the review receiving the abuse report).

parameters.name: abuseReportId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the abuse report to be deleted from the specified review (UUID).

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: An abuse report must exist before it can be deleted by an admin; this ensures that a valid report for the target review is present in the system.

operations.specification: This operation fetches the current review and rating aggregate statistics for a specific SKU. It provides retrieval of up-to-date pre-aggregated review data such as average rating, review count, and overall summary statistics for the targeted SKU by referencing the shopping_review_rating_aggregates table. This is used to enhance catalog display and search for both customers and sellers.
operations.summary: Retrieve review & rating summary aggregate for a product SKU (shopping_review_rating_aggregates).
operations.description:
This API operation allows any actor (public) to fetch the detailed summary statistics for customer reviews and ratings associated with a particular product SKU. Typical use cases include displaying product star ratings, total review counts, and average scores in catalog listings, product pages, and search rankings.

For the given SKU, the API returns the corresponding summary object from the shopping_review_rating_aggregates table: including fields such as average_rating, review_count, product_review_count, and product_average_rating. Actors do not need to be authenticated for this operation as review/rating data is intended for broad public consumption and does not expose any personal information.

The required path parameter skuId is the UUID of the SKU being queried. If no review aggregate exists, a not found error is returned. This operation stands alone but is also commonly used in conjunction with product/variant detail endpoints in catalog APIs. This endpoint never requires a request body or sensitive authentication.

Error handling is limited to validation errors (UUID format) or missing data (404 not found).

parameters.name: skuId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target SKU (UUID) for which review aggregate summary is requested.

responseBody.description: Aggregated review and rating summary object for the requested SKU, as calculated and materialized in the shopping_review_rating_aggregates table.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: SKU must be created as part of a new product before its review aggregate statistics can exist or be retrieved.
SKU must be created under a product before review aggregates can be computed or accessed for it.

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the aggregated review statistics for a specific product, identified by its unique productId. It operates on the review aggregation materialized view linked to shopping_review_rating_aggregates, which stores summary data such as average rating and total number of reviews for each product and for each SKU. The primary function is to allow clients to display up-to-date, pre-aggregated rating and review counts for a product details page or in product search results, supporting efficient read access and performance. This endpoint does not reveal individual review content but focuses on statistical/aggregate metrics from the denormalized view for faster access. The product must exist in the shopping_products table, and the response is filtered specifically for the referenced productId. No modification to review data is performed by this operation. The source Prisma table is shopping_review_rating_aggregates, with relationships to both shopping_products and shopping_skus.
operations.summary: Get aggregate review/rating statistics for a specific product by unique productId from materialized review aggregates.
operations.description:
Retrieve pre-computed aggregate review statistics (such as total reviews and average rating) for a product, identified by its unique productId. These aggregate statistics are generated by the shopping_review_rating_aggregates view, which is associated with the shopping_products table and provides summary information for product and SKU level ratings.

This API endpoint is designed to optimize catalog and product page performance by delivering immediate access to pre-aggregated rating metrics, such as number of reviews and the average rating for the overall product and each of its SKUs. It does not include detailed review content or author information, ensuring privacy and reducing data volume for client applications.

Internally, this endpoint cross-references the requested productId with the shopping_products table to verify existence, and then queries the review aggregates for that product. All metrics are derived directly from the shopping_review_rating_aggregates model as defined in the Prisma schema, including product-level and per-SKU review statistics.

No authentication is required for this endpoint, as rating information is public and intended for use across the catalog and product listing pages. Error conditions, such as a missing or invalid productId, return standard not found or validation errors as per platform conventions.

parameters.name: productId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the product whose review aggregates are requested. This must match the id field (UUID) in the shopping_products table.

responseBody.description: Aggregate review and rating statistics for the specified product, including per-SKU details, from shopping_review_rating_aggregates.

operations.name: at

prerequisites.description: Product must be created before its corresponding review aggregate statistics can exist or be queried.

operations.specification: This operation allows admin users to perform advanced searching and filtering over the platform's audit logs, which are recorded in the shopping_audit_logs table. Audit logs capture immutably all security-sensitive, operational, and business events by admin, seller, and customer actors. The search interface supports complex query criteria, including filtering by actor, event type, category, timestamp, and other log fields. The main business purpose is to provide security, compliance, and operational oversight for admins performing investigations, policy audits, and traceability reviews. The operation supports pagination for large result sets and enforces strict access control so only admin actors can view or search audit logs. This endpoint is essential for platform compliance, forensics, and administration. The source table is shopping_audit_logs as defined in the Prisma schema.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve filtered, paginated audit log records for platform security and compliance. Admins only.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered, paginated list of audit log entries from the shopping_audit_logs table, enabling admin users to review platform security, compliance, and business operations events. The operation allows extensive filtering on category, actor (admin, seller, customer), event type, date range, or description text, supporting advanced incident investigations and policy audits.

All audit logs are immutably recorded in shopping_audit_logs, with references to relevant account actors and operational categories. The API supports pagination and sorting to handle large volumes of logs efficiently.

Access to this endpoint is restricted to admin actors. Security measures include authentication, role-based permissions, and audit of log access itself. The endpoint is vital for incident response, compliance reporting, and platform governance. Any attempt to access this API by non-admins is denied, and failed access is logged for security forensics.

requestBody.description: Search criteria for filtering and paginating audit log results, including actor, category, event type, date range, or description keyword.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of audit log summary records matching search criteria, including actor and event details, from shopping_audit_logs.

The audit log table (shopping_audit_logs) contains immutable event records for all critical platform operations, covering admin, seller, and customer actions. Each log entry holds details such as actor references, event type, category, IP address, summaries, and timestamps. The endpoint supports system compliance and regulatory investigation scenarios, allowing platform administrators to perform forensic review and trace security-sensitive business events through a consistent interface. The audit log entry is only accessible to authorized admin users due to the sensitive nature of the contained information.
operations.description:
Fetch a single immutable audit log record by its unique identifier from the shopping_audit_logs table. This endpoint is intended for compliance, investigation, and platform administration; access is restricted strictly to users with admin privileges. The returned data includes actor linkage (admin, seller, customer as available), event category and type, summary, timestamp, and any supplementary details. The API ensures that sensitive business operations—such as administrative escalations, privilege changes, critical order interventions, and platform configuration changes—can be traced in support of regulatory audits and business rule enforcement.

Security is a primary concern as audit logs may contain personally identifiable and sensitive event context. Strong authentication and role checks are enforced, and all accesses are tracked for meta-audit purposes. Application layer rate limiting is advised to prevent data scraping. If the specified audit log ID does not exist, a proper not found error is returned, with no leakage of sensitive context. Referenced linked entities must be internally resolved as required for full traceability.

Returned data structure follows the IShoppingAuditLog schema and contains all fields available in the shopping_audit_logs table, including actor references and descriptive fields.
operations.summary: Retrieve one audit log entry (shopping_audit_logs) by its UUID for investigation/admin review.

responseBody.description: Full detail of the selected audit log entry for investigation/support.

operations.specification:
This operation performs a complex, filtered, and paginated search of platform-wide announcements created and managed by administrators. It interacts with the shopping_platform_announcements table, supporting use cases such as admin dashboard display, notifications management, and compliance status checks. The search supports advanced filtering by announcement status, target audience, date ranges, title/content full-text search, and scheduled publish windows. Only admin users are allowed to query all announcements; sellers and customers may only filter for active/visible subsets (enforced in business logic).

Results are returned with pagination, showing relevant metadata and announcement summaries for dashboard, reporting, or scheduling contexts. The response data structure includes all key attributes from the shopping_platform_announcements table and supports localization of titles and bodies where applicable. The endpoint is designed for administrative interfaces, platform maintenance scheduling, and audit reporting on notification compliance.
operations.description:
Query the list of platform announcements by a wide variety of search and filter parameters. Admins may query all announcements, while sellers/customers view only currently visible or targeted announcements. The search supports filters by status (draft, active, expired, scheduled), target audience (all, customers, sellers, admins), publish window periods, and full-text search over title and content. Pagination and sorting options are provided to permit efficient dashboard rendering and compliance auditing.

Security considerations include strict role enforcement to prevent unauthorized data access, especially for non-public or scheduled announcements. Response omits or redacts unpublished/draft content for non-admin actors, and sensitive scheduling information is only fully available to admins. This API is essential for admin portal interfaces, notification analytics, and regulated information reporting flows. Failure or error scenarios include invalid filter combinations, access violations, or exceeding quota/rate limits.

Returned data structure is a paginated summary list using the IPageIShoppingPlatformAnnouncement.ISummary schema, providing all primary fields from the shopping_platform_announcements table.
operations.summary: Advanced search, filtering, and pagination of admin platform announcements (shopping_platform_announcements).

requestBody.description: Search and filter criteria for announcements. Includes possible status, target audience, time windows, keywords, and pagination/sorting options.

responseBody.description: Paginated summary list of announcements matching the search/filter criteria. Each entry contains main identifiers and summary fields.

The operation targets the 'shopping_platform_announcements' table, which stores platform-wide admin-authored announcements including title, content, target audience, publication windows, and status. This API enables read-only retrieval of an announcement's full details for display in admin dashboards or user interfaces.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information for a specific platform announcement (shopping_platform_announcements).
operations.description:
This endpoint provides the complete details for a single platform announcement specified by the unique 'platformAnnouncementId'. It is designed to support admin and user views that display scheduled, active, or historical announcements published by administrators. The response includes all announcement metadata, such as title, body content, audience targeting, publication status, scheduling windows, and the authoring admin's reference. 

Security is enforced so that only authenticated actors with viewing permissions (such as admins or general platform users) may access the announcement details. This operation reads from the 'shopping_platform_announcements' Prisma table and reflects any changes to announcement content or status in real time, ensuring up-to-date information is always served.

Error handling covers scenarios where the specified announcement does not exist, is deleted, or the caller lacks permission to view the content. This endpoint is typically used in any context requiring display or audit of admin-issued platform announcements.

responseBody.description: The announcement details, metadata, targeting, status, and scheduling information for the specified platform announcement.

The data is written to the 'shopping_platform_announcements' table, which captures all required and optional fields for an announcement. Admin users use this endpoint to author and schedule communication to target audiences including customers, sellers, or all actors. The specification requires validation of required fields such as title, body, target audience, publication windows, and ensures audit traceability of the author admin. Post-creation, the announcement can be managed (edited, published, expired) through other admin APIs or platform workflows.
operations.summary: Create a new platform announcement (shopping_platform_announcements).
operations.description:
This endpoint allows an admin to create a new platform announcement, specifying key details like title, content, target audience, publication window (start/end), and current status. It populates the 'shopping_platform_announcements' Prisma table, supporting platform-wide communication, legal notices, or operational updates as required by the business.

Security policies restrict this operation to admin actors only, ensuring that only authorized personnel can publish announcements. Upon successful creation, the API response includes a full record of the announcement, including administrative metadata for traceability.

The request body must match the IShoppingPlatformAnnouncement.ICreate type and pass validation for all required fields (title, body, audience, scheduling, status). Improper input, insufficient permissions, or scheduling conflicts result in clear error messages and no announcement is created. This endpoint is most commonly used in the admin dashboard for global communication and compliance updates.

requestBody.description: Creation details for the new platform announcement including title, content, target, scheduling, and status.

responseBody.description: Full record of the newly created platform announcement, including metadata, status, and audit fields.

It is directly associated with the platform announcement management requirements for administrators. The endpoint utilizes the 'platformAnnouncementId' to identify the target record for editing or modification. It allows updating fields such as title, body, target audience, publication windows, and status, aligning with the business rules that only admins can edit announcements. This operation is essential for compliance communication, platform notification updates, and audit traceability.
operations.summary: Update a specific platform announcement by ID in the shopping_platform_announcements table.

This API endpoint enables an admin to update the content, status, or metadata of a specific platform announcement identified by its unique platformAnnouncementId. The operation is designed for administrative purposes, allowing platform admins to revise announcement details such as the title, body, publication status, visibility window (start/end times), or target audience based on platform needs.

Administrative privileges are strictly enforced for this operation, ensuring that only authorized users (admins) can perform modifications. The endpoint interacts directly with the shopping_platform_announcements table, ensuring all edits are tracked via audit logs for compliance reasons. Changes made via this endpoint are immediately reflected in user-facing announcement listings, affecting what is visible to users or system actors.

Validation rules include ensuring that all required fields are present, the new title does not duplicate any existing active announcement, date/time logic for the publish window is coherent, and the status field follows accepted enum values (draft, scheduled, active, expired, or hidden). Related endpoints for announcement creation or removal should be referenced for full announcement lifecycle management. Error handling addresses cases such as attempting to update a non-existent ID or lacking sufficient privileges.
