IShoppingAdminSuspension.description:
Represents a platform-wide suspension action imposed by an administrator on another admin, seller, or customer. This entity captures all relevant details required for full audit, compliance, and business logic, including the actor that enacted the suspension, the affected entity (admin, seller, or customer), type and reason for suspension, the effective suspension period, and business decision status. The table supports both temporary and permanent suspensions, with references to decision history and appeals via related tables. Soft deletion is used for audit retention.

This schema is fundamental for audit trails and compliance with platform business rules, especially for dispute resolution, actor access restriction, and regulatory reporting. The type structure strictly mirrors the underlying shopping_admin_suspensions table as defined in the Prisma schema. All references to actor IDs must point to valid UUIDs for the corresponding admin, seller, or customer as appropriate.

Key relations: Each suspension is created by an admin (via admin_id), affects an actor (one of admin/seller/customer), records suspension type (temporary/permanent/pending_appeal), reason, suspension times, status, and audit information. The entity links to appeals and decision history for full lifecycle traceability.

id.description: Primary key for the suspension record. This is a unique UUID. Assigned server-side and always present in read operations.

admin_id.description: UUID of the admin who performed the suspension. This is a reference to shopping_admins.id. Required for all audit and traceability features.

suspended_admin_id.description: UUID of the affected admin actor (if the suspension is on an admin). This is a reference to shopping_admins.id; null otherwise.

suspended_seller_id.description: UUID of the affected seller actor (if the suspension is on a seller). This is a reference to shopping_sellers.id; null otherwise.

suspended_customer_id.description: UUID of the affected customer actor (if the suspension is on a customer). Reference to shopping_customers.id; null otherwise.

suspension_type.description: Suspension classification (temporary, permanent, pending_appeal, etc). Used to drive workflow and business policy. See comments in Prisma for allowed values. Business logic may restrict transitions (e.g., only certain types for certain actors).

reason.description: Detailed business or compliance reason why the suspension was imposed. May reflect policy violation, fraud, etc. This field is always required for compliance traceability.

start_at.description: Timestamp of suspension start (UTC, ISO 8601). For temporary suspensions, this is when suspension takes effect. For permanent suspensions, marks start of the permanent restriction.

end_at.description: End timestamp for temporary suspensions (if applicable). For permanent suspensions, this will be null.

status.description: Current lifecycle status for the suspension (e.g., active, expired, revoked, pending_appeal). See business logic for allowed/valid transitions.

created_at.description: When the suspension record was created (UTC, ISO 8601). Always present for audit, not updateable by clients.

updated_at.description: Last update time of the suspension record. For compliance and audit. Updated whenever changes are made.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp (null if active). Populated if this suspension record was logically removed for audit/compliance. Never physically deleted.

IShoppingAdminSuspension.$comment: This schema is derived from shopping_admin_suspensions as defined in the Prisma schema. All UUIDs must be valid, timestamps are ISO 8601-compliant, and all fields follow the business and audit policies specified in the database model. Only those fields explicitly defined in the Prisma schema are present.

IShoppingAdminSuspension.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new admin suspension record. Used as the request body in POST /shopping/admin/adminSuspensions. Maps to the shopping_admin_suspensions table in the Prisma schema, and contains all information necessary to impose either a temporary or permanent suspension on an actor (admin, seller, or customer) for business, security, or compliance purposes.

The input DTO requires references for both the admin actor creating the suspension and the affected entity (one of admin, seller, or customer). It mandates selection of suspension type, reason, status, and effective suspension times. System compliance rules dictate that at least exactly one among suspended_admin_id, suspended_seller_id, or suspended_customer_id must be provided for each operation. All UUID references must be valid for their respective entities.

Timestamps must be ISO 8601 format (UTC). Business logic (outside schema) will enforce that self-suspension or suspension of the last super admin cannot be performed, and all required audit information is provided. Only fields that exist in the shopping_admin_suspensions table are present.

admin_id.description: UUID of the admin actor enacting the suspension. Reference to shopping_admins.id. Must be provided; server will authenticate actor against this value and audit trail.

suspended_admin_id.description: UUID of the affected admin if suspending an admin actor. Provide only one of suspended_admin_id, suspended_seller_id, or suspended_customer_id (others MUST be null). Reference to shopping_admins.id.

suspended_seller_id.description: UUID of the affected seller if suspending a seller account. Provide only one of suspended_admin_id, suspended_seller_id, or suspended_customer_id (others MUST be null). Reference to shopping_sellers.id.

suspended_customer_id.description: UUID of the affected customer if suspending a customer account. Must be mutually exclusive with the other two actor reference IDs. Reference to shopping_customers.id.

suspension_type.description: Classification of the suspension. Must be one of the valid business suspension types supported by the platform: 'temporary', 'permanent', or 'pending_appeal'. See platform policies for allowed values.

reason.description: Business or compliance reason for suspension. Required for all audit, dispute, and compliance requirements.

start_at.description: Timestamp when the suspension should begin. UTC, ISO 8601. Must be present at creation time.

end_at.description: Timestamp when the suspension will end (nullable). For permanent suspensions, this is null; for temporary suspensions, must be set to valid future time.

status.description: Lifecycle status for the new suspension (e.g., 'active', 'pending', etc). Business logic will enforce allowed statuses (see status enums in Prisma).

IShoppingAdminSuspension.ICreate.$comment: This schema is derived from shopping_admin_suspensions as defined in the Prisma schema. Only use fields defined in the table. All references are UUIDs, timestamps are ISO 8601 (UTC). Only supply one of suspended_admin_id, suspended_seller_id, or suspended_customer_id; others must be null. No phantom fields.

IShoppingAdminSuspension.IUpdate.description: DTO for updating an admin suspension in the shopping mall platform. This type allows authorized admin users to update mutable fields of a suspension, such as status, suspension period (start/end), type, or reason. All fields are optional, supporting partial updates. The DTO supports changing status from 'active' to 'revoked', altering the reason, or adjusting the end date of temporary suspensions. Immutable fields like creation timestamp and affected admin/customer/seller IDs are excluded. All changes are subject to business validation logic. This schema maps directly to the shopping_admin_suspensions Prisma model, referencing property documentation from the original database schema.

suspension_type.description: Type of suspension imposed ('temporary', 'permanent', or 'pending_appeal'). Must coincide with values used in shopping_admin_suspensions.suspension_type. Used to adjust whether a suspension is time-limited or permanent.

reason.description: Detailed business reason for suspension. Explains the rationale to the affected user (policy violation, fraud, etc).

start_at.description: Suspension effective start time in ISO 8601 format (UTC). Used for temporary suspensions, determines when the suspension commences.

end_at.description: End time for temporary suspensions. Null if permanent. Used for scheduling when a time-limited ban expires and account may be unlocked. Provided in ISO-8601 UTC format or set to null for permanent suspensions.

status.description: Current status of the suspension ('active', 'expired', 'revoked', 'pending_appeal', etc.). Used to update the state of the suspension lifecycle, and must match allowed values in shopping_admin_suspensions.status.

affected_entity_id.description: UUID of the affected entity (admin, seller, customer, product, or order). Used to limit query results to violations involving this entity.

IShoppingAppeal.ISummary.description:
Summary view of a formal appeal record for violations, suspensions, or admin actions within the shopping platform. This summary type is used for list/search display and reference context. It includes anchor IDs, all primary actors, business type info, and dates, providing sufficient context to link to the full appeal. All field documentation now mirrors the full entity, but as a strict subset for performance/context.

Required fields: id, status, type, reason, filer_actor_type, filer_actor_id, affected_actor_type, affected_actor_id, decision, decision_reason, created_at, updated_at, decision_at, appeal_of_policy_violation_id, appeal_of_suspension_id.
Related domain tables: shopping_appeals, shopping_admin_suspensions, shopping_policy_violations.

id.description: Unique appeal identifier for this summary record.

status.description: Current lifecycle status (e.g., 'filed', 'under_review', 'approved', 'rejected', 'closed', 'escalated').

reason.description: Business reason and submitted evidence or comments for the appeal (user/admin input).

affected_actor_type.description: The type of the affected actor for this appeal, if applicable: 'customer', 'seller', 'admin'.

affected_actor_id.description: UUID of the affected/targeted actor if applicable.

decision_reason.description: Detailed human-readable rationale for the decision rendered (may be null when no decision present).

created_at.description: Timestamp when the appeal was initially submitted.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this appeal was last updated.

decision_at.description: Timestamp when appeal was resolved (may be null if not decided yet).

appeal_of_policy_violation_id.description: Reference to the violation this appeal is for; may be null if not a violation appeal.

appeal_of_suspension_id.description: Reference to the related admin/seller/customer suspension if this is a suspension appeal. Nullable.

IShoppingPolicyViolation.ISummary.description:
A summary representation of a business policy violation detected on the shopping platform. Each instance summarizes a reported violation, including the violated policy, violation type, code, status, and related decision. This variant is designed for high-performance list, report, or dashboard use, and excludes full audit trails or downward recursion—use the full detail entity for full relational depth. Intended for admin, compliance, and operational dashboards to review platform compliance and enforce policy. See also related domain tables: shopping_policy_violations, shopping_business_policies. Do not include full nested actor/product/order objects; use only relevant summary/IDs. For status/decision fields, refer to the business logic documentation for the canonical set of values allowed by shopping_status_enums or admin/compliance requirements.

Key points:
- Each violation is uniquely identified and references an explicit policy.
- All lifecycle and compliance enforcement for violations is documented in the business requirements.
- This type is used for listing, filtering, and embedding policy violations in higher-level moderation flows, not for mutation or full detail inspection.

id.description: Unique identifier of this policy violation report. Automatically generated per violation. Corresponds to the primary key in the shopping_policy_violations database table.

policy_id.description: ID of the referenced business policy definition (shopping_business_policies.id) to which this violation pertains. Used to understand which business rule was broken or monitored; relates to compliance policy configuration.

violation_type.description: The violation category for this record. Common categories include 'abuse', 'fraud', 'policy_breach', 'duplicate_account', etc. This is a business-defined string constant that classifies the nature of the violation, usually referencing platform-wide or domain-specific status enums.

violation_code.description: Machine-readable code for the specific violation as defined in the related policy schema (shopping_policy_violations.violation_code). Used for programmatic enforcement, analytics, and cross-system reporting. Examples: 'SELLER_KYC_MISSING', 'REPEATED_CANCEL', etc.

status.description: Current business lifecycle status of the violation. Typical values include 'open', 'under_review', 'resolved', 'escalated', 'invalid', or 'canceled'. Actual values are managed by shopping_status_enums under the 'policy_violation' domain and may be extended per compliance and regulatory requirements. Check business documentation or enum registry for the latest supported set.

oneOf.description: Resolution or adjudication result (such as 'upheld', 'dismissed', 'pending', 'overturned', if applicable). Decision values are subject to admin, compliance, and business rules; refer to platform policy documentation for official options.

decision.description: Resolution/adjudication result—if the violation case has been reviewed and a business/administrative/court decision issued (see regulatory workflows). May be null if pending or in process.

oneOf.description: Optional human-readable summary or extended business context for this violation. Use to clarify why violation is considered open, resolved, or invalid; can include investigation notes or references to regulatory documents.

description.description: Human-readable summary or context for this violation. Optional, for audit logs, moderation workflow notes, and compliance review comments.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the violation record was created (ISO 8601 format, UTC). Used for audit, reporting, and compliance traceability.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last update to this violation record (ISO 8601 UTC). Indicates when the status/decision/description was last changed.

oneOf.description: Timestamp for resolution/decision (ISO 8601, UTC), if present.

decision_at.description: Timestamp for final decision/resolution on this violation if known. Null if no decision yet made.

policy.description: Summary of the referenced business policy definition (shopping_business_policies). Includes key policy context for the violation, suitable for embedding in list/grid/table views. Does not include full policy detail or downward objects.

IShoppingAdminSuspension.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for administrator-imposed account suspensions. Used to represent temporary or permanent enforcement actions against admin, seller, or customer accounts in response to business rule violations, fraud, abuse, or platform policy enforcement. Designed for fast, high-volume audit, compliance, and dashboard scenarios. Contains essential context for tracking active, expired, revoked, or appealed suspensions, and provides all information needed for operational status review and regulatory compliance.

Key points:
- Records the actor imposing the suspension (admin_id) and the affected entity (suspended_admin_id, suspended_seller_id, or suspended_customer_id), always via UUIDs only.
- Lifecycle and audit fields support tracking from suspension issue to expiry, revocation, or permanent compliance archive.
- Enum-like fields ('suspension_type', 'status') should have possible values enumerated in business or compliance requirements; platform business logic MAY enforce canonical allowed values such as 'temporary', 'permanent', 'pending_appeal' for suspension_type, and 'active', 'expired', 'revoked', 'pending_appeal' for status.
- The reason is always required for audit and compliance justification; describes the business or regulatory context that prompted the enforcement action.
- Soft-deleted records (deleted_at non-null) remain in the system for audit trails and compliance as specified in retention and platform documentation.
- This ISummary variant does not include related appeals or histories; use the full detail entity for those relationships.

id.description: Primary key for the suspension record (shopping_admin_suspensions.id). Unique for each enforcement event.

admin_id.description: UUID of the admin who imposed this suspension. Automatically set by the backend and used for audit and accountability tracking.

suspended_admin_id.description: UUID of the admin account affected by this suspension, if this was imposed on another admin account. Null if not relevant to this suspension case (targeting a seller or customer instead).

suspended_seller_id.description: UUID of the seller account affected by this suspension, if relevant to the case. Null if targeting admin or customer.

suspended_customer_id.description: UUID of the customer account affected by this suspension, if this was a customer enforcement case. Null if targeting admin or seller.

suspension_type.description: Type of the suspension: typically one of 'temporary', 'permanent', or 'pending_appeal'. Determines the intended business duration and severity. Must follow platform and regulatory policy for allowed values, transition, and expiration rules. May be extended in the future per compliance or business rules.

reason.description: Detailed business or compliance rationale for the suspension. Required for all account enforcements and referenced in appeals and compliance reports. Should summarize policy/process violation prompting the enforcement and any investigation process. May include external reference/case code for regulatory compliance.

start_at.description: Start of suspension enforcement window (ISO 8601 UTC). For permanent suspensions, this records the initiation date of perpetual restriction; for temporary suspensions, determines the start of enforced status.

end_at.description: End date/time for temporary suspensions (ISO 8601 UTC). Null for permanent suspensions; populated only for cases with defined expiration/relief window.

status.description: Current status of the suspension record: typically one of 'active', 'expired', 'revoked', or 'pending_appeal'. Determines whether the enforcement is currently applied, has ended (naturally or by admin override), or is under review. Canonical value set is governed by platform business rules and can be extended for regulatory/appeal scenarios.

created_at.description: Suspension record creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC); used for audit, compliance, and reporting. Always present.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the last update to this suspension record (ISO 8601 UTC). Used for audit, compliance, and historical tracking. Updated whenever the record's attributes change.

deleted_at.description: Soft-delete marker for the suspension record (ISO 8601 UTC, nullable). Populated if the record is logically hidden from standard views but retained for regulatory/statutory compliance. Always present for all soft-deleted items.

status.description:
Current lifecycle status of the appeal (e.g., 'filed', 'under_review', 'approved', 'rejected', 'closed', 'escalated').
See business rules for allowed transitions. Should match enum/domain constraint in shopping_appeals.status column.

decision.description: Decision/result of the appeal process if known after update (e.g., 'upheld', 'overturned'). Nullable if not yet decided. Should match application-allowed values.

decision_at.description: Timestamp of appeal decision (ISO 8601, UTC). Only set if decision result is provided and status transitions to a terminal/closed state.

reason.description: Detailed business reason, supporting context, or justification for the appeal update or decision. Required if updating to a terminal or rejected state.

IShoppingAppeal.IUpdate.description: Update DTO for shopping mall appeals records, used by admin to change status, decision, and/or rationale in audit-compliant fashion. Excludes ID/path which is provided in route. Field edit permissions and enum rules enforced by business logic. Maps 1:1 to mutable fields in shopping_appeals.

policy_name.description: Policy name (partial or exact match) to search/filter. Case-insensitive, mapped from shopping_business_policies.policy_name.

scope.description: Scope substring filter (e.g., 'orders', 'global', etc). Matches shopping_business_policies.scope.

status.description: Filter by active/inactive ('active','inactive'), mapped against shopping_business_policies.active boolean. 'active' returns active=true policies, 'inactive' returns active=false.

q.description: Generic full-text search term to fuzzy match policy name, description, and value fields.

page.description: Page number for pagination, 1-based index.

limit.description: Maximum number of records per page. Default and maximum may be set by platform config.

oneOf.description: Sort order (ascending or descending). Only values allowed: 'asc' or 'desc'.
Sort order (ascending or descending). Only values allowed: 'asc' or 'desc'.

order_direction.description: Sort order (ascending or descending). Only values allowed: 'asc' or 'desc'.

IShoppingBusinessPolicy.IRequest.description: Request DTO for searching and filtering business policies (shopping_business_policies). Supports complex query, pagination, ordering, and fuzzy text search on key columns.

id.description: Primary Key. This field uniquely identifies the business policy record within the platform for audit and governance purposes. Matches the `id` column in Prisma.

policy_name.description: Unique name for the business policy (e.g., 'order_return_window', 'seller_onboarding_requirement'). Used for outward reference and enforcement in other domains. This must be unique in combination with `scope`, per Prisma's @@unique([policy_name, scope]) constraint.

scope.description: Scope or domain where this policy applies (e.g., 'global', 'orders', 'sellers'). This field controls which functional domain(s) the business rule affects and must be specified upon creation.

value.description: Value, threshold, or state for the policy (e.g., '30', 'approved'). May represent numbers, enums, or complex values as strings. This is the value that the backend enforcement and frontends should use when interpreting the policy rule.

description.description: Detailed description of the business purpose and operational impact of this policy, used for administrative review, audit, and compliance purposes.

active.description: Whether this business policy is currently in force. Controls runtime enforcement and API visibility. Only active policies should be used for rules enforcement by application code.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the business policy record was created in the system. Used for audit and history. Read-only; managed by the backend.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the business policy was last updated. Managed automatically by backend. Used for audit/compliance.

deleted_at.description: Soft delete timestamp, if the policy is archived or replaced. Null if active. Used for audit/compliance. This field is read-only and not present in create/update DTOs.

IShoppingBusinessPolicy.description:
Business policy configuration object representing a single governing rule for the shopping mall platform. Each policy is uniquely named and scoped, contains a value (typically a threshold or setting), and includes documentation for compliance. This object is directly mapped to the shopping_business_policies table in the Prisma schema, supporting audit, governance, and API enforcement of core business logic.

Typical examples include rules such as return windows, seller onboarding requirements, commission rates, or order minimums. Used by platform administrators, seller integrations, and automated backend logic for rule enforcement. Soft deletes and changes are tracked with audit timestamps and fields. The schema enforces that only active (non-deleted) policies are returned via the main API endpoints. Sensitive or regulatory fields should be monitored according to business compliance rules.

policy_name.description: Unique name for the business policy (e.g., 'order_return_window', 'seller_onboarding_requirement'). Required. This must be unique per (policy_name, scope) in the database, per Prisma's @@unique([policy_name, scope]) constraint.

scope.description: Scope or domain where this policy applies (e.g., 'global', 'orders', 'sellers'). Required. Must match a valid domain where the rule applies. Controlled by business logic and verified on creation.

value.description: Value, limit, or state that the business policy represents (e.g., '30', 'approved', 'active'). Required. Actual value type is generally a string, but may represent numbers, enums, or JSON-serializable values for code interpretation.

description.description: Required. Human-readable explanation of policy purpose, operational impact, and context. Used by admins for audit/review/compliance and by developers for rule documentation.

active.description: Required. Controls whether the business policy is immediately active upon creation. This affects enforcement in backend logic. Setting to false allows adding dormant or not-yet-in-force policies.

IShoppingBusinessPolicy.ICreate.description:
DTO used for creation of a new business policy configuration in the shopping mall platform. This object is directly mapped to the shopping_business_policies table in Prisma. Required by the POST /shopping/admin/businessPolicies endpoint (admin privilege only).

All fields reflect core business rule attributes, and creating policies requires unique (policy_name, scope) per backend validation. Policy descriptions should be comprehensive to ensure future maintainability and compliance review. The created policy record is immediately available for enforcement by backend business logic. Audit fields (id, created_at, updated_at, deleted_at) are system-generated and omitted from create DTO.

scope.description: Scope or domain where this policy applies. For example, 'global', 'orders', 'sellers'. Editable via update.

value.description: Value or threshold for the policy (e.g., number for days, or text like 'approved').

description.description: Detail description of the business purpose and operational impact of this policy.

active.description: Whether this policy is currently active and enforced system-wide.

IShoppingBusinessPolicy.IUpdate.description:
Update parameters for a business policy entry in the shopping_business_policies table. Only updatable fields are present. At least one field must be supplied in the update request.

This schema is mapped to the shopping_business_policies table, which manages rules such as order return window, seller onboarding requirement, etc. The scope determines where the policy applies, value sets the threshold/state, description explains the business purpose, and active controls enforcement. This DTO is only for admin use and never accepts policy_name (which must come from the path, NOT duplicated in body).

scope.description: Scope/domain to filter constraints (e.g., 'global', 'carts', 'checkout', 'products'). Optional when filtering business constraints.

constraint_name.description: Constraint name (e.g., 'max_orders_per_user_day', 'sku_max_per_product'). Optional. Filters by unique business logic constraint.

active.description: Filter by constraint status. If present, only include constraints currently active/inactive.

page.description: Which result page to retrieve (for pagination). Optional.

limit.description: Maximum number of results per page (default, max system constraints apply). Optional.

sort.description: Order by field (e.g., 'created_at', 'constraint_name'). Optional. Controls result ordering.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Optional.
Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Optional.

order.description: Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending. Optional.

IShoppingBusinessConstraint.IRequest.description:
Search and filter criteria for retrieving business constraints from the shopping_business_constraints table.

Supports advanced platform audit: filter by domain scope, constraint_name, status/activity, and provides paging/sorting for large datasets. All fields are optional, but at least one filter is recommended for efficient queries.

IShoppingBusinessConstraint.description:
Business constraint entity representing a global or subsystem-level quantitative limit, restriction, or operational boundary enforced by the shopping platform. This model is defined in the Prisma schema as 'shopping_business_constraints'.

Each business constraint specifies an enforced operational rule (such as maximum orders per customer per day, SKU limits, rate limits, or transaction amount ceilings), and contains structural and contextual information for compliance, platform auditing, and configuration management. Every constraint features a unique global name (constraint_name), a scope/domain of effect (scope), machine-interpretable and human-readable values, associated units, description, current activation state, and audit timestamps for both business operations and technical traceability.

Business constraints are fully auditable: changes or deactivation are typically logged to maintain trace and compliance with business logic. Admins use this record for both operational troubleshooting and for documentation/communication purposes. The information is critical for developers, operators, auditors, and system configurators managing the dynamically changing limitations applied to the shopping ecosystem.

id.description: Primary key for the business constraint record. Universally unique. Directly maps to 'id' field in the shopping_business_constraints table.

constraint_name.description: Unique name of the business constraint, such as 'max_orders_per_user_day', 'sku_max_per_product', or 'guest_cart_expiry_days'. Used for API referencing and enforcement logic. Globally unique within the table. Corresponds to 'constraint_name' column in Prisma.

scope.description: Domain, subsystem, or process to which this constraint applies (e.g., 'global', 'cart', 'checkout', 'products', 'orders'). Commonly referenced in API endpoints and business validation routines. Directly maps to 'scope' column in Prisma.

limit_value.description: The quantitative/business value for this operational constraint (e.g., '10' for max cart quantity; '7' for max days to refund). Always stored as a string in the schema, but business logic interprets it as integer, decimal, or special code as appropriate. Mirrors 'limit_value' column in Prisma.

unit.description: Unit for the constraint value (e.g., 'count', 'seconds', 'amount', 'days'). Contextualizes the value for business users and developers alike. From 'unit' Prisma column.

description.description: Full textual description of the constraint's business purpose, how and where it's enforced, rationale, and potential operational impact. Used for documentation, admin dashboards, and API help. Direct from 'description' in Prisma.

active.description: Whether this constraint is currently active and enforced platform-wide. Toggled by admins as the business context changes. Mirrors 'active' flag in the schema.

created_at.description: Timestamp of record creation (audit field). ISO 8601 date-time string, matches the 'created_at' field in shopping_business_constraints.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the most recent record update or value/unit change (audit field). ISO 8601 date-time format, corresponds to 'updated_at'.

deleted_at.description: Indicates soft deletion of the constraint; if non-null, constraint is considered deleted but retained for audit/compliance. Null if active. Corresponds to 'deleted_at' in Prisma, can be null if not deleted.

IShoppingBusinessConstraint.ICreate.description:
DTO schema for creating a new business constraint record in the shopping platform (shopping_business_constraints table). Used exclusively in administrative and configuration management API endpoints.

This structure ensures all required fields for new constraint creation are supplied, including the unique constraint name, the affected domain/scope, quantitative value, unit of measure, descriptive context, and activation state. Upon successful creation, the full constraint record will reflect these properties. All provided fields directly map to business logic enforcement and documentation requirements.

constraint_name.description: Globally unique business constraint name (e.g., 'max_orders_per_user_day'). Required for reference, documentation, and enforcement. Maps to 'constraint_name' in Prisma.

scope.description: Scope or subsystem affected by this constraint (e.g., 'cart', 'products', 'checkout'). Required for correct application of the rule. Mirrors 'scope' column in DB.

limit_value.description: Value of the constraint as a string (to be interpreted as integer, decimal, or code by consuming modules). Examples: '10', '72', '999'. Corresponds to 'limit_value' field in schema.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the constraint: 'count', 'days', 'seconds', 'amount', etc. Ensures accurate business logic interpretation. From 'unit' column.

description.description: Detailed description of what this constraint enforces, its rationale, and business impact. Required field for documentation, dashboards, and compliance. Maps to 'description' in Prisma.

active.description: Initial activation status for this constraint (true to immediately enforce, false to store as draft/inactive). Required field, direct from 'active' Prisma column.

constraint_name.description: Unique business constraint name to identify the constraint entry. Must match the record to be updated (case-sensitive, global uniqueness). Referenced as 'constraintName' path parameter in API operations.

scope.description: Operational domain/context of the constraint (e.g., 'global', 'carts', 'checkout', 'products'). Determines logical grouping and enforcement boundary for the constraint. Must match one of the allowed scopes in the platform.

limit_value.description: Constraint value to enforce. Typically a string-encoded integer or decimal (business logic will cast as appropriate). Required for enforcement; may be empty for disabled constraints.

unit.description: Unit of measure for the constraint (e.g., 'count', 'seconds', 'amount'). Used for business validation and documentation. Free-form string, but must match valid options per the business policy.

description.description: Detailed human-readable explanation of what this constraint limits or enforces (e.g., 'Maximum cart items allowed per user per order.'). Used for UI and admin documentation. Optional.

active.description: Indicates whether the business constraint is currently enforced (true) or suspended (false). Affects enforcement at backend business logic and API layers.

IShoppingBusinessConstraint.IUpdate.description: Update payload for an existing business constraint in the shopping_business_constraints table. Corresponds to platform administrative update operations. All properties except `description` are required; changing `constraint_name` will update the constraint's identifier. Does not allow creation—only update.

flagName.description: Filter by partial or full feature flag name. If omitted, matches all names.

scope.description: Filter by logical domain/context where the flag applies (e.g., 'global', 'orders', 'checkout'). If omitted, matches all scopes.

enabled.description: Filter: true = only enabled feature flags, false = only disabled, omit to include both.

page.description: Results page number, starting at 1. Default: 1.

limit.description: Results per page. Bound by business maximum (default: 20, max: 100).

oneOf.description: Sort key for flag records. Allowed values: 'flag_name', 'scope', 'enabled', 'rollout', 'created_at'.
Sort key for flag records. Allowed values: 'flag_name', 'scope', 'enabled', 'rollout', 'created_at'.
Sort key for flag records. Allowed values: 'flag_name', 'scope', 'enabled', 'rollout', 'created_at'.
Sort key for flag records. Allowed values: 'flag_name', 'scope', 'enabled', 'rollout', 'created_at'.
Sort key for flag records. Allowed values: 'flag_name', 'scope', 'enabled', 'rollout', 'created_at'.

sortBy.description: Sort key for flag records. Allowed values: 'flag_name', 'scope', 'enabled', 'rollout', 'created_at'.

oneOf.description: Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Default: 'asc'.
Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Default: 'asc'.

order.description: Sort order: ascending (asc) or descending (desc). Default: 'asc'.

IShoppingFeatureFlag.IRequest.description: Request filter, search, and pagination parameters for feature flag search APIs. Used by platform admin feature flag search endpoint. All fields are optional and may be omitted to return all records.

id.description: Unique identifier for this feature flag record, as defined in the shopping_feature_flags Prisma table. Used internally for API reference and updates.

flag_name.description: Globally unique code (business code) identifying this feature flag for lookup and toggle control. Maps to flag_name in the Prisma schema and is used for runtime gating, dashboard filtering, and API path parameter matching.

scope.description: The business context or subsystem where this feature flag applies (e.g., 'global', 'orders', 'checkout', 'frontend'). Used for targeting feature toggles to specific domains or actors. See scope field in Prisma.

enabled.description: Indicates whether this feature is currently enabled (true) or disabled (false) for the specified scope. Used for live toggling, rollout, and experimentation. Maps to the enabled boolean field in the Prisma model.

rollout.description: Percentage (0–100) of users/traffic to enable this feature flag for gradual rollout (A/B testing or staged deployment). Null/omitted if not using gradual enablement. Corresponds to the rollout field, optional in the schema.

description.description: Human-readable, business-provided documentation for this feature flag's purpose, effect, and usage policy. Required for admin panel and developer reference.

created_at.description: Timestamp of feature flag record creation as per Prisma's created_at column (UTC, ISO 8601).

updated_at.description: Timestamp of last modification for this flag configuration, from the Prisma schema's updated_at field (UTC, ISO 8601).

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion timestamp for this flag, as per the Prisma schema's deleted_at field. Null if not deleted.

IShoppingFeatureFlag.description: Feature flag configuration entity for runtime gating, staged rollout, and admin toggling of platform capabilities. Each feature flag is represented by a unique flag_name (business code), a scope (context/domain), and an enabled Boolean (on/off). Optionally, rollout (percentage) dictates staged release. Follows the shopping_feature_flags Prisma schema definitions. Used by the admin panel, delivery automation, and runtime business logic systems. Excludes secrets, tokens, or implementation details. All fields except rollout and deleted_at are mandatory as per schema and operational compliance. Documented for integration with continuous deployment and A/B experimentation subsystems.

flag_name.description: Unique business code for this feature flag (case-sensitive, globally unique in the system). Maps to flag_name in the Prisma schema. Required for creation and future reference.

scope.description: Subsystem or domain for this flag (e.g., 'global', 'orders', 'checkout', 'frontend'), as in the scope field of the Prisma schema. Required for flag targeting.

enabled.description: Initial enabled/disabled state for this feature flag. Must be provided at creation time. Maps to enabled Boolean in the schema.

rollout.description: Percentage (0–100) for gradual rollout/A-B testing. Optional for basic toggles; set null or omit if unused. Follows rollout Float? in Prisma.

description.description: Human-readable documentation for the flag's purpose and impact. Required in the schema. Used by admins and developers: maps to description in Prisma.

IShoppingFeatureFlag.ICreate.description: Feature flag creation DTO for adding new toggles to the shopping_feature_flags table. Used exclusively by admin panel/ops APIs, validated for code uniqueness and adherence to the Prisma schema. Requires flag_name, scope, enabled state, and business description at time of creation. Optional rollout field enables gradual rollout/experimentation. Does not accept id, created_at, updated_at, or deleted_at fields; these are system-generated. Input subjected to all operational and compliance validations. Used for continuous deployment control, runtime experimentation, and dashboard-based toggle management.

enabled.description: Indicates whether the feature flag is active/enabled. This maps directly to the enabled field of the shopping_feature_flags table. Only a platform administrator can toggle this value. It controls whether the associated feature or experiment is available to platform users.

rollout.description: Optional percentage (from 0.0 to 100.0) representing the rollout value for the feature flag for staged A/B experiments, partial enablement, or gradual release. Maps to the rollout field in the shopping_feature_flags table. May be null if full enablement or not using a percentage strategy.

scope.description: Business/application context for this feature flag, e.g., 'global', 'orders', 'checkout'. This maps to the scope column in the shopping_feature_flags table and is used to control or target the enabled feature domain.

description.description: Human-readable explanation of the feature flag's purpose, usage conditions, and operational/business context. Maps to the description column in shopping_feature_flags. Required for compliance and audit.

IShoppingFeatureFlag.IUpdate.description: DTO for updating a feature flag's configuration. Used in PUT /shopping/admin/featureFlags/{flagName}. Updates the enabled state, rollout percentage, scope, and business description of the feature controlled by the flag. Maps directly to the shopping_feature_flags schema for all fields except for the flag name, which is provided in the endpoint path. Enforces business logic: only platform admins may update this configuration.

id.description: Unique platform-wide identifier for the configuration entry. Maps to the id column in shopping_system_configurations.

config_key.description: The unique system configuration key (e.g., 'core.smtp_server'), used for logical lookup and business logic. Maps to config_key, unique within the shopping_system_configurations table.

config_value.description: The string value assigned to this configuration key. Maps to config_value. Serialized as plain text or JSON, depending on the setting.

description.description: Full documentation of what this configuration entry controls. Maps to the description column in shopping_system_configurations.

created_at.description: UTC creation timestamp of the configuration entry. Maps to the created_at column in shopping_system_configurations.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp of last modification to this configuration entry. Maps to the updated_at column.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion timestamp if the configuration entry is archived or removed. Null if active. Maps to the deleted_at column in shopping_system_configurations.

IShoppingSystemConfiguration.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for a system-wide configuration setting in the shopping mall platform. Represents a key/value pair for global platform configuration with audit and documentation fields. Maps directly to shopping_system_configurations schema. Used for system initialization, runtime configuration lookups, and audit compliance.

id.description: Unique identifier for the business setting. Maps to the id field in shopping_business_settings.

setting_key.description: Business setting key (e.g., 'currency', 'country', 'tax_region'). Maps to the setting_key field in shopping_business_settings.

setting_value.description: Arbitrary string data for the setting value (could serialize as JSON for compound). Maps to the setting_value field in shopping_business_settings.

oneOf.description: Description of this setting. Maps to the description field in shopping_business_settings.

description.description: Description of this setting. Maps to the description field in shopping_business_settings.

created_at.description: Row creation timestamp. Maps to the created_at field in shopping_business_settings.

updated_at.description: Row last update timestamp. Maps to the updated_at field in shopping_business_settings.

IShoppingBusinessSetting.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for system-wide business settings. This type provides a concise but complete representation of each setting, reflecting the unique key-value configuration used for operational and regulatory management in the shopping mall platform. Each record is drawn from the shopping_business_settings table in the database and includes both human-readable and machine-oriented details. Used by admin/config interfaces, auditing, and policy enforcement.

The fields here cover essential metadata: a unique identifier, type key, value, and bookkeeping timestamps, as defined in shopping_business_settings model. The optional description field offers extra context for administrators.

id.description: Unique identifier for the status enum (primary key in shopping_status_enums).

enum_domain.description: Domain/entity scope for this status enum, such as 'order', 'review', or 'payment'.

status_code.description: Exact status code (e.g., 'pending', 'paid', 'failed'), case-insensitive, used for enum lookup and enforcement.

display_label.description: Human-readable label to display for this status in UIs.

sort_order.description: Sort ordering among status codes for deterministic dropdown/reporting.

is_active.description: Whether this status code is currently in active use (business toggle).

oneOf.description: Comment or extended description for this enum value.

description.description: Comment or extended description for this enum value.

created_at.description: Time when the enum was created, from created_at in shopping_status_enums.

updated_at.description: When this row was last updated, from updated_at in shopping_status_enums.

IShoppingStatusEnum.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a platform-wide status enum. This type represents operational status codes (e.g., for orders, reviews, payments) as defined in the shopping_status_enums table. It allows business logic and UI components to reference dynamic, administrator-configurable statuses rather than hardcoded values.

Fields correspond directly to the database model: a unique identifier, domain/type, code/value, UI label, ordering, active flag, and optional documentation field. Timestamps provide audit trail. Used by system configuration pages, validation logic, and reporting layers.

IShoppingCategoryTree.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for Shopping Category Tree. Represents a top-level taxonomy or category structure for organizing the product catalog. Used to provide lightweight information necessary for list views and reference context in related resources. Follows summary type rules: includes only essential, business-critical context fields, excludes downward HAS-MANY relations (e.g., does not include full category lists), and provides ONLY upward reference information or primary display fields. Each category tree is uniquely identified by a code and consists of a name and optional description for business context. This type is suitable for selection lists, minimal popovers, and foreign key references in APIs that require a category tree context. \n\nMaps directly to the shopping_category_trees Prisma model. All fields are present in the database schema. Do not include category arrays or children in summary types.

id.description: Unique identifier for the category tree, as assigned in the shopping_category_trees.id field.

tree_code.description: Unique business code for the category tree, identifying the taxonomy (e.g., 'main', 'brand'). Sourced from shopping_category_trees.tree_code. Used for API endpoints and global referencing. Always lowercase and unique.

tree_name.description: Display name for the category tree as shown to business users and admins. Sourced from shopping_category_trees.tree_name.

description.description: Optional detailed explanation or business context for this category tree (from shopping_category_trees.description). May be null if no description provided.

IShoppingCustomerSession.description: Represents a customer login/authentication session, recording connection context for audit, security, and compliance. Linked to shopping_customer_sessions table in the Actors namespace. Includes session start, end, IP, and context URLs. Used to display customer account sessions in security dashboards, session management APIs, and admin reviews. Contains no authentication secrets or tokens.

id.description: Primary key for the customer session. Sourced from shopping_customer_sessions.id.

shopping_customer_id.description: Foreign key to the owning shopping_customers.id. Indicates which customer is associated with this session.

ip.description: IP address at which the session originated. Used for audit, fraud detection, or device tracking. Sourced from shopping_customer_sessions.ip.

href.description: Connection URL at the time the session was started (e.g., landing page or login endpoint). Sourced from shopping_customer_sessions.href.

referrer.description: The referrer (prior URL/page) provided at session initialization. Used for audit, tracking unusual login flows, or regulatory reporting. From shopping_customer_sessions.referrer.

created_at.description: Session creation timestamp (login time). Sourced from shopping_customer_sessions.created_at.

expired_at.description: If set, when this session ended or was revoked. If null, session is currently active/open. From shopping_customer_sessions.expired_at.

IShoppingSellerSession.description:
Represents an authenticated session for a seller, including connection metadata. Used for session introspection, concurrent device management, and audit logging. Does not contain authentication material; only connection context fields and timestamps. All fields are present in shopping_seller_sessions table.

This type is useful for returning currently logged-in session details for seller accounts, viewing session history, and for admin session management. Does NOT include password or sensitive credential data.

id.description: Unique identifier for the session (UUID). Sourced from shopping_seller_sessions.id.

shopping_seller_id.description: Reference to the associated seller. Sourced from shopping_seller_sessions.shopping_seller_id.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was established. Sourced from shopping_seller_sessions.ip.

href.description: Connection URL or page where the session was initiated. Sourced from shopping_seller_sessions.href.

referrer.description: HTTP referrer or previous page causing session initiation. Sourced from shopping_seller_sessions.referrer.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this session was created. Sourced from shopping_seller_sessions.created_at.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when the session ended or was revoked. Null if session is still open. Sourced from shopping_seller_sessions.expired_at.

IShoppingAdmin.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a system administrator for the shopping mall platform. Used for embedding lightweight administrator context within other business entities—such as audit logs, administrative actions, or moderation events—when only non-sensitive fields are required. Designed for high-performance reference scenarios throughout the backend system, this summary includes only those attributes that are safe for platform-wide display and cannot be used as authentication credentials or tokens.

The schema also establishes the reference pattern for deeper-embedding of admin context objects within related resources and clarifies that only the listed fields are exposed to client applications. All properties provided are consistent with the shopping_admins table; any expansion of admin details occurs only in full admin profile endpoints, not on summary embeds. The summary complies with platform RBAC conventions and adheres to privacy and security standards, providing only essential business context for relationships and actor traceability.

Field Details:
- id: Always provided; UUID primary key for admin actor, used platform-wide in reference contexts and logs, and for foreign key relationships into child systems.
- email: Admin business email address; guaranteed unique; NEVER used directly as a credential or authentication token within this summary, always redacted for non-privileged actors if sensitive policy requires. Used in moderation, admin action notification, and history displays.
- name: Real name of the admin (used for auditing, moderation actions, and actor disambiguation during investigations/log reviews). Can be used for display in admin audits, reports, and dashboard summarization. Masking may apply in high-privacy deployments.
- role: Admin account privilege level; references platform RBAC roles such as 'super', 'support', etc. This determines the admin's scope of authority for auditing, security controls, and dashboard views. Possible values from business role enum—see broader admin policy definitions for allowed values.
- status: Lifecycle state of the admin account, such as 'active', 'suspended', 'pending', or 'locked'. Used for operational control (login eligibility), audit status reporting, and legal compliance. Allowed value set is defined by business platform status code enums. Only visible to privileged actors in some API contexts.

id.description: Administrator unique identifier. Always provided. This is the PK (UUID) of the admin actor in the shopping_admins schema and is the canonical actor reference for audit, log, and relationship tracking system-wide. Used in summary embeddings across AdminOps contexts.

email.description: Administrator business email address. This field is unique within the system, used for notifications and actor identification (not for credentialing). Never exposed for login or token purposes inside ISummary. Use with caution in client-facing UIs; may be redacted in exports per privacy policy.

name.description: Administrator's real (display) name. Used for audit/compliance logging, admin action reporting, and platform moderation trails. This name is visible in privileged audit logs and may be shown to privileged actors (admins, superusers). May be masked in cases of high privacy modes.

role.description: Admin privilege level. Encodes the administrator's business authority and RBAC scope (e.g., 'super', 'support', 'moderator', 'compliance'). Determines authorization scope—see business enum for allowed values. Used for session, action, and audit reporting.

status.description: Lifecycle or operational state of the admin account (e.g., 'active', 'suspended', 'pending', 'locked'). Determines system access privileges and login eligibility. Platform enum defines permitted values. Used for admin dashboard status tracking and incident reports.

IShoppingAdminSession.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for an administrator authentication session in the shopping mall backend. Used in API responses for session index/list and detail endpoints, as well as for embedding authentication session context within audit logs, security analysis, and privileged activity monitoring. Contains only non-sensitive session metadata; does NOT expose session tokens, credential material, or MFA details.

This summary type is optimized for embedding in higher-level admin activity logs, incident reports, and platform security reviews. In scenarios where the summary appears in admin session or audit record lists, the 'shopping_admin_id' is typically replaced by a fully embedded IShoppingAdmin.ISummary object (not plain UUID), following platform summary reference rules for traceability, actor auditability, and incident investigation requirements.

Fields provide context for identifying the owner of each session, the origin IP, connection metadata (href, referrer), lifecycle timestamps (creation, expiration), and are designed to fully support audit reporting and platform compliance. All properties are strictly non-secret and reference-only—no property in ISummary can ever be used for credential validation or session token retrieval.

Detailed property notes:
- id: UUID primary key for the session record, ensuring global uniqueness and anchoring all audit, search, and trace operations.
- shopping_admin_id: In list/detail contexts, this property may be returned either as the admin's UUID (for simple listing) or as an embedded IShoppingAdmin.ISummary for cross-context relationship embedding. When embedding, context objects must resolve to the summary schema, providing full traceability for actor actions and session correlations in admin operations.
- ip: The originating IP address where the session was initiated; used for security audits, abuse detection, and compliance checks. Follows IPv4 (or business system dual-stack) string format. Mask/omit as per policy in export or public dashboards.
- href: Original page or application endpoint where the session login occurred; vital for tracking origin in security reports, incident tracing, and diagnostics. Included as-is from session record.
- referrer: HTTP referrer or logical navigation source present in session startup; provides context for login/journey flows and is used in system-level tracing, fraud, and incident investigations.
- created_at: UTC timestamp of session creation. Used for last login displays, session lifetime analysis, and incident/abuse investigation.
- expired_at: Either null (session open/current), or ISO UTC timestamp denoting when the session was explicitly closed or timed out (for expired and audit history entries). Used for tracking most recent usage, risk assessments, and abandoned session monitoring.

id.description: Unique session record identifier (UUID PK from shopping_admin_sessions). Used as canonical reference in all security, audit, and monitoring reporting.

shopping_admin_id.description: Reference to administrator actor (shopping_admins.id). In some embedding scenarios, this may be replaced by the full IShoppingAdmin.ISummary object for cross-context lookup (see ISummary property composition rules).

ip.description: Originating IP address for this session. Used to trace login context, abuse, or suspicious activity. Collected at session creation and only visible in privileged dashboards (not user-facing APIs). May be masked per privacy/export restrictions.

href.description: Original login URL/context for session entry. Used for diagnostics and context auditing; collected at session creation for full audit trace.

referrer.description: HTTP referrer header or journey source present at session start. Used for login path tracing and fraud investigation.

created_at.description: Timestamp at which session was established. Used for login event correlation, reporting, audit history, and session analytics.

expired_at.description: If session was explicitly closed, this is the UTC ISO timestamp when closure occurred. Null if session is still open/active. Used for security reporting, incident review, and session state tracking.

IShoppingUserEmail.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for a user's email record in the shopping mall system. Represents secondary, unverified, or historical emails for customers or sellers, supporting contact updates, verification workflows, and audit/history. Each summary consists of essential identification, linkage, verification state, and audit fields. Draws from the shopping_user_emails Prisma model. Used in list, embedding, and reference scenarios where only essential details are needed.

id.description: Unique identifier for the email record. Corresponds to shopping_user_emails.id.

oneOf.description: If this email is associated with a customer account, this is the user's unique identifier. Corresponds to shopping_user_emails.shopping_customer_id.

shopping_customer_id.description: User's customer ID or null if it is an email for a seller account.

oneOf.description: If this email is associated with a seller account, this is their unique identifier. Corresponds to shopping_user_emails.shopping_seller_id.

shopping_seller_id.description: Seller account ID or null if not a seller email.

email.description: The secondary, pending, or historical email address. Unique per record. Corresponds to shopping_user_emails.email.

is_verified.description: Flag indicating this email has been verified (true) or is still pending. Maps to shopping_user_emails.is_verified.

is_primary.description: Indicates if this is the current primary email for the user (must also match the associated customer/seller table). Maps to shopping_user_emails.is_primary.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this email entry was created/added. ISO 8601 UTC. Maps to shopping_user_emails.created_at.

updated_at.description: Most recent update to this email record (e.g., for verification, promotion to primary, etc.). Maps to shopping_user_emails.updated_at.

oneOf.description: Soft deletion timestamp for audit/compliance. ISO 8601 UTC.

deleted_at.description: If this record was deleted, this is the timestamp; may be null if still present.

IShoppingPasswordReset.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for a password reset request in the shopping mall platform. Includes essential audit and reference details without exposing secure or confidential reset tokens. Useful for listing recent password reset activity, security reviews, and compliance reporting. Derived from the shopping_password_resets Prisma model.

id.description: Unique identifier for the password reset request. Maps to shopping_password_resets.id.

oneOf.description: If present, the reset is for a customer user. Maps to shopping_password_resets.shopping_customer_id.

shopping_customer_id.description: Nullable field. Customer ID if reset requested for customer, else null.

oneOf.description: If present, the reset is for a seller user. Maps to shopping_password_resets.shopping_seller_id.

shopping_seller_id.description: Nullable field. Seller ID if reset requested for seller, else null.

oneOf.description: If present, the reset is for an admin user. Maps to shopping_password_resets.shopping_admin_id.

shopping_admin_id.description: Nullable field. Admin ID if reset requested for admin, else null.

request_email.description: Email supplied to request the password reset (used for audit, matches the user table). Corresponds to shopping_password_resets.request_email.

expires_at.description: When the password reset code (token) will expire. ISO 8601 UTC, for UI expiration logic. Maps to shopping_password_resets.expires_at.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when the reset code was used/invalidated. ISO 8601 UTC.

consumed_at.description: Nullable. When reset action was completed. Null if unused.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when this password reset request was created. ISO 8601 UTC.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when this request record was last updated (e.g., consumed, canceled). ISO 8601 UTC.

IShoppingProductTag.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for shopping product tags. This schema provides a compact representation of a free-form product tag used to enhance search, filtering, or categorization in the product catalog. This summary is used in list, search, or reference output where only the tag identity and display metadata are needed. Does not include product relation arrays.

- The tag_code is the business key for search and is globally unique per tag. Display_value is the user-facing, localized string for the tag shown in UI/search. Description is for admin/documentation.
- Used by search/filter APIs to show available tags or for product details to embed assigned tags contextually.

id.description: Unique tag identifier (PK, UUID).

tag_code.description: Business code/slug for the tag (unique, lowercase). Must be globally unique per catalog. Used as the reference value for programmatic filters, search and assignment. Enforced as unique in the schema.

display_value.description: Display value for the tag, shown to users in search/filter/product UI. This field is typically localized for end-user display and is not required to be unique. Sourced and managed in the catalog/admin panel.

oneOf.description: Optional documentation or explanation of the tag's business purpose or admin-intended usage. Useful for catalog managers, administrators, or in documentation. Nullable.

description.description: Optional documentation or explanation of the tag's business purpose or admin-intended usage. Useful for catalog managers, administrators, or in documentation. Nullable.

id.description: Unique identifier for the inventory record.

shopping_sku_id.description: The SKU entity this inventory record is for (one-to-one mapping to shopping_skus.id). Represents the main inventory reference for an active product variant.

quantity.description: Current available stock units for this SKU. This value must never be negative; application/business logic enforces zero floor for stockouts and prevents overselling.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the inventory record was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the inventory record was last changed.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion/audit retention timestamp. When populated, this inventory record is discontinued/archived, retained for compliance/audit history, and not considered active for stock display or update.

IShoppingInventory.ISummary.description: ShoppingInventory summary DTO. Provides an overview of inventory state for a specific SKU, showing real-time available quantity, audit information, and status needed for stock display and API responses. Maps to the shopping_inventory table. Key for enabling stock validation, availability, and operational visibility in both customer and seller flows.

id.description: Unique identifier for the shopping cart.

shopping_customer_id.description: The customer who owns this cart.

created_at.description: Cart creation timestamp.

updated_at.description: Timestamp of the last update to the cart (e.g., item addition or removal).

items.description: A list of items currently in the cart. Each item represents a selected SKU and desired quantity for purchase.

IShoppingCart.ISummary.description: ShoppingCart summary DTO. Contains a snapshot of the current state of a customer's cart, including all items (SKU references and quantities) they intend to purchase. Used for customer-facing cart UI, API responses, and checkout preparation. Does not include any guest cart or ephemeral session data. Maps to shopping_carts.

IShoppingCartItem.ISummary.description: Summary view of an item in a customer's shopping cart. Represents a single SKU and its quantity for review or checkout. Does not expose sensitive internal identifiers or full cart structure. Includes relationships to product SKU, customer, and relevant minimal product info for cart display.

id.description: Unique identifier for this cart item.

sku.description: SKU summary for the item currently in the cart.

quantity.description: Number of units for this SKU in the cart.

added_at.description: Timestamp for when this item was added to the cart.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent update (quantity change) of this cart item.

id.description: Unique identifier for the wishlist item. Matches shopping_wishlist_items.id from the database.

sku.description: Summary information for the SKU included in the wishlist (was shopping_sku_id reference). Embeds key SKU summary for display and detail lookup, enabling atomic list display in wishlist APIs.

added_at.description: Timestamp when the SKU was added to the wishlist. Sourced from shopping_wishlist_items.added_at.

IShoppingWishlistItem.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a wishlist item belonging to a customer. Each record indicates a single SKU added to an account's wishlist, with timestamp and referential relations. SKU is inlined as a summary object for atomic reference, following summary relation rules. Derived from shopping_wishlist_items table in the Prisma schema. Used for listing or reference views.

IShoppingRefundRequest.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a refund, return, or cancellation request for a shopping order. This ISummary variant embeds the related order summary (IShoppingOrder.ISummary), actor summary (IRefundActor.ISummary), and an array of item summaries (IShoppingRefundRequestItem.ISummary). Used for list reporting, dashboards, and notification UIs where immediate context about actor, order, and affected items is needed. This summary DTO is business-ready for human-overview display and status reporting contexts.

id.description: Unique identifier of the refund request (primary key on shopping_refund_requests).

order.description: Summary of the order to which this refund/return/cancellation applies.

actor.description: Summary of the actor (customer/seller/admin) who filed the refund request.

request_type.description: Business type of this request: 'refund', 'return', or 'cancellation'.

business_reason.description: Business reason for this request (e.g., 'defective', 'changed mind', etc). Required.

request_context.description: (Optional) Additional context or metadata for this request, may contain JSON as string.

status.description: Workflow/business status for request (e.g., 'pending','approved','rejected','completed').

created_at.description: Timestamp when the request was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for last modification or status change.

items.description: Array of item summaries (order line-level per affected SKU) for this refund/return request, enabling partial/line-item refund reporting.

IShoppingRefundRequestItem.ISummary.description: Summary representation of an individual item included in a refund/return/cancellation request. Each entry refers to a single order line (SKU) claimed in the request, showing quantity, optional per-item reason, and timeline. Used in refund reporting and status tracking views supporting partial or line-item returns.

id.description: Unique identifier for this refund request item. Taken from shopping_refund_request_items.id.

shopping_refund_request_id.description: ID of the parent refund request. References shopping_refund_requests.id.

order_line_id.description: ID for the specific order line (SKU) subject to refund. References shopping_order_lines.id.

quantity.description: Number of units being claimed for refund on this order line. Must be at least 1, and cannot exceed original ordered quantity.

item_business_reason.description: Optional: Item-specific business reason for refund/return. Provided by requester and may override the parent request's business_reason. Nullable if not specified.

created_at.description: Timestamp when this refund item was created (ISO 8601).

updated_at.description: Timestamp for last modification of this item (ISO 8601).

IShoppingRefundAttachment.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a refund attachment entity, used to expose uploaded evidence, photos, documents, or files tied to a refund request or specific item. This type links each attachment to its parent refund request, and optionally to a specific item, and provides basic metadata required for displaying or handling file downloads. Suited for response bodies in refund review, audit, or attachment APIs. Properties here match the shopping_refund_attachments database table.

id.description: Unique identifier of the attachment. UUID from shopping_refund_attachments.id.

shopping_refund_request_id.description: ID of the parent refund request. References shopping_refund_requests.id.

shopping_refund_request_item_id.description: ID of the specific refund request item attached to, if any. Nullable; if not attached to a specific item, value is null.

attachment_file_id.description: ID of the attached file entity (from the platform file/image storage subsystem). References shopping_product_images.id or proper file asset.

attachment_type.description: Type/category of the attachment (e.g., 'evidence', 'photo', 'invoice'). Business constant from upload context.

oneOf.description: Optional description or comment explaining the business purpose of the attachment (e.g., 'damage evidence', 'proof of purchase').
Null when no description provided; specify explicitly as null if absent.

description.description: Optional description or purpose of the attachment file. This field is nullable.

uploaded_at.description: Timestamp for when the attachment was uploaded. ISO 8601 format ('YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ').

IShoppingRefundApproval.ISummary.description: Summary of a refund approval or rejection action performed by a seller or admin for a given refund request. Contains references to the parent refund request, the associated approval status change, actor details, decision outcome (action), timestamp, and optional rationale. Suited for embedding in refund status audit trails and dashboards. All fields match the shopping_refund_approvals database; nullable string fields are explicitly described. Enum/const business values are clarified. See shopping_refund_approvals in schema for keys.

id.description: Unique identifier for this refund approval action. Primary key from the database (shopping_refund_approvals.id).

shopping_refund_request_id.description: The unique identifier for the refund request to which this approval is linked. Foreign key reference to shopping_refund_requests.id.

shopping_refund_status_history_id.description: The status history record this approval is based on; foreign key to shopping_refund_status_histories.id.

shopping_actor_id.description: Unique ID of the actor (admin or seller) who executed this approval or rejection event.

oneOf.description: Type of actor taking approval action. Must be one of: 'admin', 'seller'. Only these constant string values are allowed; refer to business role context.
Type of actor taking approval action. Must be one of: 'admin', 'seller'. Only these constant string values are allowed; refer to business role context.

actor_type.description: Type of actor taking approval action. Must be one of: 'admin', 'seller'. Only these constant string values are allowed; refer to business role context.

action.description: Result of this approval or rejection event for the refund status transition. Business constant such as 'approved' or 'rejected'. Allowable values follow platform-defined enum for approval workflow (e.g. ['approved','rejected']). Refer to business rules for valid list.

oneOf.description: Optional business rationale or comment for the approval/rejection action.
Null if no note provided for this action.

note.description: Optional business rationale, notes, or comments regarding why the approval/rejection was issued. Nullable; may be omitted or explicitly null.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the approval or rejection was recorded in the system, in ISO 8601 format (e.g. '2025-10-31T13:00:00Z').

IShoppingShipment.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for a shipment entity. This schema provides only the core fields required for shipment list, dashboard, or order-summary API responses—excluding composition arrays or deeply-nested data. Use only for operational monitoring, tracking overviews, and order shipment summaries, not internal logistics editing or deep composition. All timestamp fields are ISO 8601 UTC (nullable if business event has not occurred yet). Nullable fields always present; if event not yet occurred, value is null (never omitted). Maps strictly to shopping_shipments model. For field-level detail, see individual property docs.

id.description: Unique ID for shipment record, from shopping_shipments.id.

code.description: Unique business reference code used for shipment tracking, customer notification, and carrier handoff (e.g., 'SHPT-2025-1101').

status.description: Current shipment status (e.g., 'pending', 'packed', 'in_transit', 'delivered', 'canceled', 'returned'). See shopping_shipments.status for allowed values. Reflects business workflow lifecycle.

carrier_company.description: Allocated courier/shipping company (e.g., 'CJ대한통운', 'FedEx', 'UPS'). Used in external/customer notification and admin dashboards.

carrier_service_type.description: Optional courier service class/type (e.g., 'overnight', 'express', 'standard'), or null if no class set. Prisma: carrier_service_type.

scheduled_dispatch_at.description: Planned warehouse shipment date/time (ISO 8601 UTC), or null if not yet scheduled. See shopping_shipments.scheduled_dispatch_at.

dispatched_at.description: Actual handoff to carrier/fulfillment dispatch timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601), or null if not yet dispatched.

delivered_at.description: Final delivery timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601) if and when confirmed delivered, or null until carrier confirms delivery.

canceled_at.description: Timestamp recorded if shipment was canceled (UTC, ISO 8601), null if not canceled.

created_at.description: Row creation timestamp. See shopping_shipments.created_at.

updated_at.description: Last status or record update timestamp. See shopping_shipments.updated_at.

shopping_order_id.description: UUID reference of source order (shopping_orders.id) fulfilled by this shipment.

shopping_seller_id.description: UUID reference to the seller responsible for fulfillment (shopping_sellers.id).

IShoppingShipmentPackage.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for an individual shipment package within a multi-package shipment event. Used for shipment list and dashboard UIs. Contains only core tracking and logistics fields—no deep composition. Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC, always present (nullable if event not yet completed). All units documented in property-level docs. Maps to shopping_shipment_packages, and references only top-level data for fast lookup. Status includes all valid business lifecycle (pending, ready, shipped, in_transit, delivered, lost, damaged).

id.description: Unique package record identifier (UUID), from shopping_shipment_packages.id.

sequence.description: Zero-based order of this package within the shipment (0=first, 1=second, ...). Used to order physical packages for picking, delivery, and reporting.

package_label.description: Business/warehouse assigned unique label for package (e.g., 'PKG1', 'PKG02'). Used internally for logistics audits and admin reference.

tracking_number.description: Carrier-issued tracking number for this package (e.g., '123ABC987654'). Used in notifications to customers/admins. Must be unique per package.
