package_weight_grams.description: Weight of package in grams (whole or float, e.g., 1500 or 1420.5). Used for shipping rates and analytics.

status.description: Business and carrier status for the package (e.g., 'pending', 'ready', 'shipped', 'in_transit', 'delivered', 'lost', 'damaged'). Direct reflection of shopping_shipment_packages.status.

delivered_at.description: Confirmed delivery timestamp (UTC, ISO 8601), or null if not yet delivered. Reflects last carrier scan/customer receipt event.

lost_at.description: Timestamp for when this package was reported lost (UTC, ISO 8601), or null if not lost.

damaged_at.description: Timestamp for declared damage during fulfillment/delivery (UTC, ISO 8601), or null if never damaged.

created_at.description: When this package record was added to the database. Sourced from shopping_shipment_packages.created_at.

updated_at.description: Most recent status or record update (UTC, ISO 8601). From shopping_shipment_packages.updated_at.

id.description: Primary key for the review. shopping_reviews.id

customer.description: Summary object of reviewer customer, referencing the minimal personal information (name, email, phone, is_active, created_at, deleted_at as applicable). Used to show reviewer details contextually in a privacy-preserving way. Directly relates to shopping_customers entity. See IShoppingCustomer.ISummary for field breakdown.

sku.description: Summary object of the SKU (stock keeping unit) or product variant reviewed. Includes business-critical identifying details of the reviewed item — such as id, code, name, price, and active state for display and aggregation. See IShoppingSKU.ISummary for structure.

order_line_id.description: ID of the order line this review corresponds to. References shopping_order_lines.id, for enforcing eligibility and audit context.

rating.description: Star rating value (1–5, required for aggregation and for product score analytics).

comment.description: User review comment (10–2000 characters, required by business process). Used for public display, moderation, and aggregation of qualitative feedback.

state.description: Current review state; must be a value from the review status enum (e.g., 'visible', 'pending_moderation', 'removed', 'under_review'). Controls display, aggregation, and moderation workflows.

created_at.description: Review creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC).

updated_at.description: Timestamp for most recent review modification (ISO 8601 UTC).

IShoppingReview.ISummary.description: Summary representation of a SKU review by a customer as recorded in shopping_reviews. Used for API list, analytics, and contextual display views. Contains reviewer (customer as IShoppingCustomer.ISummary), referenced SKU (as IShoppingSKU.ISummary), order line (id only), star rating, comment, current moderation state, and audit timestamps. Relation fields match .ISummary pattern for embedding essential actor and item context. Foreign key fields are not duplicated.

id.description: Unique identifier for the moderation action record. Primary key from shopping_review_moderations.

shopping_review_id.description: Unique identifier of the review that was moderated. References shopping_reviews.id. Links this action to the review event.

moderator_admin_id.description: Unique identifier for the admin who performed the action. References shopping_admins.id. Administrator responsible for review moderation event.

action.description: Type of moderation action performed on the review. Values are taken from a business enum such as: 'approved', 'removed', 'restored', 'flagged', 'edited', etc. Controls review lifecycle and reporting workflow.

oneOf.description: Optional business/compliance reason, policy invoked, or moderator's audit note for why this action was taken. Rationale may be referenced in future appeals or compliance reports.

reason.description: Optional business/compliance reason, policy invoked, or moderator's audit note for why this action was taken. Rationale may be referenced in future appeals or compliance reports.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the moderation action was performed and recorded (ISO 8601 UTC). Used for audit trails and reporting.

IShoppingReviewModeration.ISummary.description: Represents a single moderation action on a shopping mall product review. Summarizes moderator action (type) taking place on a review (by id), the responsible admin, an optional explanatory reason, and the exact audit timestamp of the event. Aggregates state transition events for customer, seller, and admin review. Used for displaying moderation history, appeals context, and regulatory audit trails. Sourced from the shopping_review_moderations table.

IShoppingReviewAbuseReport.ISummary.description: Summary view of an abuse or inappropriate content report related to a product review. This DTO is used in moderation dashboards, review audit logs, and customer history to summarize when, how, and by whom an abuse report was filed against a review. Business context: each entry links a reported review, the reporting customer, the reason/type of abuse, optional comments, and moderation status. Actor visibility: customers can audit their own reports; admins/moderators access all records for compliance and decision logs. Lifecycle: the report may be open (pending moderation), processed, dismissed, or soft-deleted (e.g., on customer/account deletion or admin policy). Audit: All state changes and actor actions are retained for compliance and dispute tracking. Only available for reference if the actor has proper audit/reporting permissions. Fields reflect all relevant database audit and moderation metadata, but never expose internal moderation discussion or reviewer identity beyond actor context.

id.description: Unique identifier for the abuse report. Primary key from shopping_review_abuse_reports.

shopping_review_id.description: Unique identifier of the review being reported for abuse. References shopping_reviews.id.

reporter_customer_id.description: Unique identifier for the customer who reported the review. References shopping_customers.id.

oneOf.description: Optional text comment provided by the reporter explaining the abuse or providing supporting details. Null if not provided.

comment.description: Optional text comment provided by the reporter explaining the abuse or providing supporting details. Null if not provided.

state.description: State of the abuse report (e.g., 'open', 'processed', 'dismissed', etc.). Indicates moderation/review status.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the abuse report was created.

updated_at.description: Most recent timestamp for modification of the abuse report (processed, updated, or otherwise changed).

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion marker. Non-null if report was deleted (e.g., on account removal or administrative policy).

IShoppingPlatformAnnouncement.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for a platform-wide announcement as displayed in lists, notification feeds, and moderation dashboards. This type presents metadata about each announcement, including author (admin), title, audience, status, and scheduled visibility (publish window). Business context: Announcements are used for system maintenance/update communication, compliance messaging, business policies, or feature launches. Permissions: Only actors with admin/access rights may create or edit; visibility windows determine which segment (all/customers/sellers/admins) receives active announcements. Lifecycle: status field denotes current workflow (draft, scheduled, active, expired, hidden); publish_start_at/publish_end_at set scheduling. Audit & compliance: all property changes and creation are logged via admin_id, timestamps, and status/publish window for audit trails and record-keeping. Body content and full revision logs are not included; only core announcement metadata for rapid UI query. Soft-deleted announcements are not shown except in admin audit views. Scheduling and audience enforcement policies are dictated by platform configuration and compliance requirements.

id.description: Unique identifier for the announcement. Primary key in the shopping_platform_announcements table.

admin_id.description: UUID of the admin user who authored the announcement.

title.description: Announcement title, shown in notification headers and announcement listings.

target_audience.description: Segment or role targeted by the announcement (e.g., 'all', 'customers', 'sellers', 'admins').

status.description: Lifecycle status of the announcement (e.g., 'draft', 'scheduled', 'active', 'expired', 'hidden').

oneOf.description: Optional scheduled start datetime for announcement display (UTC ISO 8601).

publish_start_at.description: Optional scheduled start datetime for announcement display (UTC ISO 8601).

oneOf.description: Optional scheduled end datetime for announcement visibility (UTC ISO 8601).

publish_end_at.description: Optional scheduled end datetime for announcement visibility (UTC ISO 8601).

created_at.description: Timestamp when the announcement record was created (UTC, ISO 8601).

IShoppingAdminActionLog.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for platform administrator action logs, used in admin list panels and compliance dashboards. Each instance represents an atomic, auditable event such as privilege escalation, forced policy or status changes, role assignments, or manual overrides by platform admins. All fields are present in the underlying Prisma shopping_admin_action_logs table. This summary type optimizes for list views, analytics, or investigation search pages by excluding deep nested object graphs, focusing on top-level business context and actor/event references needed for regulatory compliance.

Field notes:
- Fields matching Prisma log tables are always present. Affected_ fields (admin, seller, customer) are set only for records where the action is relevant to an actor, else remain null for dashboard and audit navigation.
- The 'action_type' code identifies business operation or policy change (e.g., 'GRANT_ROLE', 'FORCE_RESET'). See adminops business logic for allowable codes.
- The 'deleted_at' field is a soft deletion marker for audit/legal hiding only, never means physical/irreversible delete. Log records are retained for audit and forensic review even when suppressed from default list views.
- 'reason' is an optional admin-entered context or business justification for event, used in dispute/audit contexts.

id.description: Unique identifier for this admin action log record. Primary key for audit and dashboard linking. Maps exactly to shopping_admin_action_logs.id.

admin_id.description: UUID of the admin who performed this action. References shopping_admins.id and appears in all privileged operations. Used for actor accountability in audit.

affected_admin_id.description: UUID of the admin affected by this operation, if present (e.g., when updating another admin's privileges). Null unless directly impacted.

affected_seller_id.description: UUID of the seller impacted by this action. Set for log entries referencing sellers. Null if not a seller-targeted operation.

affected_customer_id.description: UUID of customer affected by the admin action. Set only if event directly involved a customer account. Null otherwise.

action_type.description: Constant code for admin event (e.g., 'GRANT_ROLE', 'FORCE_RESET', 'SUSPEND_SELLER'); matches business enums/logic. Used in analytics, compliance, and dashboard filters to categorize event types.

entity_type.description: Type of entity changed or managed by the admin event (e.g., 'product', 'order', 'user', 'setting'). Null if action was generic/non-entity specific.

entity_id.description: UUID for the affected entity (product, order, etc.); null if action was not entity-specific.

reason.description: Business rationale, audit comment, or admin-entered context for this operation. Included for compliance and dispute review. Optional. Null if no note entered.

created_at.description: Timestamp marking when this admin audit event was created. Used in compliance timelines and forensic investigations. Maps to shopping_admin_action_logs.created_at.

deleted_at.description: Soft deletion marker used for log hiding, not permanent erasure. Present if the log is hidden or redacted in dashboards. Always retained in compliance audit reporting.

IShoppingBusinessPolicy.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for shopping mall business policy configurations. Represents platform-wide business rules (e.g., return window, seller onboarding requirements) in a format optimized for list views and dashboard reference, as opposed to full policy detail editing or setup. Fields map 1:1 to the Prisma shopping_business_policies model; all are non-null, required, and correspond directly to table columns for policy management, audit, and compliance.

Usage notes:
- Used for admin list/table views, export, and policy audit dashboards.
- All fields are always present in summary; no fields are nullable, for UI/data integrity.
- 'policy_name' is the primary business identifier and enables filtering and audit navigation.
- 'scope' specifies context or functional area for this policy (e.g., 'orders', 'global', 'sellers').
- 'value' holds the enforced limit, threshold, or decision code for this rule.
- 'active' is a boolean indicating enforcement status.
- 'description' is always present and details business intent, compliance rationale, or operational notes.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the business policy configuration. Maps to shopping_business_policies.id, primary key for internal/external ref.

policy_name.description: Human-readable, unique business policy identifier (e.g., 'order_return_window', 'seller_onboarding_requirement'). Used in admin dashboards and rule enforcement audits. Maps to policy_name in the database.

scope.description: Domain or subsystem where this business policy applies (e.g., 'global', 'orders', 'sellers'). Drives which platform functions are governed by this rule/configuration. Maps to shopping_business_policies.scope.

value.description: Concrete limit, threshold, or code value for this business policy (e.g., '30', 'approved', 'active'). May encode numbers/text; interpretation varies by policy. Used in platform logic and admin reporting. Always present, never null in summary.

description.description: Required documentation string for this policy. Explains business rationale, operational notes, and compliance logic. Shown in admin/policy dashboards. Always non-null in summary type.

active.description: Boolean indicating if this policy is currently enforced (true) or dormant (false). Controls runtime logic and admin policy lists.

created_at.description: Creation timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC). Used in admin audit, timeline reporting, and policy compliance review. Maps to DB created_at.

updated_at.description: Last modified timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC), used for admin/audit record trace. Maps to DB updated_at.

IShoppingBusinessConstraint.ISummary.description: Summary DTO for shopping_business_constraints entity. Represents a platform or domain constraint/limit (rate limits, SKU per product, min/max values, etc.). Used in list/admin/reference scenarios. Maps directly to the Prisma shopping_business_constraints model; all fields correspond to columns listed in the schema.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) of the constraint in shopping_business_constraints.

constraint_name.description: Unique name of the constraint, e.g., 'max_orders_per_user_day', 'sku_max_per_product'.

scope.description: Domain or context for the constraint (e.g., 'global', 'checkout', 'products').

limit_value.description: Raw constraint value as string (typically integer or decimal, but always string in DB).

description.description: Full business explanation of what limit this constraint applies and its operational significance.

active.description: Whether this constraint is currently in force.

created_at.description: Constraint creation timestamp.

updated_at.description: Constraint last update timestamp.

IShoppingFeatureFlag.ISummary.description:
Summary type for a single feature flag in the shopping mall platform. This type provides a lightweight, query-friendly representation used for list responses, references, and embedding in other entities. Reflects only key columns from the shopping_feature_flags Prisma model, focusing on unique flag identification, current enablement state, scope, description, rollout percentage (if set), and audit timestamps. Intended for admin and devops UI, diagnostics, and operational switches. Does NOT include relations or sensitive logic; use the full detail type for complete information.

- Follows platform-wide feature toggle and rollout conventions.
- Used in admin controls, system status dashboards, and as return type of feature flag list APIs.
- For definition of all properties and their business role, see shopping_feature_flags table in the Prisma schema.

id.description: Unique identifier of the feature flag record as stored in shopping_feature_flags.id. This is a system-generated UUID used for referencing and audit.

flag_name.description: Unique name of the feature flag (e.g., 'new_checkout_flow', 'wishlist_enabled'). Must be unique per scope; manages API toggles and controlled feature access as configured by admins. Maps to shopping_feature_flags.flag_name.

scope.description: Domain or bounded context where this feature flag applies (e.g., 'global', 'orders', 'checkout', 'frontend'). Used to group and segment features for rollout or visibility. Maps to the scope column in shopping_feature_flags.

enabled.description: Boolean toggle indicating whether the feature is currently active in its scope. True means enabled, false means disabled. Used by application logic to gate feature access. Maps to enabled column.

oneOf.description: Optional rollout percentage for gradual enablement (0.0–100.0). If present, indicates partial rollout for A/B testing; if not present, feature is either fully on or off. Maps to rollout column from shopping_feature_flags.

rollout.description: Nullable percentage rollout for gradual enablement (0.0–100.0); see rollout column in shopping_feature_flags. If not present or null, feature is globally on/off only. Used for phased launches and experimentation.

description.description: Human-readable business description and rationale for the feature flag. Used in admin UIs and operational documentation. Maps to shopping_feature_flags.description.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the feature flag was created in the platform. Used for audit and history. Maps to created_at column.

updated_at.description: Timestamp when the feature flag record was last updated in the platform. Used for audit and history. Maps to updated_at column.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IShoppingAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

IPageIShoppingGuestCartItem.ISummary.description:
A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

IShoppingSku.description: Main entity DTO for SKUs (Stock Keeping Units). Maps directly to shopping_skus table in the catalog. Each SKU defines a variant for a product, with pricing, status, barcode, and audit fields, plus variant attribute and product context. Used for detail view, creation, update, etc.

id.description: SKU unique identifier (UUID PK).

price.description: Retail price for this SKU variant.

is_active.description: SKU enabled/disabled flag. Only active SKUs are purchasable.

oneOf.description: Optional barcode/UPC for the SKU.

status.description: Business process status (e.g., in_stock, discontinued, archived).

created_at.description: SKU creation timestamp (ISO8601).

updated_at.description: SKU last update timestamp (ISO8601).

deleted_at.description: Soft delete marker for SKU archival; null if active.

variant_attributes.description: Variant attributes assigned to this SKU (e.g., color, size, etc).

product.description: Reference to the parent product (summary view).

images.description: Image URIs associated with this SKU.

IShoppingSkuImage.description:
Image object for SKUs. Represents direct images tied to a single SKU (e.g., color swatch, variant image). Used in SKU detail lists and variant selection. Enforces relationship to parent SKU via required shopping_sku_id. Only images linked to SKUs are permitted in create/upload APIs.

Properties:
- id: UUID, primary key for the SKU image
- shopping_sku_id: UUID, foreign key, required for linkage to the SKU
- image_uri: URI of the SKU-specific image asset
- created_at: Upload/create timestamp (ISO8601)

All properties are defined in the Prisma schema and enforced for type and intent. All image uploads must reference a valid existing SKU via shopping_sku_id.

id.description: Primary Key.

shopping_sku_id.description: SKU identifier. Foreign key to shopping_skus.id; required to associate image with variant/SKU in the catalog.

image_uri.description: URI of the SKU-specific image asset.

created_at.description: Upload/create timestamp (ISO8601).

IShoppingSku.IRequest.description:
Request DTO for paginated, filterable SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) listing. This type is used in endpoints for listing/searching SKUs under a product (code-based context), supporting search, filter, sort, and pagination according to catalog management. Follows platform IPage/IRequest conventions.

All filter/sort params are optional. Path parameters such as product code are NOT repeated in the body.

page.description: Pagination: page number (1-based).

limit.description: Pagination: number of SKUs per page. Business default: 20, maximum: 100.

search.description: Global search term filter (free-text matches on sku_code, barcode, etc).

status.description: Filter: SKU status (string value, filtered per business conventions).

barcode.description: Filter: SKU barcode (exact or partial match).

min_price.description: Filter: Minimum price (SKUs with price >= this value).

max_price.description: Filter: Maximum price (SKUs with price <= this value).

sort_by.description: Sort field for results (allowed: 'created_at', 'price', 'sku_code', 'status').

oneOf.description: Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Sort direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

IShoppingSku.ICreate.description: Schema for creating a new SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) under an existing product. Used by sellers or admins to add a unique variant with pricing, activation status, and variant attribute configuration. Parent product context is provided through path parameter (productCode), not in request body. All fields are validated per business workflow and Prisma schema. Actor identity (seller/admin) is enforced by security context, not directly visible here.

sku_code.description: Unique SKU business code for the new Stock Keeping Unit. Must be globally unique. Used for catalog lookup, order lines, and variant mapping. Enforced by the unique constraint in Prisma.

price.description: Retail price for this SKU variant. Uses platform default currency. Must be greater than or equal to 0. Required for catalog display and order lines. Maps to 'price' in 'shopping_skus'.

is_active.description: Set true if the SKU is currently available for purchase. Determines if SKU is present in catalog and can be added to cart. If false, SKU is disabled from purchase (business archiving, stockout, soft retirement).

oneOf.description: Optional barcode or UPC string for scanning/fulfillment. Null if not provided. Maps to 'barcode' in Prisma schema.

barcode.description: Optional barcode or UPC string for scanning/fulfillment. Null if not provided. Maps to 'barcode' in Prisma schema.

status.description: Business process status for this SKU (e.g., in_stock, discontinued, archived, etc). Soft business state field defined per workflow.

items.description: ID of a selected attribute value for this SKU's variant (see shopping_attribute_values). For instance, selected color/size for a specific variant. Compose all relevant dimensions for this SKU variant.

variant_attribute_value_ids.description: Array of attribute value IDs chosen to define this SKU. These represent the selected dimension values (like color, size) for the specific variant. Required: must include at least one for a valid SKU.

IShoppingSku.IUpdate.description: Schema for updating mutable properties of an individual SKU (Stock Keeping Unit) under a given product. Used by sellers (for owned SKUs) or admins (all SKUs). SKU identity (skuCode, productCode) is provided via path parameters. Only mutable SKU attributes are included. Mutability of status is subject to business workflow (e.g., whether the SKU is involved in active order lines). No actor or product references are present in the request body.

price.description: Optional new price for this SKU. Must be greater than or equal to zero if supplied. If omitted, price remains unchanged.

is_active.description: Set to true if SKU should be enabled for purchase, or false to disable/hide SKU. Can be toggled for business archiving or retirement.

oneOf.description: Optional barcode to update on the SKU (e.g., UPC, EAN). May be set to null to remove existing barcode.

barcode.description: Optional barcode to update on the SKU (e.g., UPC, EAN). May be set to null to remove existing barcode.

status.description: Business process status for this SKU (e.g., in_stock, discontinued, archived, etc). Only valid transitions allowed by system.

IShoppingSku.ISummary.description:
Minimal summary of SKU for use in order line, refund item display, carts, wishlists, or references as child objects. Includes essential SKU identifier, business code, price, plus `is_active` and `status` for display and business rules context. Drawn from shopping_skus model, this summary enables availability checks, offers, and business logic that depends on SKU lifecycle. DO NOT use for editing; this is strictly a reference/summary. For full properties, see IShoppingSKU.

**Fields:**
- id: SKU unique identifier (UUID)
- sku_code: Globally unique business code
- price: Retail (catalog) price for this SKU
- is_active: SKU enabled/disabled as catalog item (business visibility and availability)
- status: Current business processing state (e.g., in_stock, discontinued, archived, etc.).

id.description: SKU unique identifier (shopping_skus.id)

sku_code.description: Globally unique business code for this SKU (shopping_skus.sku_code).

price.description: Sku price as defined in catalog at order time (shopping_skus.price).

is_active.description: SKU enabled/disabled flag for this item. Indicates if SKU can be shown or added to cart (shopping_skus.is_active).

status.description: Business process status of this SKU (e.g., in_stock, discontinued, archived, etc. from shopping_skus.status).

session_key.description: The unique session key (UUID) identifying this guest cart. Used in search queries to locate a specific session. Must be a valid UUID string if provided.

created_from.description: (Optional) Filter for carts created after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

created_to.description: (Optional) Filter for carts created before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

updated_from.description: (Optional) Filter for carts last updated after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

updated_to.description: (Optional) Filter for carts last updated before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

expires_before.description: (Optional) Filter for carts expiring before this ISO 8601 timestamp.

expires_after.description: (Optional) Filter for carts expiring after this ISO 8601 timestamp.

is_expired.description: (Optional) If true, filters for expired carts; if false, for active/unexpired carts.

sort_by.description: (Optional) Sort field, e.g. 'updated_at', 'expires_at', 'created_at'. Default is updated_at.

oneOf.description: Sort order. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.
Sort order. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

sort_order.description: Sort order. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending.

page.description: Page number for pagination (1-based).

limit.description: Max results per page. Defaults to 20, max is 100.

IShoppingGuestCartItem.IRequest.description: Query parameters for searching guest carts in the shopping_guest_carts table. Supports filtering by session key, creation/update or expiration timestamp, expired status, sorting, and pagination for admin or batch operations.

id.description: UUID primary key of this fulfillment entry (from shopping_order_fulfillments.id).

fulfillment_code.description: Business-traceable code or label for the fulfillment (from fulfillment_code).

quantity_fulfilled.description: Quantity shipped/fulfilled in this event (from quantity_fulfilled).

status.description: Fulfillment event status (pending, shipped, delivered, canceled, etc from shopping_order_fulfillments.status).

seller_address_id.description: UUID of the address where fulfillment originated (shopping_seller_address_id).

IShoppingOrderLineFulfillment.ISummary.description: Summary of a fulfillment shipment/packing event associated with an order line. Used in IShoppingOrderLine.fulfillments (from shopping_order_fulfillments).

IShoppingRefundActor.ISummary.description: Minimal identification for the actor (customer, seller, or admin) that initiated a refund request. Does not expose private PII. Used for embedding in refund objects, status transitions, approvals, and admin override entities. For customer, 'name' maps to shopping_customers.name; for seller, 'name' maps to shopping_sellers.display_name; for admin, 'name' maps to shopping_admins.name. Business context and documentation should always use this mapping for clarity.

oneOf.description: Which actor type made this request. Determines the entity (shopping_customers).
Which actor type made this request. Determines the entity (shopping_sellers).
Which actor type made this request. Determines the entity (shopping_admins).

actor_type.description: Actor type responsible for this refund operation. Accepted values: 'customer' for a platform customer, 'seller' for the merchant, or 'admin' for a system administrator. Must be one of these exact strings.

id.description: UUID for the actor. For customer, this is shopping_customers.id; for seller, shopping_sellers.id; for admin, shopping_admins.id.

name.description: Actor's display name. For actor_type 'customer', this value is sourced from shopping_customers.name; for 'seller', this is shopping_sellers.display_name; for 'admin', this is shopping_admins.name. Always ensure downstream business logic and API documentation maps the correct entity field for name based on actor_type, to prevent mislabeling or ambiguity.

scenario.draft: Test successful registration of a new customer with unique email, valid strong password, real name, and valid phone. Verify that JWT tokens are issued and customer account is created in the system. Validate that the session and audit logs are properly recorded.

Test successful login by an existing active customer using the correct email and password. Verify new JWT tokens are issued and session tracked. Confirm audit trail and session logging are completed. Test login after registration.

dependencies.purpose: Register the customer account so it exists and is available for login testing

scenario.draft: Test login for an existing customer with correct email but invalid password. Expect authentication error referencing the failed password check and proper audit logging, with no session or JWT token issued.

dependencies.purpose: Register the customer account so an incorrect password attempt can be tested

scenario.draft: Test the ability of a seller to initiate a password reset by providing a registered email address. The scenario validates that a new password reset request is created in the system, a secure reset code is issued (but not disclosed in the response), and a generic confirmation is returned. The test ensures that no information about the existence of the email is leaked in the response. Email delivery is out of band and not directly tested here.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller with a valid business email before requesting a password reset.

scenario.draft: Test completion of the password reset process for a seller by submitting the reset code (previously requested), email, and a new valid password. The scenario covers verification of the code, updating the seller's password, marking the reset code as consumed, and receiving a generic success message (whether or not the reset code/email combination is valid). It ensures that after completion, the reset token cannot be used again, and no sensitive details about account existence are revealed in the response.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller account for which the password will be reset.
Initiate a password reset to generate a valid reset token for the test seller account.

scenario.draft: This test validates that an admin can successfully create a new category in an existing category tree using all required and optional fields. The workflow includes authenticating as a new admin, creating a category tree, and then creating a category within that tree with unique category_code, specifying a display name, sort order, and (if supported) a parent_id (null for top-level). The operation should succeed with the new category being visible for further catalog use. The test also ensures the uniqueness and hierarchy rules for categories are enforced and audited.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin and establish authentication context for category creation
Create a category tree into which the new category will be added

scenario.draft: This scenario validates that an admin can update an existing category within a specific category tree, including changing the display name, sort order, and potentially updating its parent category to adjust hierarchy. The test workflow includes authenticating as a new admin, creating a category tree and at least two categories (to allow for parent-child assignment), and then performing the update operation on one category. The scenario checks that hierarchical integrity is enforced (e.g. cycles are prevented), uniqueness constraints remain intact, and all updates are correctly reflected in the system with audit trails.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin and authenticate for performing update operations
Create a category tree to hold test categories
Create at least two categories in the tree: one as potential parent, the other as the target for update

scenario.draft: Test updating a customer's profile information with valid new name and phone number. The scenario covers successful workflow with proper authentication and existing customer context. The flow is: 1) register a new customer (join) to get customerId and access token, 2) update profile with valid fields, and 3) validate that the updated information is reflected in the customer's profile.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a new customer to obtain access token and customerId for the update test.

scenario.draft: Test a customer account self-deletion to ensure irreversible removal and compliance with business/data retention requirements. The workflow is: 1) register a new customer to acquire authentication, 2) perform account deletion as the authenticated customer, and 3) verify the account and associated data are no longer accessible or return the expected deleted response.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a new customer to allow deletion under their own context.

scenario.draft: Test the ability of an authenticated seller to create an inventory adjustment for a specific SKU. The scenario covers incrementing and decrementing inventory (positive/negative), ensuring no negative inventory is allowed, and verifies that only the owner seller can make adjustments. Validate audit logging and the effect on inventory record. Expected outcomes include: successful adjustment creates audit record and modifies inventory; attempts to set negative stock or adjust SKUs the seller doesn't own are rejected with proper business errors.

dependencies.purpose: Seller authentication is required to perform inventory adjustments. This creates and authenticates a seller account for use in the adjustment scenario.

scenario.draft: Validate that an administrator can successfully update an existing status enum for a specified domain and status code, modifying properties such as display_label, sort order, activation state, and description. The test covers relabeling a status, deactivating a status, updating the sort order for display, and modifying the description for enhanced documentation. Audit logging is checked to confirm changes are tracked. Ensures that only admin actors can perform this update and that changes are instantly reflected in the business domain using the modified status code.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin actor to perform privileged status enum updates.

scenario.draft: Ensure an administrator can permanently delete a status enum code from a given domain. Test includes verifying preconditions to confirm the status is not in active business use or referenced by platform workflows (with appropriate business warning or constraints). The administrator performs the delete, and the result is validated to confirm the status code is removed and no longer available in the corresponding enum domain. Access control is confirmed by requiring authentication as an admin, and audit log records the deletion event for traceability.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin actor to acquire authorization for performing the deletion of a status enum code.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully update a feature flag's configuration, including toggling its enablement, adjusting its rollout percentage, and modifying business description. The scenario validates access control (admin-only), business logic enforcement (rollout stays within 0-100), and persistence of edits. The flow must include authenticating as an admin, then updating an existing feature flag with new values, and finally verifying that the changes are reflected in the response and persisted.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a new admin for privileged feature flag operations.

scenario.draft: Test that a platform admin can permanently delete (hard remove) a feature flag by its flagName. The scenario ensures that deletion is restricted to authenticated admin actors, the flag is no longer accessible after deletion, and proper audit trail is maintained per compliance requirements. Steps include admin authentication, deletion of an existing feature flag, and verification that querying the deleted flag returns a not-found or appropriate error response.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a new admin to perform the feature flag deletion.

scenario.draft: Verify that a customer can successfully refresh JWT access and refresh tokens using a valid refresh token. The workflow starts with customer registration (join), then directly exercises the refresh endpoint using the refresh token returned from join. The scenario validates that the returned tokens are different from previous ones, the response structure matches the IShoppingCustomer.IAuthorized schema, and session metadata is updated accordingly. Edge cases, like using a refresh token tied to an inactive or deleted session, are not included here. The expected result is a successful token rotation and updated session.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer to initialize account for refresh token testing.

scenario.draft: Verify the initiation of a password reset request for a customer by providing a valid registered email. Workflow begins with customer registration (join), and then calls the reset-request endpoint. Checks that a reset token is generated, is time-limited and associated with the email, and that the API response does not reveal email existence (privacy). The test also ensures audit log entry is made and the response structure matches IShoppingCustomer.IPasswordResetInitiated. Edge cases such as exceeding rate limits or using an unregistered email are out of scope here. The main validation is secure reset token creation and privacy-preserving behavior.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer; the reset-request requires the email to exist for a valid flow.

scenario.draft: Test full customer password reset workflow. Begins by initiating a password reset request to ensure a valid secure reset token exists. Then completes the reset by supplying the token and new password. Validates successful password change, token consumption, and correct audit logging, as well as proper error handling for invalid, expired, or already used tokens. Ensures business logic such as password strength enforcement is respected. This scenario confirms that only the valid sequence of reset-request followed by reset-completion permits password update and session restoration.

dependencies.purpose: Initiate password reset request to generate a valid, time-limited reset token for the target customer before completing the reset.

scenario.draft: Test successful seller registration process with required fields including unique business email, password, display name, and contact phone. Verifies that after registration the system issues JWT access and refresh tokens, sets the seller status to 'pending', and prevents duplicate registration for the same email. Validates that all business and security rules are followed, such as password hashing, onboarding logic, and that post-registration flows (business info completion, downstream KYC) are triggered as described in platform requirements.

Test that an admin can successfully create a new business setting with a unique setting_key, value, and description. The scenario should validate that the created setting is persisted and returns all required audit information, ensuring uniqueness enforcement on the setting_key. Also verify that non-admin actors are not authorized to perform this operation and that attempts to create a duplicate key return a proper error.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to acquire credentials for authentication and authorization as required to create a business setting.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can update an existing business setting identified by settingKey. The scenario should verify that updating the setting_value and description is reflected in the resource, and that the updated_at timestamp changes appropriately for audit. Confirm that attempts to update a nonexistent settingKey yield an appropriate error and that non-admin users are denied access.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin account to acquire credentials for authentication and authorization as required to update a business setting.
Create a new business setting that will be updated in this scenario. This is necessary to ensure the settingKey exists and can be modified.

scenario.draft: Test the workflow of an admin creating a new SKU for an existing product. First, register a new admin and authenticate. Ensure only active (non-soft-deleted) configurations are included in results. Expectation: Admin role receives full configuration detail and correct access, while unauthorized users are denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new admin to obtain access token for authenticated search requests.

scenario.draft: Test that a platform administrator can successfully create a new admin suspension record for another admin actor. The scenario includes the full administrative workflow: authenticating as an admin, submitting the suspension creation request with all required context (target actor, type, reason, duration), and verifying that a new suspension entry is created and returned in the response. The test must validate business rules such as not suspending oneself and preventing duplicate or invalid suspensions. The expected outcome is a suspension entry reflecting all provided context and audit traceability.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to obtain credentials for authorized administrative operations.

scenario.draft: Test that a platform administrator can update details of an existing admin suspension record. This includes changing the suspension status (e.g., from active to revoked), updating reason codes, or modifying the end date for a temporary suspension. Workflow includes authenticating as admin, creating a suspension, then performing an allowed update, and validating that updated data is returned. The test must also ensure business rules are not violated (such as unlocking permanent suspensions without justification). Outcomes must include full entity update and all audit requirements met.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin for authorized access to update operation.
Create an initial admin suspension to ensure a valid record exists for update testing.

scenario.draft: Test the complete administrative lifecycle for updating an appeal record. This scenario covers registering a new admin account, ensuring appropriate admin authentication via join, then updating the status and decision rationale of a specific appeal (identified by appealId). The scenario validates business field transitions (such as from 'under_review' to 'approved' or 'rejected'), the recording of rationale/remarks, audit traceability, and refusal of unauthorized field changes. It should also validate that only properly authenticated admin actors can perform status updates and that all necessary enumeration values are respected in allowed transitions.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate admin actor context before executing appeal status update.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated admin can successfully perform advanced search, filtering, and pagination over business policy configuration records. The scenario begins by creating an admin user (via join), authenticating as admin, and then issuing a filtered PATCH request to search for business policies based on multiple fields (e.g., name, scope, active status, description). The test must confirm that pagination and advanced filtering return the correct, paginated summaries, honor user permissions, and reject unauthorized or malformed queries. Also validates support for sorting and exclusion of sensitive/internal notes in the summary.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a valid admin user required for access to business policy search endpoint.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller with a valid, authenticated session can retrieve full details for an order that includes products they own, verifying the returned data includes order lines, payment attempts, shipments, and all expected status/audit fields.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a seller to own a product and enable retrieval of their order details.
Seller creates a product to be included in an order.
Seller creates a SKU for the created product.
Authenticate as a new customer to place an order.
Customer places an order including the seller's SKU to generate a valid orderCode.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the full details of any order in the system, regardless of who owns the order or its status. Ensures admin permissions provide visibility into all order, line, split, payment, and shipment data for compliance and troubleshooting.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to enable retrieval of any order details.
Authenticate as a new seller to create product for the order.
Seller creates a product that will be ordered by a customer.
Seller creates a SKU for the product.
Authenticate as a new customer to place an order.
Customer places an order with the seller's SKU to create a valid order for admin retrieval.

scenario.draft: Simulate a full seller password reset workflow: a seller initiates password reset request, then updates the reset (e.g., extend expiration or mark as consumed) through the password reset update API. Scenario covers security enforcement (seller must be authenticated), proper chaining of operations, and verifies that only the proper seller can update their own password reset request. Test should validate allowed updates, rejection of updates to expired or already consumed resets, and business logic such as audit logging for expiry or consumption. The request must strictly adhere to security and business workflows, ensuring sensitive reset actions are only performed by authorized identity. Success and expected failure paths (e.g., update after expiration) should be verified.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a new seller account for password reset flow.
Initiate a password reset request for the seller (generates a password reset entry that can then be updated).

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can permanently delete a password reset request by its unique ID. The scenario begins by creating a user entity requiring a password reset entry (e.g., create a customer password reset via the respective API), then as an admin, the system attempts to erase the reset request using the admin delete endpoint. Execute both a success path (delete an existing reset request) and a negative path (try deleting a nonexistent or already deleted/reset request). Confirm that proper security and audit requirements are enforced—only admin actors are permitted to perform this operation, and all deletions are logged for future compliance.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a new admin for performing password reset deletions.
Initialize a customer password reset request to generate a password reset record for deletion testing.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated admin can successfully search and retrieve a paginated, filtered list of customers using the customer search API. Validate support for core search parameters such as name, email, phone, active/inactive status, registration date range, and confirm result pagination and sorting work as expected. Scenario confirms that sensitive information is protected according to admin role, and that the result contains only summary-level customer information.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to access customer search API

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated admin can retrieve detailed profile information for a specific customer account using their UUID. Validate that all permitted account fields are returned per business and compliance rules, including profile, status, and audit-related fields. Confirm proper enforcement of access control: only admin or the owner can view full details, and non-existent or forbidden requests are rejected with correct error codes.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to access customer detail API
Create a customer account so there is a valid customerId to query

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can retrieve all shipping and billing addresses associated with an order they are fulfilling. This scenario starts by registering a seller account (to establish authentication context), then creates a new order as a prerequisite (handled outside this scenario), and retrieves the list of all order addresses via the seller's endpoint. The scenario validates that the list includes expected shipping and billing information, and enforces role-based visibility (seller sees only orders they fulfill).

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as seller to access order addresses

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve all shipping and billing addresses for any order in the system. The scenario first registers an admin account (to obtain authentication and establish new user context), then assumes an order with addresses exists (order creation is handled outside this scenario). The admin retrieves the order's address list and verifies it includes all relevant records for audit and compliance purposes. Verifies unrestricted admin access and data completeness.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to retrieve any order addresses

scenario.draft: Test the process of an admin permanently deleting a seller account from the system. The scenario ensures that only authenticated admin users can perform this irreversible action, and verifies that after deletion, the seller's account is marked as deleted and cannot be accessed or logged in. Also confirm that the system prevents deletion when the seller has ongoing fulfillment or dispute workflows. After successful deletion, the system should still retain historical data for compliance, while the seller's active participation is terminated in business logic. Validate compliance audit log creation as part of deletion.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a new admin user for test context

scenario.draft: Test the retrieval of a seller's full business registration and compliance information by an admin user. The scenario validates that an authenticated admin can access all required fields including legal, tax, banking, and compliance data, and that sensitive fields are properly masked for non-admin roles. It also checks that the endpoint is inaccessible without admin authentication, ensuring strict privacy and regulatory compliance for business data. Confirm that an error is returned for nonexistent sellers or if the requester is not properly authenticated as admin.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a new admin user for retrieval authorization

scenario.draft: Comprehensively test retrieval of a specific admin user's detail by adminId. This workflow ensures that admin role authentication is established by joining (creating a new admin account) before accessing the account detail endpoint. It covers confirming proper retrieval of the full admin profile including contact information, name, role, and business status. Expected outcomes include successful profile access for valid adminId and account data accuracy, along with business error handling for deleted or suspended accounts. Security checks verify that only authenticated admins can access full details.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new admin account and establish authenticated admin context required for subsequent account detail retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test the ability for an authenticated admin actor to update admin details using their adminId. The workflow begins with admin account creation via join, followed by an update operation to modify fields such as name, email, assigned role, or account status. Validation covers that changes conform to policy, email uniqueness is enforced, and that updates are successfully persisted and reflected in subsequent retrievals. Error handling for permission issues, attempt to modify restricted fields, or updating non-existent admin accounts is also verified. All updates require that the modifying user is authenticated as an admin.

dependencies.purpose: Create a new admin account and establish authentication context for performing update operation.

scenario.draft: Test the complete flow to update a platform announcement as an admin. The scenario starts by registering a new admin account, then using that authenticated admin context to create a platform announcement, and finally updating the announcement's content, target audience, publication window, and status. The test validates that the update is successful when the required fields are provided and the authenticated admin is used. It also verifies auditing requirements are met and the changes are reflected in the entity.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a new admin to gain access to platform announcement APIs.
Create a platform announcement to set up a context for the update operation.

scenario.draft: Test the business workflow for soft-deleting a platform announcement as an admin. The scenario first registers a new admin account to establish authentication, then creates a new platform announcement, then issues a deletion (soft delete) request for that announcement. The test ensures the announcement is soft-deleted (deleted_at is set), remains in the audit trail, and is no longer included in user-facing announcement listings but can be retrieved by authorized admin audit queries.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to perform the deletion operation.
Create the platform announcement to allow deletion by its ID.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully retrieve the details of a specific policy violation by its unique identifier. The scenario covers normal retrieval, verifies the presence and accuracy of decision, status, policy reference, and reporting actors. Also ensure the API returns appropriate audit fields and associated decision/escalation data, and does not expose information to unauthorized actors. The expected result is full context visibility for platform compliance review.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to acquire access rights for policy violation records

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can update a policy violation by its unique identifier, recording review results, status changes, and decision rationale. Ensure that only mutable fields are successfully updated and audit compliance is maintained. The test verifies that non-existent and immutable field updates are correctly rejected. The expected outcome is a traceable update in both business and audit fields for the targeted policy violation.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to gain update privileges on policy violation records

scenario.draft: Test permanent deletion of a file attachment from a customer review by an authorized admin. Begin by registering a new admin using the admin join endpoint to obtain authentication, ensure the admin creates a review and attaches at least one file to it. As the admin, delete the attachment using the specified endpoint. Validate that the attachment is no longer listed for the review and is fully removed from displays. Confirm audit logging of the deletion and appropriate permissions enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin actor with the necessary privileges.
Register and authenticate a customer actor (review author).
Customer creates a review that will receive a file attachment.
Attach a file to the created customer review to ensure a removable attachment exists.

scenario.draft: Test retrieval of the moderation log history for a specific review by an authorized admin. Register and join as a new admin, create a customer review, perform a moderation action (such as approval or removal) on the review using the moderation create endpoint, then retrieve the moderation history via the index endpoint. Validate that the moderation action is logged correctly and returned in the moderation history, with all relevant fields present. Confirm proper admin permissions enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate an admin actor for moderation actions and privileged access.
Register and authenticate a customer actor (review author).
Customer creates a review as the moderation target.
Admin performs a moderation action (approve or remove) on the review to create a moderation log entry.

scenario.draft: Validate that an authenticated seller is able to upload a new product image for a product they own. The flow includes successful authentication as a new seller, creation of a catalog product by the seller, then uploading a valid JPEG/PNG (≤5MB) image. Confirm business logic checks: product existence, seller ownership, image file validity, and that the newly created image entity is returned and can be retrieved. Also verify that image count does not exceed 10 per product. Edge cases include verifying failure when uploading an image if the product does not exist, if the seller does not own the product, if the file is too large, or incorrect filetype is supplied, or if the maximum image limit is reached.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate a new seller account for testing seller-side image upload.
Create a new product under the authenticated seller to upload images to.

scenario.draft: Verify that an admin can upload a product image for a specified product (regardless of ownership). The flow involves authenticating a new admin user, creation of a product under admin context, and uploading a valid JPEG/PNG product image (≤5MB). Validate full success scenario, including product existence, successful image creation, and correct association with the specified product. Edge cases to cover: attempt upload to a non-existent product, upload exceeding 10 images per product, invalid file type, and file size limit enforcement. Confirm expected error responses in those cases.

dependencies.purpose: Create and authenticate a new admin account for uploading product images.
Admin creates a product prior to image upload; image must be linked to an existing product.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can retrieve detailed information for a specific split of an order assigned to them. The scenario includes the full workflow for seller onboarding, ensuring correct authentication, and validating the retrieval of split order details such as status, assigned seller, subtotal, and audit history. The test should verify that the response data consistently reflects business assignment and data accuracy for the seller's segment of a multi-seller order.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as a seller to access order split data assigned to a seller.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve detailed information for any order split using the correct order code and split code. The scenario includes registering an admin, authenticating, and verifying retrieval of split-level detail such as status, allocated seller, subtotal, and full audit information. Validate that the operation works regardless of the seller assignment and provides unrestricted split order data as expected for platform administrators.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as an admin for system-level order split access.

scenario.draft: Test that a logged-in customer can successfully soft-delete their own wishlist. Start by registering a new customer, creating a wishlist, and then deleting it using the target endpoint. Validate that the wishlist is marked as deleted and cannot be accessed via retrieval endpoints, while the data remains for audit compliance. Business rules about traceability and proper authorization must be enforced—ensure that deletion is blocked for wishlists not owned by the current user.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a new customer to create and own wishlists before testing wishlist deletion.

scenario.draft: Test that a customer can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of items in their own wishlist. Begin by registering a customer, creating a wishlist, and adding multiple items with varied product SKUs. Use the endpoint to search and paginate items by SKU or product name, and verify correct pagination, ownership enforcement, and that filtering matches expected catalog content. Attempting to retrieve another user’s wishlist items should be rejected for authorization reasons.

dependencies.purpose: Register and authenticate as a customer with owned wishlists before performing wishlist item queries.
Create wishlist and add initial set of items so pagination and filtering can be meaningfully tested.

scenario.draft: Validate that a seller can successfully search and filter all tracking instances and their event logs for a specific shipment package that they own. Workflow: (1) Register a new seller and obtain authentication; (2) (Dependency - out of scope here) create a shipment with at least one package assigned to the seller; (3) As the authenticated seller, perform a PATCH search on shipment tracking specifying the shipment code and package label for a package under the seller’s shipment; (4) Provide various filter parameters such as status, event date range, and tracking source to ensure proper filtering and pagination; (5) Check that the tracking instance list and associated event histories are accurate, only include records belonging to the shipment and package owned by this seller, and that seller can not view tracking data for packages from other sellers; (6) Edge case: attempt operation with an unauthenticated request and verify it is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller and establish authentication for secure shipment tracking operations.

scenario.draft: Test that a customer (buyer) can search and paginate through tracking instances for packages belonging to their orders. Workflow: (1) Register a new customer and obtain authentication; (2) (Dependency - out of scope here) create an order and shipment that results in a package for the customer; (3) As the authenticated customer, perform a PATCH search on tracking for a shipment code and package label previously assigned via an order; (4) Provide tracking event filters such as status, date window, and source; (5) Verify that the API only returns tracking information for packages that belong to the orders of this specific customer—customer must not be able to retrieve tracking for shipments/packages belonging to other customers; (6) Edge case: attempt to retrieve tracking instances from an unrelated shipment and assert access is denied.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new customer and obtain authentication for access to personal shipment tracking instances.

scenario.draft: Test that when a guest user provides a non-existent guestCartId (random/invalid), the API returns an empty list and does not throw an error or expose any sensitive internal implementation details. This scenario ensures that the system handles requests for missing/expired guest carts gracefully, in accordance with privacy and rate-limiting practices. Check for proper HTTP response and empty item array.

Test retrieval of a guest cart item with a valid guestCartId but an invalid or non-existent itemId (random/expired/removed). The expected behavior is that the system returns null or an appropriate error/message indicating the item does not exist, and does not expose sensitive or unrelated data. This validates robust handling of lookup failures and enforces business privacy and integrity.

dependencies.purpose: Create the guest cart and at least one valid item, but use an out-of-range or invalid itemId for retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully retrieve payment attempt details for a specific order using orderCode and paymentReference. The scenario validates that payment attempt status, amount, and references are correctly returned for valid orders and attempts. It also covers failure cases such as requesting payment attempts for a non-existent order or invalid payment reference, ensuring appropriate error responses are triggered. Only an authenticated admin should be able to access this resource, validating correct permission enforcement.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as an admin to enable authorized access to payment attempt retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test that a customer who placed the order can retrieve detailed information for a specific shipment package using a valid shipment code and package label. Steps: 1) Register a new customer account. 2) As the customer, proceed through the full purchase and shipment flow (including order and package creation; dependencies omitted for brevity). 3) Retrieve details for a package using correct shipment code and package label. Validate that all expected fields (tracking number, label, dimensions, status, timestamps) are correctly returned and the customer receives only their shipment/package details. Ensure that sensitive data (such as tracking numbers) is accessible and accurate for the rightful customer.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as customer actor to represent the recipient of the shipment and establish user context for access control validation.

scenario.draft: Test successful seller login workflow. This scenario verifies that a registered seller can log in using valid email and password credentials. The workflow ensures that upon successful credential validation, the seller receives both JWT access and refresh tokens. The dependencies include prior seller registration, assuring the login occurs for an existing active seller account. Expected outcome: login returns authorized seller profile and tokens.

dependencies.purpose: Register a new seller to set up an account for login testing

scenario.draft: Test the seller token refresh operation using a valid refresh token. This scenario covers the process where a seller, already authenticated and owning a valid (non-expired) refresh token, requests new JWT access and refresh tokens via the refresh endpoint. The workflow confirms that valid tokens are correctly rotated and session metadata is updated. Prerequisites include registering and logging in a seller account to procure the refresh token. Expected result: New tokens are issued and session state updated.

dependencies.purpose: Create a seller account to acquire authentication context
Log in as the newly registered seller to obtain a refresh token for token rotation testing

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can successfully delete an attachment linked to their own refund request, and verify that the attachment and underlying file reference are fully removed from the refund as expected. Validate audit logging and business rules, ensuring only the attachment owner (seller or admin) can perform the deletion. Confirm proper business error if attempted on non-existent, non-linked, or not-owned attachment. Confirm error is returned if the seller tries to delete from a closed or admin-locked refund request. Business workflow: seller creates an account, creates a product, adds a SKU, places an order, initiates a refund request, attaches evidence, then deletes that attachment as seller.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a new seller for the scenario user context.

Seller creates SKU required for the test order and refund.
A customer places an order for the seller's SKU for refund eligibility.
Seller initiates a refund request, creating the parent needed for attachment.
Seller attaches evidence to the refund request for deletion testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that a seller cannot delete an attachment from a refund request that has been administratively locked or closed by an admin. Workflow: seller creates an account, product, and SKU, completes an order and refund request, attaches evidence, admin closes or locks the refund request; seller attempts to delete an attachment, and receives a proper business error (forbidden or conflict), ensuring correct enforcement of business workflow rules.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a new seller for scenario user context.
Seller creates product for test entity setup.
Seller creates a SKU for use in order and refund context.
A customer places an order for the SKU, enabling a refund request.
Seller initiates the refund request establishing the parent for attachment.
Seller attaches an evidence file for permission error testing on closed refund.

scenario.draft: Test that a customer can retrieve the full chronological status change history for a refund request they created. Validates that only authorized actors (the refund requester) receive all authorized details, and business ordering/metadata for each transition is correct.

Seller creates SKU to be purchased in the order.

Customer initiates refund request for status history testing.

scenario.draft: Verify that only the refund request's owner (customer) can access the full status change history of a refund. Scenario: customer creates an account, places an order, creates a refund request, advances it through status transitions, and successfully retrieves the status history. Confirm that retrieval attempts by unauthorized actors, such as another customer or a non-involved seller, are denied with proper business error messages, ensuring access control and privacy.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a customer for user context.
Seller creates a product for SKU creation.
Seller creates a SKU for the order and refund flow.
Customer places order for seller SKU to be eligible for refund.
Customer initiates a refund request whose status history is tested for access control.

scenario.draft: Test that the refund status history is returned in strict chronological order and that each status transition entry contains the correct actor, timestamp, status code, and any context or notes required by business policy. Populate at least three business-relevant states (e.g., submitted, under_review, approved/declined) and check for data integrity for each. Scenario demonstrates creation of refund request, status advancement, and in-depth validation of history response fields.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as new customer for scenario context.
Seller creates a product for SKU creation.
Seller creates SKU for customer order and refund scenario.
Customer places an order for the SKU to trigger refund eligibility.
Customer creates a refund request to seed status transitions.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can successfully update the business registration and compliance information for a seller. The scenario should include joining as an admin and then updating the seller's business info, ensuring that required KYC data such as legal name, registration number, support contact, and bank details are accepted and properly updated in accordance with platform validation rules. Validate that audit logs and full replacement of business info are completed and that all changes are reflected in the seller's record.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain authorization for updating seller business info.

Create a seller and an address to initialize required sellerId. This is necessary because there is no direct seller creation endpoint and the existence of sellerId is prerequisite for updating business info.

scenario.draft: Test that a seller can retrieve a paginated and filtered list of all their registered business, return, warehouse, and pickup addresses. The scenario should include joining as a seller, registering a new address, and then requesting the address list, confirming that only addresses belonging to the authenticated seller are returned. Verify correct handling of pagination, filtering, and access restriction for unauthorized users.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as seller to enable access to retrieving own address records.
Register a new address for the seller to ensure at least one address exists in the system before retrieval.

scenario.draft: Test that an admin can retrieve the full details of a specific approval action tied to an existing refund request. Validate that the returned object includes all business-required details such as actor, action status, rationale, and audit timestamps. Confirm that only legitimate, structured approval or rejection actions are returned and that the chain of business decisions is visible to the admin. Expectation: Approvals fetched match those on the refund, are accurate, and match all compliance/audit requirements.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin prior to any admin privilege operations (approval retrieval, override, etc).
Authenticate as seller: seller is required for product/catalog/resource creation.
Authenticate as customer for order/refund simulation.

scenario.draft: Verify that an authenticated admin can successfully retrieve detailed information about a specific feature flag using its unique flagName. Authentication as admin must precede this operation to guarantee access rights. The test also validates that only non-soft-deleted flags can be retrieved.

Create a new feature flag as admin to ensure a known flag exists for retrieval

Successful creation should result in the new flag being queryable via feature flag retrieval and changes being audit logged.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to gain permission for feature flag creation

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated seller can successfully retrieve a paginated and filtered list of their product SKU inventory entries. Verifies that the response includes only SKUs belonging to the authenticated seller, respects pagination parameters, and supports sorting and filtering fields. Checks that unauthorized requests (missing token or invalid token) are denied access.

scenario.draft: Test that an authenticated admin can retrieve the detailed real-time inventory state for a single SKU by its unique code. The test should verify proper error handling for non-existent SKU codes, and confirm that unauthorized or unauthenticated requests are denied access.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as admin to obtain authorization for the inventory detail API
